title: Destroy the window when its renderer fails to load. Otherwise the card never appears again in that session.
body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Destroy the window when its renderer fails to load. Otherwise the card never appears again in that session.** `load` calls `void browserWindow.loadURL(...)` and `void browserWindow.loadFile(...)`. A rejected load is not handled. Two things then go wrong: - The rejection is unhandled in the main process. - `RecordingReadyWindow.show()` has already returned `true`, so the recording page never shows its in-app fallback. `rendererReady` stays `false`, so `present()` never shows anything. The window is not destroyed, so `ensureWindow()` returns early on every later `show()`. The user then loses the "Your video is ready" card until restart. Catch the rejection and destroy the window. The existing `closed` handler then clears `this.window`, and the next `show()` creates a fresh window.
Proposed fix
```diff --- "a/apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-ready-window.ts" +++ "b/apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-ready-window.ts" @@ -255,18 +255,24 @@ return new RecordingReadyWindow({ ...app, createWindow: (options) => new BrowserWindow(options), load: (window) => { const browserWindow = window as BrowserWindow; + const onFailure = (error: unknown): void => { + console.error("[recording-ready] the card window failed to load", error); + if (!browserWindow.isDestroyed()) browserWindow.destroy(); + }; if (is.dev && process.env["ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL"]) { - void browserWindow.loadURL( - `${process.env["ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL"]}/?window=recording-ready`, - ); + browserWindow + .loadURL(`${process.env["ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL"]}/?window=recording-ready`) + .catch(onFailure); } else { - void browserWindow.loadFile(join(__dirname, "../renderer/index.html"), { - search: "?window=recording-ready", - }); + browserWindow + .loadFile(join(__dirname, "../renderer/index.html"), { + search: "?window=recording-ready", + }) + .catch(onFailure); } }, ipc: ipcMain, screen: { getAllDisplays: () => screen.getAllDisplays(), ```
The PR description notes this gap. The one-time failure still would not trigger the in-app fallback. The fix keeps later recordings working.
Committable suggestion
> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion load: (window) => { const browserWindow = window as BrowserWindow; const onFailure = (error: unknown): void => { console.error("[recording-ready] the card window failed to load", error); if (!browserWindow.isDestroyed()) browserWindow.destroy(); }; if (is.dev && process.env["ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL"]) { browserWindow .loadURL(`${process.env["ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL"]}/?window=recording-ready`) .catch(onFailure); } else { browserWindow .loadFile(join(__dirname, "../renderer/index.html"), { search: "?window=recording-ready", }) .catch(onFailure); } ```

This lets the existing `closed` handler clear `this.window`, allowing a later `show()` to create a fresh window. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. title: The reused shade window never recovers from a renderer crash or failed load.
body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **The reused shade window never recovers from a renderer crash or failed load.** `ensureWindow` returns the existing window whenever `isDestroyed()` is false. The shade window is now long-lived, but it has no `render-process-gone`, `did-fail-load` or `unresponsive` handler. If the renderer dies, `ready` stays true and `present` sends to a dead page. Each later countdown shows an empty, screen-covering window. The window never gets replaced. The capture overlay handles these events. Do the same here. Destroy the window on these events so the existing `closed` handler resets state and the next `show` creates a new one.
Proposed fix (inside `ensureWindow`, after the `closed` handler)
```diff + const discard = (): void => { + if (!window.isDestroyed()) window.destroy(); + }; + window.webContents.on("render-process-gone", discard); + window.webContents.on("did-fail-load", (_event, code, _desc, _url, isMainFrame) => { + if (code !== -3 && isMainFrame !== false) discard(); + }); ```

title: Filter ineligible revisions before applying the retry limit.
body:

title: Seeded gap segments get a random `crypto.randomUUID()` id, so seeding the same take twice gives two different scenes.
body:
Seeded gap segments get a random `crypto.randomUUID()` id, so seeding the same take twice gives two different scenes. `wholeFingerprint` (Share) and `editFingerprint` (an untouched editor scene that was never saved) both hash `scene.webcam` with these ids. For any take with gaps, the fingerprint is new on every mount, and "already exported → reuse" never finds the earlier export. That contradicts the PR note that the fingerprint covers seeded segments automatically.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Seeded webcam gap segments make export fingerprints unstable

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/webcam/webcam-model.ts:155 — `id: crypto.randomUUID()` in `gapSegments`
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/library/components/share-recording.tsx:127-130 — `initialScene(...)` in a `useMemo`, then `wholeFingerprint(scene.webcam)`; a new hash on every mount for a take with gaps
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/export/export-reuse.ts:63-85 — `stableStringify` includes segment `id`s

## Required outcome
- Seeding the same `WebcamTrackMeta` (same gaps, same duration) twice gives an identical `WebcamScene`, so `wholeFingerprint` / `editFingerprint` are stable across mounts.
- Add a test next to the existing `export-reuse.test.ts` "same webcam → same fingerprint" case, using a meta that has `gaps`.

## Suggested approach
- Derive the id from the gap, e.g. `` `gap-${segments.length}` `` or `` `gap-${gap.startMs}` ``. `validateWebcamSegment` accepts any string id, so a session round-trip still works.
````

</details>

title: This closes the gap too early when the camera goes on, off and on again while the first re-open is still pending.
body:
This closes the gap too early when the camera goes on, off and on again while the first re-open is still pending. The off is not queued: it calls `turnWebcamOff()` straight away, which supersedes the request. The superseded `turnWebcamOn` then resolves `"ok"`, and by that time `webcamOn` is `true` again from the second on. So the gap closes when the cancelled camera finished opening, not when the second camera's first frame arrives. During that warm-up the editor shows the frozen frame from the start of the gap, and if the second re-open fails it shows it until the file ends.

The comment above the `queue` line ("an off that follows waits for this camera to open") also does not match the code, since off never goes through the queue.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Gap closed by a superseded re-open

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:938-944 — `if (webcamOn) gaps.close(...)` after a superseded `turnWebcamOn` that returned "ok"
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:787-793,810 — a superseded request returns "ok", which cannot be told apart from a real feed

## Sequence
off (gap opens) → on (turnWebcamOn#1 pending) → off (turnWebcamOff supersedes #1, gap stays open) → on (#2 queued behind #1, webcamOn = true) → #1 resolves "ok" → gap closes now → #2 opens the camera and feeds frames later.

## Required outcome
- A gap closes only when the request that actually fed a frame resolves (or when the file ends).

## Suggested approach
- Keep a local toggle generation in `forwardLiveSettings` and close only when the resolving call is the latest on request. Alternatively, let `turnWebcamOn` return a distinct "superseded" result that the store ignores.
- Fix the queue comment so it describes what actually happens.
````

</details>

title: When a master's first copy finishes, `runningCopyOf` returns `null` as soon as the runner leaves `"exporting"`.
body:
When a master's first copy finishes, `runningCopyOf` returns `null` as soon as the runner leaves `"exporting"`. But `exports` only grows after the async `refresh()` that the `readyId` effect starts. In that window `hasCopies` is false, so "Copies from this original" unmounts, "Where is it going?" comes back (unless dismissed) and "Export a copy" disappears. Then everything flips back once the list arrives. The old `showCopies = master || …` kept the panel mounted through this gap.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Bottom section flickers between panels when the first copy completes

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library-detail/library-detail-page.tsx:189: `hasCopies` reads only `exports` and `running`
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library-detail/library-detail-page.tsx:146-148: `refresh()` runs only after `runner.ready` is set, so `exports` lags the end of `running`
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/prepare/components/master-copies-panel.tsx:35: `runningCopyOf` returns null once `status !== "exporting"`

## Required outcome
- Between the runner reporting the copy ready and the re-list landing, the page keeps showing the copies panel (with the finished copy or its last running state) instead of falling back to the destinations panel

## Suggested approach (optional)
- Treat a `runner.ready` whose source asset is this recording as "has copies" until `exports` contains it, e.g. fold it into `hasCopies`
````

title: 16 DIP is far less room than the card's shadow needs.
body:
16 DIP is far less room than the card's shadow needs. `.card` in `status-card.module.css` uses `box-shadow: 0 30px 80px -30px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8)`, which reaches about 80px below the card. Where the window ends, 16px below the card, the shadow is still around 0.25 alpha. So the floating card will end in a hard horizontal shadow line, easy to see over a light desktop or app. Inside the app the dark UI hid this; floating over other apps, it won't.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Floating card's shadow is clipped by its window

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-ready-window.ts:18 — `READY_WINDOW_PADDING = 16`, documented as leaving room so the shadow is not clipped
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/assets/main.css:87 — `padding: 16px` on `body[data-window="recording-ready"]`
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/status-cards/status-card.module.css:11 — `box-shadow: 0 30px 80px -30px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8)`, which extends about 80px below and about 50px to the sides of the card

## Required outcome
- In the floating window, the card's shadow fades out inside the window bounds, with no visible cut at the window edge.

## Suggested approach (optional)
- Option 1: in `recording-ready-card.module.css`, give the card a tighter shadow that fits in the 16px padding (scoped to `.frame`).
- Option 2: make the bottom and side padding large enough for the existing shadow, and update `readyWindowBounds` and the CSS together.
- Option 1 keeps the transparent area that sits over other apps small.
````

</details>

title: With `useFileDrop` gone, no route other than Export calls `preventDefault` on `dragover`/`drop`.
body:
With `useFileDrop` gone, no route other than Export calls `preventDefault` on `dragover`/`drop`. A video dropped on the Library now makes Electron navigate the window to `file://…/clip.mp4` and replaces the app. `use-file-drop.ts` documents exactly this, and `main/index.ts` has no `will-navigate` guard. The Library used to absorb this. The new test at `library-page.test.tsx:80-87` only checks that nothing was imported, so jsdom can't catch it.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>


````markdown
# Unhandled file drops navigate the Electron window

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library/library-page.tsx:53: the Library no longer mounts any window drop handler.
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library/library-page.test.tsx:80-87: asserts `importVideoFiles` was not called, but not that the drop was `defaultPrevented`.
- apps/kaipu-record/src/main/index.ts: no `will-navigate` handler on `mainWindow.webContents`.

## Required outcome
- Dropping a file on the Library (or any non-Export route) leaves the app where it is, with no navigation to the file.
- A test asserts the drop is `defaultPrevented` on the Library.

## Suggested approach
- Add an app-wide guard that `preventDefault`s file `dragover`/`drop` at the shell level, or block file navigation in main with `webContents.on("will-navigate", …)`. Then the Library (and Record/Editor) are safe without importing anything.
````

</details>

title: This can close the gap too early if the camera is toggled off → on → off → on quickly.
body:
This can close the gap too early if the camera is toggled off → on → off → on quickly. The first `turnWebcamOn` (A) is superseded by the second off, and the engine returns `"ok"` for a superseded call. But `webcamOn` is already `true` again from the second on (B, still queued), so `gaps.close()` runs when A resolves. B's camera hasn't sent a frame yet at that point. The held frame then shows in the editor and export for B's whole warm-up, which can be up to about 6 s. If B fails to reopen, it shows until the file ends.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>


````markdown
# Superseded reopen closes the camera-off gap before frames are back

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:939-944 — the `queue` callback treats any `"ok"` as "frames are back" whenever `webcamOn` is true, even when a later off/on pair superseded this request
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:790-792, 810 — a superseded `turnWebcamOn` returns `"ok"`, the same result as a real reopen

## Sequence
off(t1) → on(t2, A queued) → off(t3: `turnWebcamOff` bumps `cameraRequest`; `gaps.open` is a no-op because the t1 gap is still open) → on(t4: `webcamOn = true`, B queued after A) → A resolves `"ok"` (superseded) → `webcamOn` is true → `gaps.close(tA)`. B then opens the camera, and its own `gaps.close` is a no-op.

## Required outcome
- A gap closes only when the request that actually fed the relay delivers its first frame (or when the file ends), never when a superseded request resolves.

## Suggested approach
Keep a toggle generation in `forwardLiveSettings` that is bumped on every camera off and on. Capture it when the on is queued, and call `gaps.close()` only if it is unchanged after `await handle.turnWebcamOn()`. Another option: have the engine return a distinct result for a superseded call. A store test for off/on/off/on with A resolving before B would pin the fix down.
````

</details>

title: With `useFileDrop` removed, nothing on the Library calls `preventDefault` on `dragover` / `drop` any more.
body:
With `useFileDrop` removed, nothing on the Library calls `preventDefault` on `dragover` / `drop` any more. `use-file-drop.ts` says what happens then: "a file dropped where nothing handles it makes Electron navigate the window to that file". `main/index.ts` has no `will-navigate` guard. A user who drops a video on the Library, as NIW2-579 taught them to, will probably see the app replaced by a bare video player. The new test cannot catch this because jsdom never navigates.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Unhandled file drops on the Library navigate the Electron window

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library/library-page.tsx:53 — the `useFileDrop` call that absorbed drops was removed
- apps/kaipu-record/src/main/index.ts:400 — `setWindowOpenHandler` is set, but there is no `will-navigate` handler for the main window
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library/library-page.test.tsx:80 — only checks that `importVideoFiles` is not called

## Required outcome
- Dropping a file anywhere in the app outside Export must not navigate the window away from the renderer.

## Suggested approach (optional)
- Add a window-wide guard: either `mainWindow.webContents.on("will-navigate", e => e.preventDefault())` for non-app URLs in main, or a shell-level `dragover`/`drop` `preventDefault` that Export's `useFileDrop` overrides. Another option is to have the Library catch the drop and route to `/export` with the files, so the old gesture still works.
- This also protects Record, Editor and Settings, which were already exposed before this PR.
````

title: `releaseAll`'s doc comment is now attached to `releaseWebcam`
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠📝 **Fix · docs: `releaseAll`'s doc comment is now attached to `releaseWebcam`**

title: The "late frame is dropped (and closed)" path is never tested
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The "late frame is dropped (and closed)" path is never tested**

The comment says a frame the old camera still delivers after `cut()` is "dropped (and closed), not relayed". But `cut()` (`webcam-relay.ts:66-70`) cancels the reader first, so `first.push(late)` either throws (and the `catch` swallows it) or enqueues into a stream that was already cancelled. Either way, the pump never reads `late`, so the `current !== reader` branch that calls `value.close()` (`webcam-relay.ts:91-93`) never runs. The test also never asserts `late.close`. In a real camera that branch handles a frame that was already queued when the cut happened, and an unclosed `VideoFrame` there leaks GPU memory. One way to cover it: enqueue `late` *before* calling `relay.cut()` without flushing, then assert `expect(late.close).toHaveBeenCalled()` and that `written` does not contain `"a2"`.

title: Progressbar nested inside the pill's button is hidden from assistive tech
body:

The pill is a `<button aria-label={t("expand")}>` (line 199–203) that wraps a `<span role="progressbar" aria-valuenow=…>`. Buttons have presentational children in ARIA, and the button's `aria-label` overrides its content, so screen readers announce only "Show the export's progress". They never hear the percent or the progressbar role. If the minimized state should still report progress, move the progressbar out of the button so it is a sibling, or add the percent to the button's accessible name (for example, by including the `pill` text in the label).

body:

`close()` only hides the window, so its React tree keeps showing the last payload. On the next `show()`, `rendererReady` is still true, and `present()` sends the new payload and calls `showInactive()` straight away (lines 223–225). You could avoid this by clearing the card when it is hidden: for example, send a null payload on close, or have the card ack the paint before main shows the window.

body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Comment says a later "off" waits on the queue, but the off branch runs right away**

The comment says the turn-on is queued "so an off that follows waits for this camera to open and releases it". The off branch (lines 924–934) never touches `queue`. title: If the camera can't be reopened, the face may be recorded nowhere, not "back in the capture"
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: If the camera can't be reopened, the face may be recorded nowhere, not "back in the capture"**

The PR's premise (camera-bubble-window.ts:40-44, recording-hub.ts:301-303 and 310-314) is that a running capture leaves out a window that was protected when the capture started, so only a new window gets recorded. On a failed reopen, main has already called `cameraBubble.show()` on the parked window, which was protected at capture start. The `recordingWebcamEnded` handler (recording-hub.ts:456-460) then only unprotects that same window; it does not replace it the way line 304 does. By the PR's own reasoning, the face is then left out of the screen recording too. This comment and the `webcamReopenFailed` docs (line 797, "the face went to the screen") say otherwise, and the user is told the face went to the screen. This is the same best-effort path as an unplugged camera. Could the hub replace a protected window that is still showing when the webcam file ends mid-take, the way line 304 does for a parked one? If not, the comments should say the face may be lost.

body:

The renderer has not repainted yet, so the hidden window's last frame (the old recording's duration and size) can appear briefly before the new card replaces it. One option: have the card clear its state when it is dismissed. Another: show the window only after the card has painted, for example on the first `resize` after a payload.

title: A failed reopen leaves the face out of both the webcam file and the screen capture
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A failed reopen leaves the face out of both the webcam file and the screen capture (confidence medium)**

When the camera is turned back on while the webcam file is still live, `takeRecordsWebcam()` is true, so line 305 shows the same parked window. That window is protected, and by the PR's own premise (lines 310-313, `camera-bubble-window.ts:40-44`) the running capture leaves it out. Only after that does the renderer try to reopen the camera (`turnWebcamOn`, recorder-engine.ts:779-819). If the reopen fails (busy, denied, or no frame within `WEBCAM_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS`), it calls `endWebcam`, and main's `recordingWebcamEnded` handler (line 456-460) only runs `bubbleProtection.webcamEnded` and `applyProtection()` on that same excluded window. Main never destroys it or creates a new window, so for the rest of the take the face is in no file. The comment at recorder-store.ts:946-947 says "main put the bubble back in the capture", but nothing does that. The user only hears about it after saving (`webcamUnavailable`). Suggested fix: in the `recordingWebcamEnded` handler, while a take is active and the camera is on, replace the window (destroy + show) the same way line 304 does for a parked one.

title: A press on the floating card during the next take shows the main window mid-recording
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A press on the floating card during the next take shows the main window mid-recording (confidence high)**

The floating card has no timer and is not closed when a take starts. Its content protection exists so that "a card still up never lands in the next recording" (`recording-ready-window.ts:206-208`), so the card is meant to stay up through a following take. If the user clicks a chip, Edit first or Open during that take, `openInMain` calls `showMainWindow()` with no check.

Every other path that reveals the main window refuses while a take is active. The deep-link focus does `if (!hub?.isActive()) showMainWindow()` (`main/index.ts:185`). `triggerStartRecording` says "Don't un-hide the (deliberately hidden) main window into an active recording — it would get burned into the video" (`main/index.ts:475-477`). The hub hides the main window at start on purpose (`recording-hub.ts:689`).

With this change, the main window shows up in the video, and its renderer is navigated to Prepare or the editor in the middle of the take. That renderer is the one running the recorder (`main/index.ts:460-462`).

Fix: guard `openInMain` with `hub?.isActive() || hub?.isPending()` (ignore the press, or show the already-recording notice), or close the ready card when a take starts.

If the card's renderer fails to load, `recording-ready:card-ready` never arrives, `present()` never shows the window, and the user gets no "Your video is ready" for that take, with no visible error. title: Back onto the recording page pops the floating card up on the desktop again
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Back onto the recording page pops the floating card up on the desktop again (confidence medium)**

`useFloatingReadyCard` remembers what it already asked for in a ref (`use-floating-ready-card.ts:18`), and that ref is lost when the page unmounts. The request is keyed by `location.key` and gated on `location.state.fromRecording` (lines 101, 130-134). Both survive a router Back, because the remounted page sits on the same history entry. So this sequence reopens the window: a chip on the floating card sends the main window to `/prepare/...` (a push, `use-recording-ready-hand-offs.ts:31`), or the user closes the card with ✕ and later leaves the page. When they press Back, the page asks `showRecordingReady` again and the always-on-top window reappears over whatever app is in front.

The old in-app card had the same remount reset (`cardDismissedFor` is plain state). But that card only came back inside the app's own page. Now it is a desktop window on every Space, and it reappears for a card the user already acted on. That goes against the hook's and the doc's "once per arrival" claim.

Possible fix: remember the history keys already asked for in module scope or in `sessionStorage`, or have the hand-off and dismiss paths clear `fromRecording` with `navigate(..., { replace: true, state: {} })`.

body:

This change removes `useFileDrop` from the Library. That hook was the Library's only `dragover`/`drop` handler, and its own docstring says why the window needs one: "a file dropped where nothing handles it makes Electron navigate the window to that file" (`features/library/hooks/use-file-drop.ts:8-11`). The main process does not stop it either. `src/main/index.ts` sets `setWindowOpenHandler` (line 400) but has no `will-navigate` guard, and no other window-level `drop`/`dragover` listener exists in `src/` (the only ones are in `use-file-drop.ts:48-51`).

The PR says that after this change "dropping a file there does nothing". In practice, dragging an MP4 from Finder onto the Library replaces the renderer with the file. The app UI disappears, and so does any renderer-side state, including an export the background runner (`export-runner.ts`) is encoding in that renderer. No error explains what happened.

The Library is where a user who used to import by dropping will try it first. The simplest fix is to keep a window-wide drop guard mounted here: call `useFileDrop` with a handler that sends the files to Export or shows a toast pointing there. A broader option is an app-wide guard, such as `will-navigate` with `preventDefault` in main or a root-level dragover/drop `preventDefault`, which would also cover the other screens that never had one.

This test pins the new Library behaviour: nothing handles a file dropped on the window. It only checks that `importVideoFiles` is not called, and it ignores what `fireEvent.drop` returns (line 85). Library used to mount `useFileDrop` through its import drop zone, so window-level `dragover`/`drop` were `preventDefault`ed. Now the only caller of `useFileDrop` is `usePrepareImport` (`features/prepare/use-prepare-import.ts:55`), which only Export mounts. So a video dropped on Library, which until this PR was the place to drop videos, can replace the app UI with a file:// player and leave no way back. I didn't confirm Chromium's default navigation in Electron here; I'm relying on the hook's comment for that.

Suggested fix: keep a window-level handler that only calls `preventDefault` while Library (or the whole shell) is mounted. Alternatively, add a `will-navigate` guard in main. Either way, assert in this test that the drop was prevented (`expect(fireEvent.drop(...)).toBe(false)`), as `dropFiles` does in export-page.test.tsx:416.

title: Camera off → on → off can leave the camera open while the toggle says off
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Camera off → on → off can leave the camera open while the toggle says off (confidence high)**

Turning the camera off calls `handle.turnWebcamOff()` synchronously (line 928). Turning it on again does not: it queues `handle.turnWebcamOn()` on the shared `queue` (line 939). Mic toggles (line 902) and noise-suppression reopens (line 868) also run on that queue. If the queue is busy, say while a mic is opening, an off that comes in after the on reaches the engine before the queued `turnWebcamOn` starts. In the engine, `turnWebcamOff` then finds `cameraWanted` already false. It bumps `cameraRequest` and returns true (recorder-engine.ts:769-778).

When the queued `turnWebcamOn` finally runs, it sees `cameraWanted === false`. It sets `cameraWanted` to true, takes a fresh `request` and opens the camera (recorder-engine.ts:781-787). Nothing bumps the counter after that, so the supersession check at line 790 passes. The camera's frames go into the webcam file and the in-use light comes on, while the toggle shows off and main has parked the bubble. The store sees "ok" with `webcamOn === false` and leaves the gap open, so the editor hides those frames. Nothing visible tells the user the camera is recording.

The comment at line 938 says an off that follows "waits for this camera to open and releases it", but the off path is not on the queue. Fix: inside the queued callback, return early when `!webcamOn` before calling `turnWebcamOn`. Another option is to put the off path on the queue too.

title: The "late frame is dropped and closed" case is never exercised
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The "late frame is dropped and closed" case is never exercised (confidence high)**

`relay.cut()` cancels the old camera's reader (`webcam-relay.ts:66-70`), and that closes the fake stream. So `first.push(late)` throws inside the `try` and the frame never reaches the pump. The relay's own drop branch (`if (current !== reader) { value.close(); break; }`, `webcam-relay.ts:91-94`) never runs, and nothing checks `late.close`. The test passes because the stream was cancelled, not because the relay drops a frame that was already in flight. To cover the branch, use a fake processor whose `cancel` does not close the stream, or one that has already queued a frame when `cut()` runs, and then assert `expect(late.close).toHaveBeenCalled()`.

title: Show in Finder and the drag on the Library's ready card leave the copy marked unseen
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Show in Finder and the drag on the Library's ready card leave the copy marked unseen (confidence high)**

The toast's version of these actions calls `markCopySeen(recording.assetId)` before both `revealLocalRecording` and `startFileDrag` (`export-status-cards.tsx:280` and `:293`). The ready-copies store defines that contract: a copy is unseen "until the user opens it ... or acts on its ready card (Show in Finder, drag it out)" (`ready-copies.ts:10-11`).

The new Library card skips that call on Show in Finder (line 80) and on drag start (line 93). Here is what happens: the user drags the YouTube copy from the Library's "Ready to upload" card into YouTube Studio, then leaves the Library. `retireReadyCards` removes the card, but the copy is still in `unseenCopyIds`. When the user comes back, the regular card is still outlined and the "1 copy ready" chip still counts it, even though the user already uploaded it. Only opening the copy's page clears it.

Fix: call `markCopySeen(video.assetId)` in both handlers, as the toast does. That also removes the card right away, which matches the toast's behaviour.

title: A card left open shows up as a black box in the next recording on Windows before 10 2004
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A card left open shows up as a black box in the next recording on Windows before 10 2004 (confidence medium)**

The card has no timer and nothing closes it when the next capture starts. Content protection is the only thing keeping it out of later recordings and screenshots (lines 206-208). On Windows builds before 10 2004 (19041) there is no `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`. On those builds, content protection paints the window black in the capture instead of leaving it out. `area-geometry.ts:81-92` says this, and the hub skips the full-display border there for that reason (`recording-hub.ts:701-703`).

The capture toast doesn't rely on content protection alone. Its comment calls content protection the "second guard behind `beforeCapture` dismissing it" (`capture-toast-window.ts:305-307`), and `index.ts:670` wires `dismissToast` into the capture hooks.

The result: a user who leaves the card up and starts another full-display recording or screenshot gets a black rectangle in the top-right of the video, with no error. Fix: close the card when a take starts and in the screenshot capture hooks, as the toast does. Or skip the floating window when `fullDisplayBorderAllowed` is false.

body:

title: A file dropped on the Library now navigates the whole window to that file
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A file dropped on the Library now navigates the whole window to that file (confidence high)**

The Library no longer calls `useFileDrop`, and nothing else on that screen cancels `dragover`/`drop`. The hook says why it listens on the window: "a file dropped where nothing handles it makes Electron navigate the window to that file" (`features/library/hooks/use-file-drop.ts:9-11`). The main process has no `will-navigate` guard either: only `setWindowOpenHandler`, which covers new windows and not same-window navigation (`src/main/index.ts:400-403`). Today the only other caller is `usePrepareImport` (`features/prepare/use-prepare-import.ts:55`), which is mounted only on Export.

So if a user drags an MP4 from Finder onto the Library, as they could before this change, the renderer is replaced by Chromium's file viewer. The app UI disappears, and there is no error and no way back. The PR body says "dropping a file there does nothing", but that is not what happens.

Fix: keep a window-level `dragover`/`drop` `preventDefault` that is mounted for the whole app, in the shell or `main.tsx`, and that ignores the files. Or add `webContents.on("will-navigate", e => e.preventDefault())` for `file:` URLs in main. Either fix also covers the other screens that have never handled drops.

title: Library no longer intercepts file drops, and the new test pins that: a video dropped on Library navigates the Electron window to the file
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Library no longer intercepts file drops, and the new test pins that: a video dropped on Library navigates the Electron window to the file (confidence medium)**

Only one place in the app still takes a file drop at the window level: `useFileDrop`, which is mounted only through `usePrepareImport` (`use-prepare-import.ts:55`), which now only `ExportPage` calls (`export-page.tsx:85`). Before this PR, Library mounted the drop hook. The removed test "imports a video dropped anywhere on the window" covered that. Now a user who drops a video on Library out of habit loses the whole renderer to a `file://` page. The background export also runs in the renderer, so a copy being exported at that moment is lost with no warning.

The new test only checks that `importVideoFiles` was not called. It does it synchronously, and the import would be async anyway (`importDropped` from `useImportVideos`), so the assertion would pass even if a handler were present. It never checks whether the drop was default-prevented. Compare `export-page.test.tsx:416`, which does check this through `fireEvent.drop`'s return value.

Suggested fix: Library (or the app shell) should still call `preventDefault` on file `dragover`/`drop`, either by redirecting to Export or by ignoring the drop. The test should then assert `fireEvent.drop(...)` returns `false`.

This doc (and step 12 of the PR body) says the Library "no longer takes window drops", which suggests a drop there does nothing. title: A camera-off that lands before a queued turnWebcamOn runs leaves the camera recording while the toggle says off
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A camera-off that lands before a queued turnWebcamOn runs leaves the camera recording while the toggle says off (confidence high)**

Turning the camera on puts `handle.turnWebcamOn()` on `queue` (line 939). Turning it off calls `handle.turnWebcamOff()` synchronously (line 928), not on the queue. The comment says "an off that follows waits for this camera to open", but the off does not wait. Here is how it goes wrong when the queued on has not started yet. This happens when an earlier item still holds `queue`: a mic toggle awaiting `acquireMicrophone`, a noise-suppression reopen, or an earlier `turnWebcamOn` still opening during quick off/on/off clicks.

1. Off: `turnWebcamOff` sets `cameraWanted = false` and `cameraRequest++` (recorder-engine.ts:771-772), then returns true.
2. The queued on runs later. `cameraWanted` is false, so it does not return at line 781. It takes a new request number (line 783), opens the camera and feeds the relay (lines 784-808). No later toggle bumps `cameraRequest`, so it returns "ok".
3. Back in the store, `webcamOn` is false, so the gap stays open (line 943).

Result: the user turned the camera off and main parked the bubble (hidden), but the recorder holds the camera open again. The in-use light is on, and the face is written into `<name>.webcam.mp4` until the next on or the end of the take. The editor hides it only because the gap stays open, so the file still contains footage the user turned off.

Fix: in the queued callback, skip the call when the toggle has moved on, e.g. `if (!webcamOn) return;` before `await handle.turnWebcamOn()`. Alternatively, queue the off as well.

title: A superseded turnWebcamOn closes the gap before the newer camera delivers a frame
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A superseded turnWebcamOn closes the gap before the newer camera delivers a frame (confidence medium)**

When an on is superseded (off, then on again while it opens), the engine returns "ok" for the stale request (recorder-engine.ts:792 and :810). By then the newer on has set `webcamOn = true`, so `gaps.close(takeTimeMs())` runs at line 943 even though the camera from the next queued `turnWebcamOn` has not reached the file yet. The held frame then shows in the editor while that camera opens, for up to `WEBCAM_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS`. This goes against the stated rule that a gap closes on the first new frame. One option is to have the engine tell "superseded" apart from "fed", or to tag each queued on with a request number in the store and close the gap only for the latest one.

title: A quick off → on → off → on closes the gap before the second camera's first frame, so the editor shows a frozen face
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A quick off → on → off → on closes the gap before the second camera's first frame, so the editor shows a frozen face (confidence medium)**

The store test covers off → on → off while the camera reopens. It does not cover the case where a second `on` arrives while the first reopen is still pending, and the code gets that case wrong.

Sequence (recorder-store.ts:924-953 with recorder-engine.ts:769-819):
1. off: the gap opens.
2. on₁: queued. The engine starts `openWebcamWithin`.
3. off₂: the engine bumps `cameraRequest` and returns true. `gaps.open` does nothing because a gap is already open.
4. on₂: the store sets `webcamOn = true` and queues a second `turnWebcamOn` after on₁.
5. on₁'s open finishes. `request !== cameraRequest`, so the engine stops that stream and returns "ok" (recorder-engine.ts:790-792). Back in the store, `webcamOn` is now true, so `gaps.close(takeTimeMs())` runs (recorder-store.ts:943).
6. Only after that does on₂ open its camera and feed its first frame. That can take up to `WEBCAM_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS`.

The gap therefore ends while the relay is still cut and the file is still holding the last frame. The editor seeds a hidden segment only up to that point, so the preview and the export show a frozen face until on₂'s frames arrive. If on₂ fails, the frozen face shows until the file ends. Nothing warns the user.

Suggested fix: close the gap only when the `on` that resolved is the latest one the store issued. For example, keep a counter for `on` requests and skip `gaps.close` when a newer `on` is queued. Add a test here: off, on (pending), off, on, then resolve the first `on`. The gap should stay open until the second one resolves.

title: `show()` answers true before the card has painted, so a renderer that never loads loses the card silently
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: `show()` answers true before the card has painted, so a renderer that never loads loses the card silently (confidence high)**

`show()` returns true as soon as the BrowserWindow exists (l.137–146). `present()` only paints after `recording-ready:card-ready` (l.108–112, 221). If `loadFile`/`loadURL` rejects (its promise is discarded with `void`, l.261/265), or the card's renderer crashes before it sends `ready()`, the page has already been told `true`. `useFloatingReadyCard` therefore never sets `inApp` (use-floating-ready-card.ts:26-28), and the user gets no card anywhere, with no visible error. The same happens when an existing window's renderer has gone away: `rendererReady` stays true, and `showInactive` shows an empty transparent window. The PR body acknowledges this. A cheap way to close the gap: resolve the invoke only once the card reports ready, or after a short timeout that resolves false, so the in-app fallback covers load failures too.

title: Back to the recording's page floats the card again after the user already acted on it
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Back to the recording's page floats the card again after the user already acted on it (confidence medium)**

The `asked` ref only lives as long as the component instance. Say the user picks a chip on the floating card: main hides it and navigates to Prepare. If they then press Back, `LibraryDetailPage` remounts under the same history entry, with the same `location.key` and, presumably, the same `fromRecording` state (library-detail-page.tsx:130-134). The ref is null again, so the hook calls `showRecordingReady` a second time and the card pops up on the desktop over whatever the user is doing. The in-app card also came back on Back (`cardDismissedFor` is component state), but that happened inside the page. Now it is an always-on-top window outside the app, after the user already answered the question. The doc on l.4 ("a revisit is a new one") implies the key alone dedupes. To make that true, keep the asked keys in module scope (or in `history.state`) instead of a ref that dies on unmount.

title: Doc says the card goes away when the user leaves the page; the floating one does not

"stays until the user picks something, closes it or leaves the page" is still true of the in-app fallback. It is not true of the floating window: `RecordingReadyWindow` only hides on an action, ✕ or Escape (recording-ready-window.ts:150-172), so it outlives navigation, and it also outlives deletion of the recording, after which its chips and Open lead to an asset that is gone. title: Card stays up over the next take; content protection does not hide it everywhere
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Card stays up over the next take; content protection does not hide it everywhere (confidence medium)**

The card has no timer and is not closed when a recording starts. It stays on top during the next take and relies on `setContentProtection(true)` to stay out of the video. The hub itself does not trust content protection on every platform: it gates the display border on `fullDisplayBorderAllowed(process.platform, release())` (recording-hub.ts:703) because old Windows cannot exclude windows from capture. On those systems a card left up lands in the next recording. Closing the card on `recordingStart`, or applying the same gate, would avoid it.

title: Router Back to the recording page floats the card again, even after it was used or dismissed
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Router Back to the recording page floats the card again, even after it was used or dismissed (confidence medium)**

The "once per arrival" guard is `asked` in `use-floating-ready-card.ts:18`, a ref keyed by `location.key`. A ref does not survive an unmount. Here is the sequence: the floating card's chip sends the main window to `/prepare/...`. The user then goes router Back (or leaves for Settings and comes back the same way). React Router reuses the same history entry, so `location.key` is the same and `state.fromRecording` is still true. `showCard` is true again, the new mount's ref is null, and `showRecordingReady` runs a second time. The card the user already handled opens again on the desktop.

The old in-app card had the same gap, because `cardDismissedFor` was component state. The difference now is that this is an always-on-top window outside the app, and the hook's doc ("`key` is its history entry, so a revisit is a new one") suggests that keying by `location.key` deduplicates arrivals. One fix: keep the asked/dismissed keys somewhere that outlives the page, such as a module-level Set or the history entry's state via `navigate(..., { replace: true, state: { ...state, fromRecording: false } })` once the request is sent. Then main's replace-on-next-show never gets a stale request.

title: Every library re-list unmounts the Export screen and throws away the picked destination
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Every library re-list unmounts the Export screen and throws away the picked destination (confidence medium)**

`ExportPage` returns the "Loading" placeholder whenever `isLoading` is true (line 117), before it gets to `<ExportScreen>`. `useLocalLibrary().refresh` sets `isLoading` back to true on every re-list (`use-local-library.ts:42`), not only the first one, and it re-lists on every `library:changed` broadcast (`use-local-library.ts:133`). Main sends that broadcast after the catalog refresh that the hook starts on mount succeeds (`use-local-library.ts:130`, `main/library/index.ts:73-76`), on account changes (`index.ts:85-87`), and when items are saved or imported (`index.ts:185`, among others).

Each time this happens, `ExportScreen` unmounts and mounts again. Its `selected`, `youtube` (1440p/4K) and `framings` (Fill/Fit) state go back to `initialDestination` from `?to=`, and the screen flashes "Loading…". In practice:
- A signed-in user picks a card in the first moments after opening Export, and the catalog refresh then resets it to "Where is it going?".
- The PR says Export stays on screen after an export starts. When the copy is saved and the library re-lists, the user's choice is wiped.

The `chosen` ref is cleared only when `assetId` changes (lines 78-80), so it keeps the old pick while the visible selection has reset. A dropped video or "Change video" then opens with a destination the screen no longer shows.

Suggested fix: show the placeholder only while the video is not available yet, e.g. `if (isLoading && !video)`. Keeping `ExportScreen` mounted across a refresh is safe because its `key` is `preparable.id` (line 152).

title: A file dropped on the Library now navigates the whole window to that file
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A file dropped on the Library now navigates the whole window to that file (confidence high)**

This PR removes the `useFileDrop` call from the Library. That hook was the only window-level `dragover`/`drop` handler on this screen. In its own doc comment, the hook explains why it covers the whole window: "a file dropped where nothing handles it makes Electron navigate the window to that file" (`features/library/hooks/use-file-drop.ts:9-11`).

Nothing else guards against this:
- The renderer adds no other `drop` or `dragover` listener (the only ones are in `use-file-drop.ts:48-51`).
- `src/main/index.ts` has no `will-navigate` handler.

So after this change, dragging an MP4 from Finder onto the Library replaces the app with the file. The user loses the app UI and any in-memory state until a reload. Before this change, the same drop imported the video.

The PR body says "dropping a file there does nothing" (test step 12). That is not what will happen.

Suggested fix: keep a window-level guard on the Library that calls `preventDefault` on `dragover` and `drop` and ignores the files. This keeps the decision that the Library no longer imports. Even simpler, call `useFileDrop(() => {})`, or route the drop to Export.

title: Screen readers don't hear the GitHub limit verdict on the size bar
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Screen readers don't hear the GitHub limit verdict on the size bar (confidence medium)**

The size card is `role="img"`, so assistive tech reads only its `aria-label`. That label is `barLabel` ("Your recording {from}, the copy {to}"). It leaves out the `tag`: "fits the 10 MB limit", "over GitHub's 10 MB free-plan limit" or "N% lighter". It also leaves out the `barPicture` line.

For GitHub, whether the copy fits the free-plan limit is the main thing this card tells the user, and a screen reader never announces it. Consider adding `tag` to the label, or dropping `role="img"` and keeping only the bar `aria-hidden`.

title: Opening /export/:assetId clears the badge, but that screen doesn't show the finished copies
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Opening /export/:assetId clears the badge, but that screen doesn't show the finished copies (confidence high)**

`onExport` matches with `end: false`, so `/export/<assetId>` also calls `announceReadyCopies()`. That URL is what a recording page's "Prepare for…" and its quick chips now open. On that route, though, `ExportPage` renders the recording's header and stage. `RecentExports`, the list that actually points at finished copies, only renders on the bare `/export` (export-page.tsx:101-112).

So here is what happens: a copy finishes out of sight, then the user opens Export for a different recording. The badge clears even though nothing on screen pointed at the copy. That contradicts the doc comment's "both point at the copies" (sidebar.tsx:107-108). The copy is still outlined in the Library, so nothing is lost; only the rail's reminder goes away.

To match the comment, announce only on an exact match of `ROUTES.exportNew` (`end: true`), as the Library check does. The comment at line 52 ("Active on /export and /export/:assetId") is about the highlight and can stay as it is.

title: Library no longer stops a dropped file from replacing the app window
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Library no longer stops a dropped file from replacing the app window (confidence medium)**

The new test makes sure Library does not import a dropped file, but it does not check what happens to the drop instead. `useFileDrop` explains why the whole window had a listener: "a file dropped where nothing handles it makes Electron navigate the window to that file" (`features/library/hooks/use-file-drop.ts:9-11`). Result: a user who drops a video on Library out of habit (it used to import) sees the app replaced by the raw file. No error appears, and they have to reload to get the app back. The Export test checks exactly this case (`!fireEvent.drop(...)`, `export-page.test.tsx:414-416`); this test should check it too.

Suggested fix: keep a window-level handler in the app shell that calls `preventDefault` on file `dragover`/`drop` events nothing else handles (or add a `will-navigate` guard in main), and assert here that `fireEvent.drop(document.body, …)` returns false.

title: Reopen failure with the camera on only drops protection on the existing window
body: When the camera is turned on again mid-take and the recorder cannot reopen it, the engine ends the webcam file (`recorder-engine.ts:794-798`). At that point the bubble is the same native window, shown and already protected, because `show()` at `recording-hub.ts:305` reuses it. The `recordingWebcamEnded` handler (`recording-hub.ts:456-460`) then only calls `applyProtection()`, which calls `setContentProtection(false)` on that window (`camera-bubble-window.ts:146-152`). The code's own comments say two things that conflict here. First, the doc comment on `applyProtection` says it is unverified whether a running ScreenCaptureKit stream picks up a window that drops protection. Second, the comment at `recording-hub.ts:301-303` says that the window to record is a new, unprotected one, and that a running capture leaves out only the windows that were on screen when it started. The parked case is handled by destroying the window and creating a new one (line 304). The more common case, where the camera is on and the reopen fails, is not. If the existing window stays excluded, the face is in neither file, and the post-take notice (`webcamReopenFailed` → `webcamUnavailable`) tells the user it went into the screen. Was the reopen-failure path with the camera on checked in the owner QA? If not, consider replacing the window in this path (destroy, then `show()`), as the parked path does.

title: reconcileWebcam seeds gap segments without the recording duration
body: `initialScene` now passes `durationSeconds` to `seedWebcamScene`, so a gap stretched to the minimum segment length is clamped inside the recording. `reconcileWebcam` here still calls `seedWebcamScene(webcam)` without it. A session saved before the webcam layer existed, opened on a recording with gaps, gets segments whose end can run past the recording when the final gap is very short. The caller has the scene's clip items, so it can derive the duration and pass it. Either do that, or note why the clamp is not needed on this path.

title: Spec still says a camera turned off leaves the bubble in the capture, and that the layer stops drawing after the last frame

body:

title: The 'cut camera's frames never get through' test passes without exercising the drop path
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The 'cut camera's frames never get through' test passes without exercising the drop path (confidence medium)**

`relay.cut()` cancels the camera's reader, which closes the underlying stream. The test's own `try/catch` around `first.push(late)` shows that the enqueue throws (the stream is already cancelled), so `late` never reaches the pump. The branch in `webcam-relay.ts:91-94`, which closes and drops a frame delivered after the cut (`current !== reader`), is never run. `late.close` is never asserted either, although the comment says the frame is 'dropped (and closed)'. A regression that relayed a late frame, or leaked it by not closing it, would still pass. To cover the branch, make the fake processor's stream ignore cancellation (a reader whose `read()` resolves with a frame after the cut), then assert `late.close` was called and `written` has no 'a2'.

body:

title: Every library re-list unmounts ExportScreen and resets the user's selection
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Every library re-list unmounts ExportScreen and resets the user's selection (confidence medium)**

`useLocalLibrary().refresh` sets `isLoading` to true on every call (`use-local-library.ts:42`). `ExportPage` returns the "Loading" placeholder whenever `isLoading` is true, even when the video is already resolved. `ExportScreen` is therefore unmounted and remounted. Its local state (`selected`, the YouTube 1440p/4K choice, the Fill/Fit framings) goes back to the initial values, and the picked card and focus are lost.

A re-list happens without the user doing anything. `useLocalLibrary` fires `refreshCloudCatalog()` on mount (`use-local-library.ts:130`), and main broadcasts `library:changed` when that succeeds (`main/library/index.ts:73-75`). Account changes, tag edits and imports broadcast too (`index.ts:85-87`, `110`, `185`). A signed-in user who picks a destination right after opening Export can see the screen flash "Loading" and the selection revert to `?to=` or to "Where is it going?".

The editor routes avoid this with `if (isLoading && !source)` (`editor-routes.tsx:79`). Show the loading placeholder only while `video` is still unresolved (`isLoading && !video`), or keep the last resolved video. I did not run the app, so I have not seen the flash; I read the code path.

title: A video file dropped on the Library window now navigates the window to the file
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A video file dropped on the Library window now navigates the window to the file (confidence medium)**

The Library used to mount `useFileDrop`. That hook's comment (`use-file-drop.ts:10-11`) says why: a file dropped where nothing handles it makes Electron navigate the window to that file. After this change `LibraryPage` mounts no drop handler. I found no replacement. There is no `will-navigate` guard in `src/main` (`main/index.ts:400` only sets a window-open handler), no global `drop`/`dragover` listener, and `useFileDrop` is now mounted only through `usePrepareImport` in `ExportPage`. The new test at `library-page.test.tsx:80` only checks that `importVideoFiles` is not called. It does not check that the drop is cancelled, so it passes while the window navigates away. Fix: keep a drop guard on the Library, for example `useFileDrop` with a handler that toasts or redirects to Export (`ROUTES.exportNew`). Alternatively, block navigation in the main process with `will-navigate`, which would cover every page. Extend the test to assert `defaultPrevented` on the drop.

title: A video dropped on the Library now falls through to Electron's default, and the test doesn't check for it
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A video dropped on the Library now falls through to Electron's default, and the test doesn't check for it (confidence medium)**

The PR removes the Library's `useFileDrop` import door (`ImportDropZone`). `usePrepareImport` is now the only non-test caller of `useFileDrop` (`features/prepare/use-prepare-import.ts:55`). `useFileDrop`'s own doc says why it listens on the window: "a file dropped where nothing handles it makes Electron navigate the window to that file" (`features/library/hooks/use-file-drop.ts:10-11`). I found no guard elsewhere. There is no `will-navigate` handler in `src/main`, no drop handling in `shell/app-root.tsx`, and nothing in the preload. So a user who drops a video on the Library, the old import door, probably gets the main window navigated to the file and has to reload the app. The Library page also has no copy telling them to go to Export.

The new test "does not take a video dropped on the window" only asserts `importVideoFiles` was not called. It passes whether or not the window navigates away. The Export tests already show the right check: `dropFiles` returns `!fireEvent.drop(...)`, i.e. whether the default was prevented.

Fix: add a window-level guard that swallows file drops everywhere outside Export, for example in `app-root.tsx`, or call `useFileDrop` with a no-op on the Library. Then assert that `fireEvent.drop` on the Library is default-prevented. The other pages that never handled drops, such as the editors, share the exposure; I did not check them.

title: An off→on→off toggle can leave the camera open while the toggle is off
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: An off→on→off toggle can leave the camera open while the toggle is off (confidence medium)**

The turn-on is queued (`queue = queue.then(...)`), but the next turn-off is not: it calls `handle.turnWebcamOff()` synchronously (line 928). The comment at line 938 says the off "waits for this camera to open and releases it". That only holds once `turnWebcamOn` is already running, because only then does its `request !== cameraRequest` check catch the off.

If the queued on is still waiting behind another item (a mic `getUserMedia`, a noise-suppression reopen), this happens:
- The second off runs `turnWebcamOff()` at `recorder-engine.ts:769`. `cameraWanted` is already false, so it bumps `cameraRequest`, cuts the relay and returns true.
- The queued `turnWebcamOn()` then runs. `if (cameraWanted) return "ok"` (line 781) does not fire, so it opens the camera and feeds the relay.
- The forwarder sees `webcamOn === false`, so it does not close the gap (line 943).

The result: the recorder holds the camera (in-use light on) while the user's toggle is off. The bubble's renderer has released it, so nothing shows this, and the gap stays open until the next toggle or the end of the take.

Fix: skip the queued turn-on if the camera was turned off again before it runs, for example `if (!webcamOn) return;` at the top of the queued callback (line 940). Alternatively, have `turnWebcamOn` check the current wanted state after it is dequeued.

title: A floating card left up during a new take un-hides the main window into the recording
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A floating card left up during a new take un-hides the main window into the recording (confidence high)**

The card has no timer and nothing closes it when a recording starts. A `recordingReady` search in `main/` finds only the create, `openInMain` and shutdown call sites, so neither `recordingStart` nor the countdown touches it. Unlike the capture toast, it is not dismissed either: the toast has a 6 s timer and `dismissToast` runs in `beforeCapture` (`capture-window-hooks.ts:56`). The PR's own test step 7 ("Record twice without closing the card") leaves the first card up during the second take.

A press on that leftover card (chip, Edit first, Open) then runs `openInMain`, which calls `showMainWindow()` (`index.ts:449-457`: restore, show, focus) and navigates the renderer. The main window is hidden on purpose while a take runs (`recording-hub.ts:689`, the `recordingStart` handler). `triggerStartRecording` explicitly refuses to un-hide it into an active recording because it "would get burned into the video" (`index.ts:475-481`). The card is content-protected, but the main window is not, so the user's app window and a navigation away from the recorder land in the video. The old in-app card lived in the hidden main window and could not be pressed mid-take, so this is a regression.

If the next take is not eligible for a card (Settings toggle off, or a non-local video), the previous take's card also stays up indefinitely, showing the wrong recording.

Fix: call `recordingReady?.close()` when a take starts or its countdown begins. Also make `openInMain` do nothing while `hub?.isActive() || hub?.isPending()`, like the other entry points.

body:

The other three channels check `isOwnSender`, but the `recordingReadyShow` handler accepts a call from any renderer. title: Only Export takes window file drops now; a video dropped on the Library navigates the window to the file
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Only Export takes window file drops now; a video dropped on the Library navigates the window to the file (confidence medium)**

`usePrepareImport` (which mounts `useFileDrop`) is now the only caller of `useFileDrop` outside tests. This PR removes it from the Library, which was the one page that took drops, and it is called here on Export only. `useFileDrop` is what calls `preventDefault` on `dragover` and `drop` (`features/library/hooks/use-file-drop.ts:29-47`), and `use-prepare-import.ts:32-34` says its purpose includes that "a drop never makes Electron navigate the window to the file".

Nothing else guards it. `src/main/index.ts` has no `will-navigate` or `will-navigate`-style handler, only `setWindowOpenHandler` (line 400), and no other renderer code listens for `drop` or `dragover`. So a video dragged onto the Library, the screen people will still drag files onto, takes Electron's default: the window loads `file://…` and the app UI is gone until a reload. The PR's step 12 claims "dropping a file there does nothing", but the code does not show that.

Fix: keep a drop guard that only prevents the default on pages other than Export. That can be a shared app-level `dragover`/`drop` `preventDefault`, or a `will-navigate` handler in main that blocks non-app URLs.

title: A video dropped on the Library now navigates the Electron window to the file
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A video dropped on the Library now navigates the Electron window to the file (confidence medium)**

The Library used to mount `useFileDrop`, which listens for `dragover` and `drop` on the window and calls `preventDefault`. That is what keeps Electron from navigating the window to a dropped file. This PR removes the hook from this page. `use-file-drop.ts:10-11` says why it exists: "a file dropped where nothing handles it makes Electron navigate the window to that file". `use-prepare-import.ts:32-34` repeats it: "a drop never makes Electron navigate the window to the file".

Nothing else guards the Library page. In `src/main` I found no `will-navigate` handler, only `setWindowOpenHandler` at `main/index.ts:400`. In the renderer, `useFileDrop` is only used by `use-prepare-import.ts`, which only Export mounts. Users who had the drop strip here will keep dropping videos on it. The window will load the raw `.mp4` and the app UI will be gone until a reload. The PR body says "dropping a file there does nothing", and `library-page.test.tsx:80` asserts only that nothing is imported. Neither covers the default action.

Fix: keep a drop guard on the Library (a `dragover`/`drop` `preventDefault` for `Files` drags, with no import), or add a `will-navigate` guard in main for the main window so a file URL cannot replace the app. The Library test should assert `event.defaultPrevented`.

title: Sections 2 and 3.2 still say a camera turned off ends the webcam file
body: The PR rewrote decision 7 so that, with a relay, turning the camera off keeps the file running and records a gap. Two later passages in the same spec still describe the old rule. Line 286 says "after its last frame (turned off) the layer is not drawn". Lines 328-329 list a webcam file ended by "turned off" among the cases that leave the bubble in the screen capture. Under the new behaviour, off in a take with a relay parks the bubble, keeps it protected, and hides the face through a `gaps` segment. Only the no-relay and countdown cases and a failed reopen still end the file and unprotect the bubble. Qualify both passages, or point them at decision 7. `testing/webcam-track-check.md:41` (not in this PR) has the same stale claim: duration-mismatch is "expected when the camera was turned off mid-take (the webcam file ends there)". That is no longer so for takes with a relay.

title: Off→on→off→on quickly closes the camera-off gap before the camera is back
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Off→on→off→on quickly closes the camera-off gap before the camera is back (confidence medium)**

The off branch (`turnWebcamOff`, line 928) runs immediately, but the on branch is queued (line 939). Sequence: on (queued, opening), off (bumps `cameraRequest` in the engine, `webcamOn=false`), on again (`webcamOn=true`, queued behind the first). The first `turnWebcamOn` finishes with `request !== cameraRequest` and returns "ok" without a camera feeding the relay (recorder-engine.ts:810). Because `webcamOn` is true again, line 943 calls `gaps.close(takeTimeMs())`. The gap ends while the second open has not started, so the editor shows the held last frame as live for up to the open time. Close the gap only when the engine confirms its camera is feeding, e.g. have `turnWebcamOn` distinguish "superseded" from "fed". The comment on line 938 is also wrong: the off is not on the queue (line 928 calls the engine directly). It is the engine's `cameraRequest` counter that makes a late camera release itself.

body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: `show()` answers true even if the card page never loads, so the in-app fallback is skipped (confidence medium)**

`show()` returns true as soon as the `BrowserWindow` object exists. body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Dropping a video on the Library now navigates the Electron window to the file (confidence medium)**

`useFileDrop` is the only code in the renderer that calls `preventDefault` on `dragover`/`drop`. The Library is newly exposed, and it is the screen users drag files onto by habit. Fix by keeping a drop guard on the Library, or on the whole shell, that calls `preventDefault` and ideally points to Export. A `will-navigate` handler in main would also work. The backlog doc says the Library "no longer takes window drops" but does not mention this.

title: Reused shade has no recovery from a crashed or failed renderer, so one failure lasts the whole session
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Reused shade has no recovery from a crashed or failed renderer, so one failure lasts the whole session (confidence medium)**

Before this change, every take created its own shade window, so a renderer that crashed or failed to load affected only that take. Now `ensureWindow` returns the existing window whenever `!isDestroyed()` (line 135). It listens only for `ready-to-show` and `closed` (lines 181-193), not for `render-process-gone`, `did-fail-load` or `unresponsive`.

This causes two problems:
- If the prewarmed page fails to load (or the renderer dies before it paints), `ready` stays false forever. Every later `show` sets `wanted` and returns at line 88, waiting for a `ready-to-show` that never comes. The hub's `onShown` (`markCountdownShown`, recording-hub.ts:546-551) never runs, so `recordingCountdownVisible` (recording-hub.ts:558-561) stays pending on every region countdown for the rest of the session.
- If the renderer crashes after it painted, `ready` stays true. `present` sends state to a dead page, shows an empty window and calls `onShown` at once. Every later countdown and REC border is invisible, with nothing telling the user why.

The overlay windows guard against exactly this case (capture-overlay-windows.ts:657-670). Suggested fix: on `render-process-gone` and on main-frame `did-fail-load` (ignoring ERR_ABORTED), destroy the window so the `closed` handler resets it and the next `show` loads a fresh one. The new test "loads a new window when its page is gone (crash, closed)" only calls `destroy()`, so it does not cover a crash.

title: Does setBounds size the shade correctly when it moves between displays with different scale factors?
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡❓ **Consider · question: Does setBounds size the shade correctly when it moves between displays with different scale factors? (confidence low)**

Before, the shade was created at the target display's bounds every take. Now one window is created at the primary display's bounds (line 58) and moved with a single `setBounds(display.bounds)`. On Windows, Electron has a known problem: one `setBounds` that moves a window across monitors with different DPI can give the wrong size. If that happens here, the dim and the REC border would sit in the wrong place around the area. Has this been tried on mixed-DPI setups? The PR body lists it as a risk to check by hand. If it does misbehave, calling `setBounds` twice (move, then resize) is the usual workaround.

`hideAppForTake` waits `delay(WINDOW_HIDE_SETTLE_MS)` in the main window's renderer right after main has called `mainWindow.hide()` (recording-hub.ts:599-604). The bar, shade, overlay and camera windows all set `backgroundThrottling: false`, but the main window does not set it anywhere in `src/main`. If Chromium throttles timers in this hidden renderer, the 50 ms timer can fire much later, and the clock starts late. Starting on time at the end of the countdown is the whole point of this change. Have you checked that the hidden main window's timers aren't throttled here (for example, because an active capture or AudioContext exempts the page)? Your own `clock started at countdown end +Nms` mark would show it.

title: The cache also turns the recovery re-assertions into no-ops, so the 'app vanishes from Dock/⌘-Tab after a recording' fix can come back
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: The cache also turns the recovery re-assertions into no-ops, so the 'app vanishes from Dock/⌘-Tab after a recording' fix can come back (confidence medium)**

`appliedPolicy` only records what this process last *asked for*. It cannot see the state macOS actually has. The callers of `applyDockPolicy()` were written to repair a state that drifted outside our control:
- `recording-hub.ts:281-284`: "Hiding the main window for the recording can drop the app from the Dock / Cmd+Tab on macOS; re-assert the policy".
- `roadmap.md:185-187`: this re-assertion on stop is recorded as the fix for "the app vanishing from the Dock & ⌘-Tab after a recording".
- `index.ts:233-237`: the `⌘⌃O` rescue shortcut calls `applyDockPolicy()` to bring a lost app back.

`showInDock` defaults to `true` (`shared/types/ipc.ts:214`). For those users, `registerSettings()` sets `appliedPolicy = "regular"` at startup. After that, `forceRegularPolicy()` at recording start (`recording-hub.ts:267`), `applyDockPolicy()` on stop (`recording-hub.ts:284`) and the rescue shortcut (`index.ts:236`) all return at line 82 without touching AppKit. If macOS drops the app after the main window is hidden, the code that used to repair it no longer runs. The user is left with an app missing from the Dock and ⌘-Tab, with no error. The rescue shortcut no longer restores the Dock icon either. It still shows the window and focuses it.

Only the camera-on call at `recording-hub.ts:157` caused the reported bug. A fix that keeps the guard there but still repairs on the restore paths: let `applyDockPolicy` take a `{ force: true }` that `applyStopWindowState` and `bringAppToFront` pass. Another option is to decide "unchanged" from `app.dock?.isVisible()` instead of a module variable. Either way, check on device that a recording with Show in Dock on still leaves the app in ⌘-Tab after stop.

title: Window check is check-then-act: a concurrent intent resume can extend the ticket between the check and `release`
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🔐 **Fix · security: Window check is check-then-act: a concurrent intent resume can extend the ticket between the check and `release` (confidence high)**

`cancelUpload` reads `ticketExpiresAt` with `findRevision` and checks the window here, then calls `assets.release` (line 39). `release` only guards `status = 'reserved'` (`packages/infra-db/src/repositories/cloud-asset.repository.ts:350`), and so does `extendTicket` (`cloud-asset.repository.ts:268-273`). A client whose reservation is past the window but has not been swept yet (the cron is not wired, per the spec's open question 2) can send cancel and a resume of the same `intentKey` (`create-upload-intent.ts:152-162`) together. If the resume's `extendTicket` lands after cancel's `findRevision` and before its `release`, the reservation is released, the object is deleted, and the client holds a freshly signed 5-minute ticket that no revision counts. That is the F-1 hole this PR is closing, now opened by a race the client controls. `sweepExpiredReservations` already has the same race (it lists, then calls `release` without re-checking expiry), so the fix belongs in the repository: give `release` a cutoff (`... and ticket_expires_at < ${cutoff}`) and pass `now - grace` from both cancel and the sweep, so the check and the claim happen in one statement.

title: Skipped in-window rows still use up the `limit` batch
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Skipped in-window rows still use up the `limit` batch (confidence medium)**

`listDeleting(limit)` (`cloud-asset.repository.ts:534-541`) returns the oldest `deleting` rows by `updated_at` and knows nothing about the window. The skip happens here, after the batch is fetched. If `limit` or more deferred deletes are still inside their window, a run finishes nothing, even when older-window rows behind them could be settled. The delay is bounded by the window (about 3 h 05 min), but one account can cause it for every account by confirming and then deleting many assets. Filtering in the query (`ticket_expires_at < now - grace`) would make every row in the batch actionable, the way `listReservedExpiredBefore` already does for the sweep.

body:

title: Does mediabunny's overflow error actually match /maximum packet count/i?
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠❓ **Fix · question: Does mediabunny's overflow error actually match /maximum packet count/i? (confidence low)**

Every export now uses `fastStart: "reserve"`, including Original, the only preset the editor reaches today. That makes the FR9 fallback (lines 210-222) the only thing between a variable-rate burst that overflows `maximumPacketCount` and a failed export. Before this change the same export succeeded with `fastStart: false`. The fallback runs only when the worker's error text matches `/maximum packet count/i`. I could not check that string against the installed mediabunny version (there is no node_modules in the checkout), and the hook test mocks the message. If mediabunny words it differently (for example "packet count exceeded"), an overflow falls through to `fail(GENERIC_ERROR)` and an export that used to work now fails. Did you check the regex against mediabunny's actual throw site, and could a test pin it to the library's message?

title: Capped branch can assume < 30 fps, contrary to the docblock
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Capped branch can assume < 30 fps, contrary to the docblock (confidence high)**

The docblock says "The video rate never assumes less than 30 fps — a variable-rate screen recording can burst above its average". When `maxFps` is set (Small file below 1080p), the code uses `Math.min(opts.maxFps, Math.max(1, opts.fps))`. A mostly static recording averaging, say, 8 fps therefore reserves for 8 fps, even though bursts up to the 30 fps cap get through. The worker only raises the count using `computePacketStats(240)`, i.e. the first 240 packets (export-worker.ts:203-206). An edit that keeps the high-motion parts can overflow the reserve, which costs a full second encode through the fallback. `Math.min(opts.maxFps, Math.max(30, Math.ceil(opts.fps)))`, or simply `opts.maxFps`, matches the comment.

title: Label being re-edited is still drawn under the editor, so the old and new text overlap
body: The SVG still renders every visible overlay, including the one in `editingText.id` (lines 382-397). The textarea sits at the same x/y with a nearly transparent background (`rgba(0,0,0,0.04)`, video-annotation-layer.module.css:37). title: Reopened multi-line label shows only its first line until the user types
body: The textarea starts with `rows={1}` and `overflow: hidden`, and its height only changes in `onInput` (lines 424-429). When a multi-line label is reopened, the prefilled `defaultValue` fires no input event, so the editor is one line tall and the other lines are clipped. title: Re-edit box uses the current tool's color and size, not the label's

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Re-edit box uses the current tool's color and size, not the label's (confidence high)**

When a label is reopened by double-click, the textarea is still styled from `toolState.color` and `TEXT_PX[toolState.textSize]` (lines 415-417). Say a label is size 2 and red, and the toolbar is on size 0 and blue. While editing, the text shows small and blue. The screenshot editor, which this code mirrors, stores the label's own color and size when it reopens it (annotation-layer.tsx:142-150) and uses them (`editing.color ?? tools.color`, `TEXT_PX[editing.size ?? tools.textSize]`, annotation-layer.tsx:374-376).
