title: Reused shade window never recovers from a renderer crash
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Reused shade window never recovers from a renderer crash (confidence medium)**

The shade window is now created once and kept for the whole session. `ensureWindow` only builds a new one when the window is `null` or destroyed (line 135), and it only listens for `closed` (lines 187-193). A renderer crash leaves the BrowserWindow open: it is not destroyed and `ready` stays true. After that, every later `show` takes the reuse path (lines 78-91). `send` goes to a dead webContents, `showInactive` puts up an empty transparent window, and `onShown` fires right away. The hub then marks the countdown as shown (`recording-hub.ts:546-551`), so the recorder starts counting with no visible 3-2-1 and no REC border, for every take until the app restarts. Nothing tells the user.

Before this change each take loaded a fresh window, so a crash affected only one take. The sibling overlay windows handle this case: `capture-overlay-windows.ts:657-660` reacts to `render-process-gone`, and to `did-fail-load` and `unresponsive`.

Fix: on `render-process-gone`, destroy the window (or set `this.window = null; this.ready = false`) so the next `show` loads a new one.

title: System-audio write-back now happens during the countdown and survives a cancel

The live-settings forwarder is now attached as soon as the countdown's acquisition resolves (line 490). title: Policy cache ignores the Dock-hide that the floating panels trigger, so re-asserting can no longer restore the app
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🔴🐛 **Blocker · bug: Policy cache ignores the Dock-hide that the floating panels trigger, so re-asserting can no longer restore the app (confidence medium)**

`appliedPolicy` only records what this module set. Something else changes the policy behind its back. `CameraBubbleWindow.show()` creates a new window on every camera-on (destroy-on-off, `recording-hub.ts:162`). It then calls `setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true, { visibleOnFullScreen: true })` without `skipTransformProcessType` (`camera-bubble-window.ts:47`), and `ControlBarWindow` makes the same call (`control-bar-window.ts:62`). Electron documents that, on macOS, this call switches the process to a UIElement (accessory) app, which is a Dock hide. The repo's own comments describe the same effect: "Showing a floating panel can drop the app from the Dock/Cmd+Tab on macOS; re-assert the policy" (`recording-hub.ts:155-157`, `281-284`). That re-assertion is the only repair, and this change turns it into a no-op because the cache still says `regular`.

With `showInDock = true` (the default), the result is:
- **Camera on:** the bubble is created and the app leaves the Dock and Cmd+Tab. `applyDockPolicy()` returns early at line 82, so the app stays out of them.
- **Recording:** `forceRegularPolicy()` (`recording-hub.ts:267`) runs before the bar is created asynchronously, so the bar's transform drops the app during the take. On stop, `applyDockPolicy()` (`recording-hub.ts:284`) is a no-op, so the app is still missing after the recording.
- **Rescue shortcut:** `bringAppToFront()` (`index.ts:234-237`) also relies on `applyDockPolicy()` and can't restore it either. Only flipping the `showInDock` setting off and on again recovers.

The new tests mock both window classes (`recording-hub.test.ts:39-54`), so they can't see this. Possible fixes:
- Pass `skipTransformProcessType: true` in both windows, after checking it still floats over full-screen Spaces.
- Reset `appliedPolicy = null` after creating a panel window.

I couldn't read Electron's native source from here, so the transform itself rests on Electron's documented behaviour and on this repo's comments.

`listDeleting(limit)` returns the oldest `deleting` rows by `updated_at` (`packages/infra-db/src/repositories/cloud-asset.repository.ts:534-541`). title: The spec says the sweep boundary and the predicate agree "and vice versa", then says they don't
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The spec says the sweep boundary and the predicate agree "and vice versa", then says they don't (confidence high)**

title: Capped packet count trusts the average rate, so variable-rate sources under-reserve the moov box
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Capped packet count trusts the average rate, so variable-rate sources under-reserve the moov box (confidence medium)**

The docstring at lines 209-213 says the video rate "never assumes less than 30 fps — a variable-rate screen recording can burst above its average". The `maxFps !== null` branch does the opposite: `Math.min(opts.maxFps, Math.max(1, opts.fps))`. It reserves for the source's *average* rate, which can be far below 30 for a mostly static screen recording. In the worker (`export-worker.ts:203-211`), that average comes from only the first 240 packets (`computePacketStats(240)`). The renderer passes 30 when `sourceInfo` is omitted, but the worker raises the count with `Math.max`, never lowers it.

Example: a Small-file export below 1080p (maxFps 30) from a source that averages about 10 fps but has long active stretches near 30 fps can emit up to 30 frames/s after the cap. That outruns `d × 10 × 1.33` packets, the muxer throws, and `use-video-export.ts:210-221` silently re-runs the whole export with `fastStart: false`. The user waits twice as long and gets a file without fast start, which is the main point of this PR, with no visible signal.

Suggested fix: when capped, reserve for the cap itself. Use `opts.maxFps` (or `Math.min(opts.maxFps, Math.max(30, Math.ceil(opts.fps)))`) so the bound matches the frames the fps-cap loop at `export-worker.ts:293-294` can actually emit.

A label reopened with `initialText = "first\nsecond"` therefore opens one row tall, and every line after the first is clipped and invisible until the user types something. The user edits text they can't see, and an immediate Enter or blur commits it as is.

The screenshot sibling handles this in its focus effect at `screenshots/annotations/annotation-layer.tsx:117-122`. title: A crashed shade renderer is reused for every later take and paints nothing
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A crashed shade renderer is reused for every later take and paints nothing (confidence medium)**

The shade window now lives for the whole session. `ensureWindow` only replaces it on `closed` (lines 187-193), and nothing listens for `webContents` `render-process-gone`. When the shade renderer crashes, the BrowserWindow stays open and `ready` stays true. Every later `show` sends state to a dead page, calls `showInactive` on an empty transparent window and fires `onShown`, so the hub marks the countdown as shown (recording-hub.ts:546-551). From then until the app restarts, the user gets no dim, no 3-2-1 number and no REC border, and nothing says why. Before this change each take loaded a new window, so a crash lasted for one take only. The overlay windows in this same PR guard against this case (capture-overlay-windows.ts:655-660). Suggested fix: on `render-process-gone`, destroy the window (or set `this.window = null` and `ready = false`) so the next `show` or `prewarm` loads a new one.

title: Can a reused shade briefly show the previous take's frame?
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡❓ **Consider · question: Can a reused shade briefly show the previous take's frame? (confidence low)**

`hide()` hides the window first and only then sends `idle` (line 114, then line 115). While the window is hidden, Chromium may not produce a composited frame for that state. `present()` sends the new state and calls `showInactive()` straight away (lines 126-127), without waiting for the renderer to receive or paint it. So when the window comes back, can the OS show the last frame it composited, which is the previous take's REC border or dim, for a frame or two? The PR claims "a reused window never repaints the previous take" and lists the Retina ↔ non-Retina move as a manual check. Has this ordering been checked on macOS and Windows? An ack from the renderer after it paints, or `webContents.invalidate()` before the show, would close the gap.

title: Is 50 ms enough to keep the app window out of the first encoded frame?
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡❓ **Consider · question: Is 50 ms enough to keep the app window out of the first encoded frame? (confidence low)**

Before this change, `recordingStart` hid the main window and only then did the screen capture open. That took about a second, so the app's window was long gone before the first frame. Now, on the Record page, the capture opens during the countdown while the window is still on screen. `hideAppForTake` hides the window and then waits only `WINDOW_HIDE_SETTLE_MS` (50 ms) before `prepared.begin()` starts the output (recorder-store.ts:380-389, 525-535). The comment's estimate is one 30 fps frame plus one display refresh. That leaves no margin for the OS capture pipeline's latency (ScreenCaptureKit / DXGI delivery) or for the compositor canvas still holding the last frame it drew. If that latency goes over 50 ms on some machines, the app shows up in the first frame of the video and no error says so. Has the 50 ms been checked on real macOS and Windows captures? A safer option would be to wait for the first capture frame that arrives after the hide, for example via `requestVideoFrameCallback`, instead of a fixed delay.

title: Memoizing on the last applied policy turns the rescue re-assertions into no-ops
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Memoizing on the last applied policy turns the rescue re-assertions into no-ops (confidence medium)**

Every caller other than the settings update calls `applyDockPolicy()` to repair a state that macOS changed on its own, not one this module changed. The doc comment right below (lines 88–92) says hide/show cycles and floating panels "can otherwise drop the app from the switcher". `applyStopWindowState` (`recording-hub.ts:281-284`) repeats that reason, and so does the ⌘⌃O rescue shortcut `bringAppToFront` (`index.ts:233-237`, "Bring the app back to the foreground from any state"). `appliedPolicy` only records what this process last asked for, so it cannot see that kind of drop.

With `showInDock: true` (the default, see `settings-store.test.ts:68`), startup sets `appliedPolicy = "regular"`. After that:
- `forceRegularPolicy()` at recording start returns early.
- `applyDockPolicy()` at recording stop returns early.
- `applyDockPolicy()` in the rescue shortcut returns early.

None of them reaches `setActivationPolicy`/`dock.show()` for the rest of the session. If the drop those comments describe happens, the stop path and the rescue shortcut no longer bring the app back into the Dock/Cmd+Tab, and nothing tells the user.

The bug only needed the camera-on path (`recording-hub.ts:157`) to stop re-asserting. Possible fixes:
- Keep the early return for that path only, e.g. drop the call there or make it memoized.
- Give `bringAppToFront` and `applyStopWindowState` a forced variant that ignores `appliedPolicy`. Those paths show and focus the window anyway, so a `dock.show()` cycle there is harmless.

If the drop-from-switcher behaviour turned out not to be real, update the comments at lines 88–92 and in `recording-hub.ts` and `index.ts` to say so. Then the memo is the whole story.

title: Deferred deletes are common, not rare: the window is the ticket TTL plus 3 h of grace
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Deferred deletes are common, not rare: the window is the ticket TTL plus 3 h of grace (confidence high)**

The spec says a ready revision "only has an open window if it was confirmed within 5 minutes of its last ticket, so this branch is rare in practice". The predicate is `ticketExpiresAt + RESERVATION_GRACE_SECONDS <= now` (`packages/application/src/cloud/ticket-window.ts:10`), where the TTL is 5 min and the grace is 3 h (`packages/domain/src/constants/cloud-limits.ts:25,30`). It depends on when the delete happens, not on when the confirm happened. Any asset deleted within about 3 h 05 min of its last ticket is deferred, and that includes the usual "upload, then remove it" case. While a delete is deferred the revision stays `deleting` and keeps counting as used (`cloud-asset.repository.ts:367`). So a user who deletes a fresh upload to free space does not get the quota back for up to 3 h. Until NIW2-328 schedules `retryPendingDeletes`, they never get it back. The "Strongest argument against" section (lines 202-206) and open question 1 name this cost only for cancels. Please correct the rarity claim and add the delete-side quota hold to the accepted trade-offs.

Line 157 says the predicate and the sweep share the same boundary, "so a revision the sweep would release is one the predicate calls closed, and vice versa". The sweep lists `ticketExpiresAt < now - grace`, a strict comparison (`sweep-expired-reservations.ts:22-23`, `cloud-asset.repository.ts:526`). The predicate uses `<=` (`ticket-window.ts:10`). title: In-window rows are filtered after `limit`, so they can fill every batch
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡⚡ **Consider · perf: In-window rows are filtered after `limit`, so they can fill every batch (confidence medium)**

`listDeleting(limit)` returns the oldest `deleting` rows by `updated_at` (`cloud-asset.repository.ts:534-541`). The new check skips in-window rows only after that `limit` has been applied. Skipped rows keep their `updated_at`, so the next run lists them again. If `limit` or more in-window rows sit at the head of that order, each run skips all of them and does no work. Revisions whose storage delete really failed, possibly from other accounts, then wait up to about 3 h 05 min and keep counting as used. One account can cause this by uploading and deleting many tiny assets. Filtering in the query (a `ticket_expires_at < now - grace` condition on `listDeleting`, matching how `listReservedExpiredBefore` filters) would keep each batch to rows that can actually be finished.

title: Capped-fps packet count trusts the source's average rate, which the docstring says never to do
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Capped-fps packet count trusts the source's average rate, which the docstring says never to do (confidence high)**

The docstring at lines 209-213 says the video rate "never assumes less than 30 fps — a variable-rate screen recording can burst above its average". The `maxFps !== null` branch does the opposite: it uses `Math.min(opts.maxFps, Math.max(1, opts.fps))`. A screen recording that is mostly static can average 5–10 fps, so the reservation is sized for 10 fps. But the fps cap in the worker (`export-worker.ts:293-294`) only limits the output to 30 fps, and bursts of motion can reach that rate.

Once `start()` gets real `sourceInfo`, this undercounts in both places. In the renderer, `use-video-export.ts:125` passes `sourceInfo.fps`. In the worker, `export-worker.ts:206` uses `averagePacketRate`. The `Math.max` at `export-worker.ts:212` doesn't help, because both inputs come from the same low average. When the reservation runs out, mediabunny throws mid-export and the hook redoes the whole encode without fast start. The user waits through two exports and still gets a file without fast start.

The Small-file byte budget subtracts `reserveBytes(packetCounts)` (line 366), so it is undercounted the same way.

Fix: when a cap is set, use the cap itself as the rate (`fps = opts.maxFps`). That is the true upper bound on frames per second and matches the docstring.

title: Hit-test still uses single-line `text.length` geometry, so the second line of a label is not clickable
body: The PR says a multi-line label's lower half used to be unselectable and that `textBoxPx` fixes this. But the change only resizes the drawn outline (`overlay-shapes.tsx:144-145`). title: Stale poster is never refreshed on edit/overwrite unless save path rewrites it
body:
**Note (correctness): Stale poster is never refreshed on edit/overwrite unless save path rewrites it**

The freshness check in `ensureScreenshotPoster` (and its "regenerates when PNG is newer" test) is only reached from the protocol's 404 fallback. If a poster file exists but is stale, the `thumb` route serves it as is. Manual step 4 (Edit + Save, card shows updated image) therefore depends entirely on the edit/overwrite path going through `screenshotSave` and calling `writeScreenshotPoster`. The plan only wires that call after `vault.writeImage` in `screenshotSave`. Please confirm every code path that rewrites a PNG (editor overwrite, any other `writeImage` caller) goes through it. Otherwise the stale poster is served until the `?v=` token changes, and even then the old file is returned.

title: Capped paste still creates tags it cannot assign
body:
**Note (correctness): Capped paste still creates tags it cannot assign**

addMany calls onCreate for every valid piece before assignMany applies the per-item cap. With one slot left and a paste of `x, y, z, `, all three tags are created in the registry and only one is assigned, which leaves orphan tags. The 'caps a paste' test checks only the length of the onAssign argument, so it would not catch this. Stop resolving pieces once idsRef.current.length plus resolved.length reaches TAGS_PER_ITEM_MAX.

title: Bar-hidden test may pass without the fix
body:
**Note (correctness): Bar-hidden test may pass without the fix**

The test releases the `getSources` promise and then awaits a single `Promise.resolve()` before asserting `bar.show` was not called. `displayIdForSource(...).then(...)` needs more than one microtask to run, so the assertion can run before the callback and pass even if the `barGeneration` guard is missing. Flush with `await vi.runAllTimersAsync()` (or several ticks), as the next test does, so the test fails without the guard.

title: Timeout path force-resets a renderer that may still be alive
body:
**Note (correctness): Timeout path force-resets a renderer that may still be alive**

On the close/quit timeout the hub calls `forceReset()`, which under this plan aborts every writer session (and, under plan 22, releases them). The renderer may only be slow, not dead, and a slow finalize can then fail because its session is gone. The plan lists the slow `copyFile` case as a follow-up. The same race also applies to a finalize that is still running when the timeout fires, and that is worth stating in Global Constraints.

title: Heartbeat does not actually bound gaps to 1 s
body:
**Note (correctness): Heartbeat does not actually bound gaps to 1 s**

The heartbeat is a 1 s setInterval that only draws if `now - lastDrawAt >= 1000`. If a source frame drew at t=500 ms, the tick at t=1000 sees only 500 ms elapsed and skips, so the next draw can be up to ~2 s after the last one on a mostly static screen. That contradicts the stated 1 s bound for R1 (VFR gaps). Use a shorter tick (e.g. 250 ms) with the same >=1000 check, or reset the interval on each draw, so the plan's guarantee holds.

title: useTimeSelector passes a new subscribe function every render
body:
**Note (correctness): useTimeSelector passes a new subscribe function every render**

The planned `useSyncExternalStore((onChange) => subscribeTime(() => onChange()), ...)` creates a new subscribe closure on each render. React then unsubscribes and resubscribes on every render of the host component. This is correct but wasteful. Wrap the subscribe function in `useCallback` keyed on `subscribeTime`, or pass `subscribeTime` through a stable wrapper, before the plan is implemented.

title: Prompt points at docs/adr/, which does not exist here
body:
**Note (adr): Prompt points at docs/adr/, which does not exist here**

The prompt tells Claude that "the ADRs in docs/adr/ hold its decisions", but this repository keeps them in `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/architecture/decisions/`. `docs/adr/` is a path from the kit's original repository. Claude will find nothing there, so it can't check changes against accepted decisions, and the "contradicts an accepted decision" rule in RULES won't work. Make the ADR directory configurable, or point the prompt at the real path. `.github/claude-review.md` could name it.

title: Unpinned installer piped to bash in a job that holds the API key
body:
**Note (security): Unpinned installer piped to bash in a job that holds the API key**

`curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash -s "$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION"` pins the Claude Code version but not the installer script. The installer is fetched live and run in the same job that later receives `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. The same step appears in `on-demand` at line 158. Consider verifying a checksum of the installer or the binary, or installing from a pinned npm package. The workflow also uses floating action tags (`actions/checkout@v4`, `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`). If that matches the other workflows here, ignore this.

title: The `review` job runs the PR head's own script with the API key
body:
**Note (security): The `review` job runs the PR head's own script with the API key**

In `review`, the checkout is the PR head and the script runs from that checkout. A same-repo PR that edits `scripts/claude-review.ts`, `.claude/` or `bunfig.toml` can exfiltrate `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or alter the budget. The header and ADR 0028 accept this under the owner-only trust assumption. The `on-demand` job already runs the default branch's script, so `review` could do the same by checking out the default branch's `scripts/` the way `on-demand` does. That would remove the inconsistency cheaply. The ADR's "What would reopen this" already covers a second collaborator joining.

title: `cancel-in-progress` on on-demand lets any later @claude comment kill a running review
body:
**Note (correctness): `cancel-in-progress` on on-demand lets any later @claude comment kill a running review**

The group is per PR with `cancel-in-progress: true`. If the owner comments `@claude review`, then a quick `@claude why …` question before it finishes, the review is cancelled after Claude has already spent budget. Nothing is posted and the next run starts over. Because the cancelled run never posts a marker, nothing is corrupted, but the spend is wasted. Consider `cancel-in-progress: false` so runs queue.

title: Import now always writes an empty registry, even if the vault is unavailable
body:
**Note (correctness): Import now always writes an empty registry, even if the vault is unavailable**

Before, importLegacy only wrote when tags were found. Now it always calls write(tags). If tags.json is ENOENT because the vault folder is missing or unmounted (for example an unplugged external drive), vault().list() returns nothing and the empty registry is persisted. Check whether write()'s mkdir then creates a local .kaipu directory at the vault path. If it does, the empty tags.json would shadow or precede the real registry once the drive is back, and the import would be marked done for good. Consider skipping the persist when the vault directory itself does not exist. Also, the crash window between write() and the sidecar rewrites drops those items' legacy tags permanently. The comment accepts that, but it is not covered by a test.

title: Recovered title is a hard-coded English string
body:
**Note (other): Recovered title is a hard-coded English string**

"Recovered recording" is persisted in the sidecar and shown in the Library. The rest of the change localizes its user-facing strings (en/es). Consider an i18n key, or a title that is a stable sentinel the UI translates at render time.

title: Sweep of os.tmpdir() relies on an mtime heuristic
body:
**Note (other): Sweep of os.tmpdir() relies on an mtime heuristic**

The sweep adopts every `kaipu-rec-*.mp4.part` in the shared system temp dir older than 2 minutes. A long-paused recording by another running instance, or a writer that does not touch the file for more than 2 minutes, would be moved out from under it. Check whether single-instance locking makes this impossible. Otherwise, prefer a stronger signal than mtime.

title: No feature doc or backlog entry
body:
**Note (other): No feature doc or backlog entry**

CLAUDE.md requires every new feature to have a doc under `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/` (a `backlog/` page plus a row in `backlog/index.mdx`). This PR adds stranded-recording recovery and a save-elsewhere flow but no doc.

title: Header comment still says the owner is matched by association
body:
**Note (other): Header comment still says the owner is matched by association**

The `on-demand` condition now matches the login `csdev19`. The file's header comment still describes the gate in terms of "the repository owner" and "only the owner's `@claude` comment starts a run". That is still accurate, but the login is hardcoded. If the owner account is renamed or ownership moves, the job will silently skip every comment. The new inline comment explains why the login is used, so this is a minor maintainability point and not a bug. GitHub logins are unique and cannot be spoofed in the event payload, so the trust boundary is not weakened. It is in fact narrower than `MEMBER`.

title: isVisible() probe may lag right after dock.show(), risking repeated show
body:
**Note (correctness): isVisible() probe may lag right after dock.show(), risking repeated show**

The ADR itself notes `app.dock.isVisible()` can lag after `DockShow`. If a re-assertion (e.g. recording stop followed closely by `applyDockPolicy()`/`⌘⌃O`) lands in that window, the probe reports not-regular and the setter calls `app.dock.show()` again on an active app. That is the window-churn this cache was introduced to prevent. The ADR calls this theoretical because `setActivationPolicy` runs synchronously first. It is untested against real AppKit, so keep it on the owner QA list (rapid start/stop and camera toggles).

title: ADR 0029 status differs between the index and the ADR page
body:
**Note (adr): ADR 0029 status differs between the index and the ADR page**

The index lists 0029 as "Proposed — implemented, owner QA pending". The ADR page's status row says "Implemented on `fix/dock-lost-after-floating-panels`; owner QA outstanding". It also names a branch, which will go stale after merge. Use one status vocabulary in both places and drop the branch name.

title: Stale temp cleanup no longer matches new temp names
body:
**Note (correctness): Stale temp cleanup no longer matches new temp names**

`remove()` still deletes `<cursorTrack>.tmp`, but writes now use `<target>.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp`. A crash mid-write leaves a uniquely named temp file that nothing removes, so these accumulate in `.kaipu`. The `.tmp` rm is now dead code. Consider a startup sweep or removing the dead line.

title: chmod-based failure test fails when run as root
body:
**Note (other): chmod-based failure test fails when run as root**

`chmod(dir, 0o500)` doesn't block writes for root (e.g. some Docker CI). The test would then see the write succeed and fail. Also skip when `process.getuid?.() === 0`.

title: API key goes to a reusable workflow on a floating tag
body:
**Note (security): API key goes to a reusable workflow on a floating tag**

`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is passed to `niway-dev/agent-review/.github/workflows/review.yml@v1`. `v1` is a movable tag, so any change pushed to it runs with this repository's key and a `pull-requests: write` token. The deleted workflow checked the Claude binary against a SHA-256 for this reason. The header comment says the tag floats on purpose, but for a job that holds a secret, a full commit SHA (bumped by Dependabot or by hand) would keep the old guarantee. Consider pinning, or confirm that you control tag protection on `niway-dev/agent-review`.

title: Safeguards from the old workflow now depend on the external workflow
body:
**Note (other): Safeguards from the old workflow now depend on the external workflow**

The old file skipped drafts, forks, Dependabot and `release-please--*` branches. It also ran the review job only for the owner's comment and queued runs per pull request. This caller has no `if:` and no `concurrency:`, so all of that now rests on `review.yml@v1`. The header only confirms the fork skip and the operator check. Please check the reusable workflow still skips Dependabot and release-please branches (ADR 0027 says reviewing them only spends money). Also check that it serialises runs per pull request, so a burst of comments does not start parallel paid runs.

title: Decision text edited in place instead of amended
body:
**Note (adr): Decision text edited in place instead of amended**

Decision 7 is rewritten to say the review runs through `niway-dev/agent-review`. That changes how the accepted decision is implemented: the repo-local script and `claude -p` are gone, and decision 2 and the front-matter description still describe them. Under the append-only rule, record this as an amendment or a new superseding ADR. The `Amends` field is still `—`, and the index is unchanged.

title: ADR 0030 reverses a 0024 non-goal but 0024 is not marked as amended
body:
**Note (adr): ADR 0030 reverses a 0024 non-goal but 0024 is not marked as amended**

The 'Relates to' row says ADR 0024's 'recording through the overlay' non-goal is the feature designed here. 0024 also rejected a second picker, and 0030 decision 4 gives the overlay a `record` intent. That changes 0024, much as 0024 amended 0022 (the index shows 'amended by 0024' on 0022). The index row for 0024 still says plain 'Proposed'. ADRs are append-only, so add a status note on 0024, such as 'amended by 0030', and update its index row. The spec also says 0022, 0024 and 0029 'all stand'. Reword it, or state which part of 0024 is amended.

title: Window target shape differs between the ADR and the spec
body:
**Note (other): Window target shape differs between the ADR and the spec**

The ADR defines `{ kind: "window", sourceId }` and `{ kind: "display", displayId }` without `name`. The spec (section 1) defines every variant with `name: string`. Pick one shape so the ADR and the spec agree before the contract task starts.

title: Grip preview can outlive a release that doesn't change the persisted size
body:
**Note (correctness): Grip preview can outlive a release that doesn't change the persisted size**

`applySize()` is the only thing that clears `previewSize`, and it only runs when the persisted size differs from `appliedBubbleSize`. If a grip drag ends on the size that is already persisted (for example, dragging out and back), or the renderer's last in-flight preview differs from `start.applied`, the settings write doesn't change the size. The hub then skips `applySize()`, and `CameraBubbleWindow.previewSize` stays set. The window can stay at the preview size while settings say another. Clearing the preview on release regardless of change would avoid this, for example with a dedicated 'preview end' call or by clearing it in the `updateSettings` path.

title: Pending throttled write is dropped on unmount
body:
**Note (correctness): Pending throttled write is dropped on unmount**

The effect cleanup clears `timer.current` without sending `latest.current`. If the last change in a burst (slider drag or key press) is made within 60 ms of the previous write and the component then unmounts, that final value is never persisted. The unmount can come from closing the Record page or the panel. Flush the pending value in the cleanup, for example by calling `send()` when the timer is set, instead of just clearing it.

title: Empty-object cast hides missing deps
body:
**Note (other): Empty-object cast hides missing deps**

`deps?.getShortcuts() ?? ({} as ShortcutSettings)` casts an empty object to the full type. `menuDeps` is always set by `createTray`, so the fallback is unreachable, and a future change that reaches it would show no accelerators with no error. Make `menuDeps` non-optional, or build the menu only after `createTray` has set it, and drop the cast and the `noop` fallbacks.

title: New RecentRecordings component and hook have no test
body:
**Note (other): New RecentRecordings component and hook have no test**

`RecentRecordings` and `useRecentRecordings` add filtering (`kind === "recording"`), sorting, a limit of 4, a refresh on window focus, and the "Today/Yesterday" label logic. Nothing in this part tests any of that. Add a small test that covers an empty list (renders null), ordering, and navigation to `/library/:assetId`.

title: Phase report accepts any finite number as the countdown value
body:
**Note (other): Phase report accepts any finite number as the countdown value**

`parsePhaseReport` accepts any finite number for `counting`. The value goes into the shade's URL and is drawn as the countdown number. The sender is our own renderer, so this is low risk. Still, the report crosses the IPC boundary, so consider restricting it to a small integer range (for example 0–10).

title: Divider drawn even when the intent switch is absent
body:
**Note (correctness): Divider drawn even when the intent switch is absent**

`SelectionToolbar` always renders the `barDivider` after `<IntentSwitch>`, but `IntentSwitch` returns null when `chrome.onIntent` is undefined (the field is optional). In that case a stray divider appears at the toolbar's left edge. `RecordWidget` guards its divider with `chrome.onIntent &&`. The toolbar should do the same. The only caller I found, capture-overlay.tsx, always sets `onIntent`, so this does not show today.

title: New record.* keys appear unused
body:
**Note (other): New record.* keys appear unused**

Keys added under the record namespace (inputMicrophone, inputSystemAudio, inputCamera, inputOn, inputOff, chipMic, chipSystem, chipCamera, frameCaption, ratioFree) have no t() call in the renderer I could find in .tsx files (the overlay uses overlay.chipMic etc.). If they are really unused, drop them from en.json and es.json to avoid dead translations. Ignore if RecordingToggles (another part) builds them dynamically.

title: Arrow-left from the unchecked-in-list "Custom" chip lands on the wrong preset
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Arrow-left from the unchecked-in-list "Custom" chip lands on the wrong preset**

When the Size value is custom (not a preset), `enabled` excludes the custom chip, so `current` is -1. Pressing → goes to index 0 (correct), but pressing ← computes `(-1 - 1 + n) % n = n - 2`, which is the second-to-last preset instead of the last one. Treat `current === -1` specially: for delta < 0 pick `enabled.length - 1`, for delta > 0 pick 0.

title: Doc comment sits on the wrong function
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Doc comment sits on the wrong function**

The block "Header + settings (or the blocked card), and the focus contract…" is placed above `useSettingsFocus`, but the first half describes `CameraSettingsContent`, which has no comment. Split the comment between the two.

title: Hardcoded ON/OFF status text bypasses i18n
body:
🟡📜 **Consider · rules: Hardcoded ON/OFF status text bypasses i18n**

Everything else on this tile goes through `useTranslations`, but "ON"/"OFF" are literals, so the Spanish locale shows English. Move them into the `cameraSettings` messages (unless the existing plain tile deliberately keeps them as literals, in which case ignore).

title: Unmount drops a pending throttled camera change
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Unmount drops a pending throttled camera change**

The effect cleanup clears `timer.current` without flushing. If the user changes a setting and the drawer or popover closes within PERSIST_EVERY_MS (60 ms), the last change is applied on screen but never sent to main, so it is lost. Flush `latest.current` through `updateSettings` on cleanup when a timer is pending, and do the same for a patch still held in `early`.

title: Switching P then V keeps the ratio but not a box that matches it
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Switching P then V keeps the ratio but not a box that matches it**

`locked` is null while the intent is `capture`, so the box can be freely drawn or resized after pressing P. The chosen ratio stays in `ratio` state. Pressing V sets `recording` back to true, and the frame is not passed through `fitRatio`. The ratio chip then shows e.g. 16:9 as pressed, and Start (line 323) and Enter send `ratio` with a rect that is not 16:9. The remembered area stores that ratio, so the next open refits the box and it jumps. Refit the frame when `recording` turns true, for example in an effect keyed on `recording`. Alternatively, reset `ratio` to `free` when leaving record.

title: Pending start can stay armed after the pick
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Pending start can stay armed after the pick**

`pendingStartId` is only cleared when the selected source matches and nothing is recording. If the settings write fails or the selection ends up on a different source, the id stays set. A later change to that source (for example choosing it again from the tray) would then start a recording unexpectedly. Consider clearing it on picker re-open or after a timeout.

title: Test name promises the panel grows, but only containment is asserted
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Test name promises the panel grows, but only containment is asserted**

The test is named "…opens the inline drawer, growing the panel" but only checks that the drawer is a descendant of the root element. Either rename it to what it checks, or assert the growth (for example, that the ResizeObserver-driven resize is requested after opening).

title: Class-equality test may pass vacuously
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Class-equality test may pass vacuously**

The test compares `className` of the number in two renders of the same CSS module. If the test setup maps CSS modules to an identity proxy or to empty strings, both sides are equal whatever the component does, so it can't tell a shared component from a copy. The earlier assertions already prove the shared overlay is used (region style, no Cancel button), so this test adds little. Drop it, or assert something that fails for a copy.

title: Region variant inherits the full-window dim and blur
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Region variant inherits the full-window dim and blur**

`.region` is added on top of `.overlay`, which has `background: rgba(0,0,0,0.72)` and `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)`. The old shade left the region only lightly dimmed (0.25) and had no blur. Now the recorded area is dimmed to 0.72 and blurred, while the outside gets only a 0.4 shadow. That is the reverse of what the doc comment says (region clear, outside dimmed). Consider overriding `background` and `backdrop-filter` in `.region`, for example a lighter background and `backdrop-filter: none`. Also check the pop and fade animations on a region that has a large box-shadow.

title: Inline `inset: "auto"` works around the class order
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Inline `inset: "auto"` works around the class order**

The inline style resets `inset` only to undo `.overlay { inset: 0 }`. Move the reset into `.region` with `inset: auto;`, and keep only left, top, width and height inline. The `position: fixed` and CSS comment then stay in one place.

title: TOOLBAR_BASE_WIDTH_DIP still budgets for the Record button
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: TOOLBAR_BASE_WIDTH_DIP still budgets for the Record button**

In the capture intent the toolbar no longer draws Record (about one button plus a divider), but the 540 DIP base width is unchanged. The toolbar width feeds `toolbarPlacement` and the `named` threshold, so the bar is placed and centred as if it were wider than it is. The PR description admits this. Either lower the constant, or compute the width by intent so the record-intent Window picker keeps its extra button. The comment above the constant now says 'Record only in the record intent', which makes the fixed 540 look inconsistent.

title: `await video.play()` has no timeout and can stall recording start
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: `await video.play()` has no timeout and can stall recording start**

`measureFrameSize` now sits on the critical path of `startEngine`, and `startEngine` awaits it before the compositor or the encoder exists. A `<video>` fed by a `MediaStream` only resolves `play()` once it has data. If the desktop track delivers no frame (the source is gone, the track is muted, or capture permission is half-granted), `play()` can stay pending. The recording then hangs on start, with no error and no fallback to the reported size. The `catch` and the fallback only run if `play()` rejects. The test file's own comment says jsdom's media element never resolves `play()`, which shows that a pending `play()` is a known state.

Race `play()` against a short timeout, for example 1–2 s, and fall through to `getSettings()` when it expires. Alternatively wait on `loadedmetadata`, with the same timeout. Add a test where `play` never resolves.

title: No test for the fallback paths of `measureFrameSize`
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: No test for the fallback paths of `measureFrameSize`**

Both new tests cover only the case where the video element reports a size that differs from `getSettings()`. Nothing covers the other branches of `measureFrameSize`: `videoWidth` of 0, a rejected `play()`, and the fallback to `getSettings()` or to the passed-in fallback size. The project's jsdom default is `videoWidth` 0, so existing tests exercise the fallback only by accident. A small `frame-size.test.ts` would pin those branches. It would also pin the cleanup of `pause()` and `srcObject = null`.

title: 10 s start timeout can fire during a first-run OS permission prompt
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: 10 s start timeout can fire during a first-run OS permission prompt**

START_TIMEOUT_MS covers getUserMedia for the screen and the mic. On first run, macOS can show a permission dialog there, and a user can take longer than 10 s to answer it. The start is then reported as failed and the late engine is discarded. Consider a longer cap, or starting the clock only after the permission-gated acquisitions. Also, `discardStart` does not end the cursor-track session that `beginCursorTrackSession` opened for a cancelled or timed-out start. Check that main cleans it up on `recordingStop` or `recordingAbort`.

title: Renderer-supplied label is logged with control characters intact
body:
🟡🔐 **Consider · security: Renderer-supplied label is logged with control characters intact**

`receiveRecordTiming` truncates the label to 80 characters but leaves newlines and other control characters in it. A compromised renderer, or any frame that can reach `recording:timing`, can forge extra `[record-timing]` lines in the main-process log. It can also send `begin` at will, which resets main's clock. The impact is low. Strip control characters, for example `label.replace(/[\^@-\^_\u007f]/g, " ")`, before logging.

The handler also does not check the IPC sender. That matches the neighbouring handlers, so I am not asking for a change there.

title: New constant is placed between the two BASE_MIN_* constants
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: New constant is placed between the two BASE_MIN_* constants**

`OVERLAY_PREWARM_AFTER_LAUNCH_MS` sits between `BASE_MIN_WIDTH` and `BASE_MIN_HEIGHT`, which splits a pair of related window-size constants. Move it above them or below `BASE_MIN_HEIGHT`.

title: ADR 0028 still says check-workflows runs `bun test ./scripts/`
body:
🟡🏛️ **Consider · adr: ADR 0028 still says check-workflows runs `bun test ./scripts/`**

This change removes `bun test ./scripts/` from `check-workflows`. It is consistent with the repo, because no test files remain under `scripts/`. But ADR 0028 (Consequences, lines 68-69) still says that `bun test ./scripts/` in `check-workflows` runs the copied review script's tests. That is no longer true. ADRs are append-only, so don't rewrite the line. Record the change in a follow-up note or amendment, or supersede the ADR. Also check that the review script copy is still tested somewhere. If its tests were deleted on purpose, say so in the PR description.

title: New paragraph opens with an orphaned reference and mixes languages
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: New paragraph opens with an orphaned reference and mixes languages**

The surrounding section is written in Spanish, but the added paragraph is in English. It also starts with 'it would otherwise keep that "Saving…"', which points at nothing in the preceding text if the earlier Saving description is not directly above. Write it in the section's language and make it self-contained.

title: Countdown length is read from two places that can briefly disagree
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Countdown length is read from two places that can briefly disagree**

Main decides whether to draw the shade from getAppSettings(), while the renderer store decides whether to count from its own cached copy (primed async, updated by broadcast). If the two differ at the moment of a start, for example right after a change, main draws no shade while the renderer counts, or main draws a shade while the renderer skips the countdown. The 'starting' report then clears it, so it is cosmetic and short-lived. Passing the length from the renderer in the start request would make the two agree.

title: releaseAll is never called, so the handle leak it targets remains
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: releaseAll is never called, so the handle leak it targets remains**

The doc comment says `releaseAll` closes every open session when a take's renderer is gone (crash, window closed mid-take). A grep of `apps/kaipu-record/src` finds no caller outside the tests. Neither the `closed` handler nor `render-process-gone` in `main/index.ts` calls it. A renderer crash or window close mid-recording therefore still leaves the file handle open. Call it from those two handlers, or remove it until something uses it.

title: A failed take-back is reported as a salvageable FinalizeMoveError
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A failed take-back is reported as a salvageable FinalizeMoveError**

If `takeBack` cannot move the file back, it returns silently. The media then stays in the vault with no sidecar, and `session.tempPath` no longer exists. The caller still gets `FinalizeMoveError(session.tempPath, cause)`, so the save dialog will offer a salvage that fails. In that case, either don't throw `FinalizeMoveError`, or point it at `dest`, where the media actually is.

title: Library scenario never asserts the recording is listed
body:
🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: Library scenario never asserts the recording is listed**

The test is named "seeded recording lists and opens its detail page", but it only sleeps 1s (`waitForTimeout(1000)`) and screenshots the list. Nothing checks that the seeded recording (title "E2E Sample") is visible. A proof screenshot taken after a fixed sleep can show an empty or half-loaded list and the scenario still passes. Replace the sleep with an assertion on the seeded item, e.g. `await expect(s.page.getByText("E2E Sample")).toBeVisible()`, then take the shot. Also check the locator against the matching e2e spec.

title: Fixed sleep before the final screenshot
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Fixed sleep before the final screenshot**

`waitForTimeout(800)` waits for the card to slide in. It is a guess and can be flaky on slow machines. The SKILL says to wait for the element and then pause briefly, so this is consistent with it. If the card has a stable end state, such as a settled bounding box, waiting on that would be more reliable.

title: A failed teardown skips video post-processing and masks the test error
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A failed teardown skips video post-processing and masks the test error**

If `teardown()` throws, for example because `app.close()` fails, the clip rename and cleanup never run. The exception also replaces any error already thrown from the test body, because `finish()` runs in `finally`. This hides the original failure. Consider wrapping teardown in try/finally, or catching and logging its error, so the clips are still finalized and the original failure is reported.

title: Comment still names the old `@agent-review` command
body: The engine was renamed to wachi-reviewer. The header comment still tells users to comment `@agent-review review`, and the file and workflow name are still `agent-review`. If the renamed engine now listens for a different mention or command, this comment is stale and on-demand runs will silently do nothing. Please confirm the trigger is unchanged, or update the comment.

title: An exact tag can still be moved; the comment says it never does
body:
🟡🔐 **Consider · security: An exact tag can still be moved; the comment says it never does**

The comment says the tag "never moves", and the ADR amendment (0028 line 99) justifies the pin by saying a moved tag would run an unreviewed release with this repository's `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. A tag like `v1.2.0` can be deleted and re-pushed by anyone with write access to wachi-reviewer, unless that repository protects tags or uses immutable releases. I could not check that from here. The old comment pointed to a full commit SHA as the way to freeze. If the key exposure is the concern, pin `@<sha> # v1.2.0`. If the engine protects its tags, say so in the comment and the ADR. Otherwise change "never moves" to "is not meant to move".

title: Intro still describes the design as "split toggle + popover"
body: Line 12 still says the chosen direction is "1a — split toggle + popover", while the UI section now says the Record page uses an inline drawer, not a popover. The line quotes the design direction's name, so it may be intentional history. A short note that the Record page later moved to a drawer would stop readers from taking the intro as the current behavior.

title: Panel-named exports now serve the Record page too
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Panel-named exports now serve the Record page too**

`MicPanelDrawer`, `SystemAudioPanelDrawer`, `CameraPanelDrawer` and `CameraPanelTile` are now used by the Record page with `variant="page"` / `compact={false}`. Their names still say "Panel", which misleads readers of `record-page.tsx`. Consider renaming them (for example `MicDrawer`) or re-exporting under neutral names. The `exclusive` doc comment in `use-settings-disclosure.ts:29-32` also still says it is used by the capture panel only.

title: Over-long doc comment line
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Over-long doc comment line**

The first line of the `MicSettingsBody` doc comment was merged into one very long line when the word "popover" was removed. Re-wrap it to match the neighbouring comments.

title: Test named "asks for more lines… and follows live changes" does not test live changes
body:
🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: Test named "asks for more lines… and follows live changes" does not test live changes**

The test only asserts the initial hook call (1080) and then calls cleanup() and renders a second bubble that receives a pushed settings change. The first `video` is detached and only checked with `expect(video).toBeDefined()`, which always passes. The second bubble starts with the stub settings, where framing is already off, so its empty transform proves nothing about following a push. Render once, push a settings change that turns framing off or lowers the zoom, and assert on that same bubble that the transform clears and the hook's lines change as expected. Alternatively, drop the "follows live changes" half from the name.

title: Doc omits that the capture resolution is frozen during a take
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Doc omits that the capture resolution is frozen during a take**

The capture-resolution paragraph says the stream is reopened when the line count changes and then holds for 400 ms. It does not mention that CameraBubble keeps the lines from the start of the take until the take ends (camera-bubble.tsx:111-116). Zooming in mid-take therefore shows a softer image in the video, because the stream stays at its old resolution. Document that trade-off, since the doc says framing works "mid-take".

title: Status banner should be 🟢 per the status legend
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Status banner should be 🟢 per the status legend**

CLAUDE.md defines 🟡 as in progress and 🟢 as "Ready to validate", which is what a shipped-but-unvalidated feature should use. This section says "implemented; pending owner validation", so 🟢 matches the legend. Also check whether the status row in backlog/index.mdx needs updating.

title: Dead compact handling left in the Size block
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Dead compact handling left in the Size block**

The Size block is now rendered only when `!compact`, so `compact={compact}` on this RadioChips is always false and can be dropped. The `sizes`, `valueText` and `onSliderKey` values (lines 276-308) are also still computed on every compact render though nothing uses them there. If the CSS still has `.fields[data-compact]` rules for the slider, ticks or range, those are dead too.

title: The automatic first-launch default gets persisted as if the user had picked it
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: The automatic first-launch default gets persisted as if the user had picked it**

The default effect calls `update({ selectedMicrophone: microphones[0] })`. That goes through `updateRecordingSettings`, and the hub (recording-hub.ts:268-274) saves any changed `selectedMicrophone` to `AppSettings.microphone`. After the first launch, the system default at that moment is stored as a user choice. If the user later changes the macOS default input, the app keeps the old device. The doc says the list puts the system default first and 'until something is picked' that one is selected, but the first launch already counts as a pick. Consider keeping the automatic default out of the remembered setting, for example by not persisting when the patch comes from the default effect. If persisting it is intended, say so in the doc.

title: Drag folders of a previous vault location are never cleaned
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Drag folders of a previous vault location are never cleaned**

cleanupDragCopies only wipes `<current vault>/.kaipu/drag`, and is called with `vaultDirectory().path` at startup and quit. If the user changes the vault directory (setVaultDirectory in vault-location.ts), any drag folder left in the old vault (crash, or a drag made in the last hour before the switch) holds hard links that are never pruned, because pruneDragCopies only runs for the vault being dragged from. They are small (hard links) but keep the file's data alive if the user later deletes the original. Consider cleaning the old vault's drag folder when the location changes.

title: Spec describes an implementation that differs from what this PR ships
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Spec describes an implementation that differs from what this PR ships**

The spec says it is the contract ("this file wins"), but the code differs from it. (1) `forceReset` aborts writer sessions via `RecordingWriter.abortAll()` in the spec (lines 17, 54-78, 215-223). The PR adds only `ids()` and keeps `writer.releaseAll()` (recording-hub.ts:862-863), which keeps the partial files on disk. The writer test also covers only `ids`. (2) The spec's `barGeneration` counter and `activity.active` check (lines 203-212) are not in the hub. The bar is already guarded by `take !== takeCount` (recording-hub.ts:691). (3) The `ControlBarWindow` `wanted` flag (Task 3) already exists (control-bar-window.ts:50, 116) and is not part of this diff. As written, the doc describes behaviour that does not exist, and "Closes: REC-B3, REC-B4" is not backed by this diff. Update the spec to match the shipped design (releaseAll, existing bar guards) or note the deviations.

title: Stamp file name no longer describes its content
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Stamp file name no longer describes its content**

The file `node_modules/.native-deps-electron-version` now holds `<electron>+patches-<hash>`, not an Electron version. The name appears in rebuild-native.sh, setup-dev.sh, release-desktop.yml and the Windows release spec. Renaming it to something like `.native-deps-stamp` would avoid confusing the next reader. This is optional, since the rename touches several files.

title: Test only checks patched sources, not the compiled binary
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Test only checks patched sources, not the compiled binary**

The test reads the C sources in node_modules. Those are patched by `bun install` whether or not `rebuild-native.sh` ran, so it cannot detect the failure that CLAUDE.md calls the trap (patched sources next to an unpatched binary). The stamp checks in setup-dev.sh and the Windows release job cover that case. The macOS release job and `build:mac` have no equivalent stamp check, so the macOS release relies only on the rebuild step not being removed. A stamp check in the macOS job would close that gap.

title: Measured numbers are promised but not included
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Measured numbers are promised but not included**

The approved spec's task list (spec line 279) asks for the cadence paragraph "with the measured numbers". This paragraph says they are "still to be measured". The spec's decision 9 also asks to confirm that requestVideoFrameCallback fires on the hidden recorder window. Measure it before merging and fill in the numbers. Otherwise, state in the PR that this spec item is open.

title: Comment line wrongly wrapped
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Comment line wrongly wrapped**

The edit left a very long line (the `meta.durationMs + 250 ... The tracker keeps sampling until ...` text) while the rest of the block wraps at ~90 columns. Re-wrap the paragraph to match the surrounding comment.

title: Pause before first-media resolves is not tracked in videoClock
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Pause before first-media resolves is not tracked in videoClock**

`videoClock` is only created when `firstMediaTimestamp` resolves. `pauseRecording` and `resumeRecording` skip it while it is null (lines 831, 841). If the user pauses and resumes before t0 resolves, that pause is never removed from the video duration. The spec lists this as the known pre-t0 pause gap and keeps it out of scope. It is not tested, though, so a test that pins the accepted behaviour would help.

title: No test covers the new visible-only guard in CameraBubbleWindow.raise()
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: No test covers the new visible-only guard in CameraBubbleWindow.raise()**

The bar's `raise()` change has a test, but the bubble's equivalent change (`raise()` now does nothing while the bubble is hidden) has none. No `camera-bubble-window*.test.ts` exists in the directory, so this is a new test file. A short test that `moveTop` is skipped after `hide()` and called when visible would stop a regression back to the macOS behaviour where `moveTop()` puts a hidden window back on screen.

title: Uncleared 5s timer after kill
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Uncleared 5s timer after kill**

The fallback `setTimeout(resolve, 5_000)` is never cleared. When `closed` settles first (the normal case after SIGKILL) the timer stays pending for up to 5s, which can hold the worker open. Keep its handle and clear it in a `finally`, as the first race does.

title: Theme-flash fix is dated the same day as the experiment, not one day before
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Theme-flash fix is dated the same day as the experiment, not one day before**

The text says `78f6deac` (2026-10-01) was fixed "one day before the experiment". Line 259 calls the same commit "the commit before the experiment" and the first experiment section (line 16) is dated 2026-10-01 too. Both can't hold: the fix landed the same day as the experiment started. Change "one day before" to "the same day, just before".

title: Release dates disagree with the changelogs
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Release dates disagree with the changelogs**

`apps/web-hono/CHANGELOG.md:3` dates web 0.11.0 as 2026-10-20. `apps/kaipu-record/CHANGELOG.md` dates desktop 0.14.0 (line 11) and 0.14.1 (line 3) as 2026-10-20. This page gives web-v0.11.0 as 2026-10-19 (line 252, and 2026-10-18/19 on line 12) and desktop as 2026-10-19/21 (line 251). Use the changelog dates, or say the 10-18/19 dates are when the work merged rather than when it shipped. The "both Pre-release" claim isn't backed by anything in the repo I could find.

title: Stage 3 status differs between ADR and backlog
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Stage 3 status differs between ADR and backlog**

The ADR status says stages 3–4 are planned. The backlog table (stylex-migration.md:253) says stage 3 is "partly" done. Align the two, for example by saying stage 3 has started in the ADR, or by calling it open in the table. The ADR status cell is also getting long. Move the web-v0.11.0 detail to the backlog page, which already carries it.

title: Deadline-range test only restates the constant
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Deadline-range test only restates the constant**

This test asserts `QUIT_DEADLINE_MS` is between 10 s and 30 s. It exercises no behaviour, and its name promises a relation to Playwright's 120 s timeout that it never checks (`playwright.config.ts:45`). It fails only when someone edits the constant, and the failure says nothing about the hang. Either delete it, or assert the real relation by importing the timeout. For example, export the 120 s value and check that deadline + sample timeout (20 s in `sampleProcess`) + launch fits inside it.

title: pick() still opens windows after dispose()
body: `dispose()` sets `disposed`, and `scheduleWarm` checks it. `pick()` does not. After `before-quit` has run `begin()`, a pick can still arrive (an IPC from the main window while it closes). `pick()` then calls `createOverlay` for every display, or reuses spares. That is the window-created-after-quit case this PR is meant to stop (NIW2-548). Only the `browser-window-created` guard in app-shutdown.ts would catch it, and that guard logs it as a leak. Add `if (this.disposed) return Promise.resolve({ kind: "cancelled" })` at the top of `pick()`, and a test for it. The current tests only cover `prewarm()`.

title: disposeCaptureOverlay does nothing when the overlay was never created, and a later pick builds a live one
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: disposeCaptureOverlay does nothing when the overlay was never created, and a later pick builds a live one**

`overlayWindows` is created lazily by `overlayWindowsInstance()` (lines 56-64). If no overlay existed at quit, `disposeCaptureOverlay()` does nothing because `overlayWindows?.dispose()` is a no-op on null. A later `overlay.pick` then creates a fresh, non-disposed instance and opens windows. Keep a module-level `disposed` flag that `overlay.pick` and `prewarmCaptureOverlay` check, or create the instance in `disposeCaptureOverlay` and dispose it.

title: One throw in hub.dispose() skips the rest of the hub's teardown
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: One throw in hub.dispose() skips the rest of the hub's teardown**

`hub.dispose()` is a single participant. If `shade.destroy()` or `bar.destroy()` throws, the later calls do not run, and `AppShutdown` only logs the failure. `ControlBarWindow.destroy()` (control-bar-window.ts:170-175) calls `this.window?.destroy()` without an `isDestroyed()` check. Electron throws when you call `destroy()` on an already-destroyed window. If the control bar's window was already destroyed, `cameraBubble.destroy()` never runs, and that is a window the quit would wait on. Wrap each step in its own try/catch, or register the shade, bar and bubble as separate participants. Also, neither the control bar nor the camera bubble gets a `disposed` flag. After `hub.dispose()`, a `show()` on either can create a window again.

title: The ADR says every window class gets a disposed flag; the control bar and camera bubble do not
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The ADR says every window class gets a disposed flag; the control bar and camera bubble do not**

Decision 2 says "Each window class gains a `destroy()` and a `disposed` flag; after it, `prewarm()` / `show()` create nothing." That holds for the capture panel, shade, toast and overlay windows. `ControlBarWindow` and `CameraBubbleWindow` already had `destroy()` and get no flag in this diff, so their `show()` can still create a window after the quit began. Either add the flag to both, or reword the decision to say these two rely on the `browser-window-created` guard.

title: ADR index not updated for 0032 and 0033
body: The ADR index (decisions/index.mdx) stops at 0031 (line 16). This PR adds ADRs 0032 and 0033 but does not add rows for them, so they are missing from the index that CLAUDE.md and the review rules treat as the catalogue. Add one row each (title, status 'Proposed', date 2026-10-29). I could not edit this file here since it is not in the diff; the finding is placed on the existing last row.

title: Switching to Opus 5.5 contradicts ADR 0028's decision 1 with no amendment
body:
🟡🏛️ **Consider · adr: Switching to Opus 5.5 contradicts ADR 0028's decision 1 with no amendment**

ADR 0028 is accepted, and its decision 1 says "**Claude Sonnet 5.5 reviews a pull request**" (`apps/documentation/src/content/docs/architecture/decisions/0028-advisory-claude-review-on-pull-requests.mdx:31`). Its frontmatter description says the same (line 3). This line moves the review to `claude-opus-5-5`, but the PR does not touch the ADR. The ADR already records later engine changes as dated amendments (lines 83–101).

Suggested fix: add an amendment, e.g. "Amendment: reviews run on Opus 5.5" dated 2026-10-29. Put the model change and the cost reasoning from this PR's body in it, and update the Status row. The ADR stays append-only, so leave decision 1 as written and let the amendment record the change.

title: ITEM_NOT_FOUND_MARKER doc still mentions a case that no longer rejects
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: ITEM_NOT_FOUND_MARKER doc still mentions a case that no longer rejects**

The comment says a rename rejects with this marker when the id no longer names a media file, giving "already renamed by a double commit" as an example. That was true before this PR. Now `renameItem` finds the item by `assetId` under the names lock (`resolveTarget` → `resolveIdentity`, library-vault.ts:497-499), so a second commit follows the item to its new name and does not reject. It only throws `ItemNotFoundError` when no item has that `assetId` any more. `electron-api.ts:227` already describes this correctly ("Rejects when no item has `assetId`"). Suggest rewording this comment to match it, and the same for `ItemNotFoundError` at library-vault.ts:95.

title: renameItem doc says a failed title write throws ItemNotFoundError, but the fs error is rethrown as is
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: renameItem doc says a failed title write throws ItemNotFoundError, but the fs error is rethrown as is**

The docstring says `renameItem` "Throws `ItemNotFoundError` for an id without media, or when even the title cannot be written." But the title write at line 417 (`await atomicWriteFile(oldSidecar, …)`) has no try/catch. On a read-only vault or a locked sidecar the raw fs error (EACCES, EPERM, …) is rethrown without the `ITEM_NOT_FOUND_MARKER`. Either wrap that write so it matches the doc, or change the doc to say a failed title write rethrows the underlying error. Callers that use the marker to tell "gone" apart from other failures depend on this.

title: If the app crashes after allocateId, the stub sidecar is never cleaned up and its stem stays taken
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: If the app crashes after allocateId, the stub sidecar is never cleaned up and its stem stays taken**

`allocateId` writes a stub sidecar (with a fresh `assetId`) before the media exists. Failures are handled: `vault.remove(id)` runs when the move fails (line 204), and screenshot-save.ts and stranded-recordings.ts do the same. A crash or kill between the allocation and `moveFile` is not handled, though. It leaves `.kaipu/<stem>.json` with no media and no `localRemovedAt`. `isStemFree` treats such an orphan sidecar as a cloud-only item (library-vault.ts:268-271), so the stem stays reserved for good. Stranded recovery then brings the take back under "… (recovered)" and never reclaims or removes the stub. One option is to mark stubs (for example `pendingSince`) and sweep stale ones during `recoverStrandedRecordings`.

title: The case-only rename test never runs the case-insensitive branch on Linux CI
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The case-only rename test never runs the case-insensitive branch on Linux CI**

The test uses a temp directory from `mkdtemp(tmpdir())`. On Linux that directory is case-sensitive, so `isStemFree("Demo")` is true and `resolveRenameTarget` returns `mode: "free"` at `library-vault.ts:337`. It never reaches the `mode: "case"` / `moveInPlace` branch at `library-vault.ts:338-339`, which exists for APFS and NTFS. The test passes on CI, but the branch its name describes is untested there. To cover that branch everywhere, you could stub `isStemFree`/`isSameFile` so the folded name reads as taken by the same file, or add a test that runs only on a case-insensitive filesystem.

title: Roundabout file name expression in the media-URL test
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Roundabout file name expression in the media-URL test**

`` `${id}.mp4`.replace(".mp4", " clip.mp4") `` just produces `` `${id} clip.mp4` ``. Writing that directly would be easier to read. The test also looks up `` `${id} clip` `` a few lines further down.

title: ADR index says "nothing implemented yet" for an ADR this PR implements
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: ADR index says "nothing implemented yet" for an ADR this PR implements**

This index row lists ADR 0032 as "Proposed — design NIW2-560, nothing implemented yet". That isn't true. The ADR's own status table (0032 line 12) says it is implemented on this branch with acceptance pending owner QA, and this PR ships the implementation. Change the row to match, for example "Proposed — implemented, owner QA + manual Windows test pending". Row 0031 uses the same wording.

title: Gotcha leaves out the ambiguous-identity rejection
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Gotcha leaves out the ambiguous-identity rejection**

This gotcha says a rename rejects only for an unknown id (`ITEM_NOT_FOUND_MARKER`) or a title that cannot be written. The same page contradicts it at line 112, which says `AmbiguousIdentityError` is thrown before anything changes, and so does ipc-contract.mdx line 88, which lists `AMBIGUOUS_IDENTITY_MARKER` and invalid arguments as rejections. The renderer also handles that case with its own toast. Add the ambiguous-identity case (and invalid arguments) here so a reader doesn't assume the renderer only needs to handle not-found.

title: §4–§5 contract blocks describe an API the later change-log entries replaced
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: §4–§5 contract blocks describe an API the later change-log entries replaced**

The code blocks in the spec body still show `renameLocalRecording(id: string, title: string)` (line 269), a handler that takes only `id`/`title` (lines 275–281), `renameItem(id, title, …)` (line 211) and `RenameKeptReason = "locked" | "busy" | "io"` (line 184). The code that shipped is `renameLocalRecording(id, assetId, title)` (`shared/types/electron-api.ts:230`) and `RenameKeptReason` now includes `"editing"` (`shared/types/library-storage.ts:80`). The §5.1 outcome table also has no rows for `editing` or the ambiguous-identity toast. The change log (lines 397–402) records each of these changes, so nothing here is hidden. But someone who reads §5 as the contract gets the wrong signature, and the header (line 8) says the spec is implemented. Consider adding a one-line "superseded, see change log / ipc-contract.mdx" note at the top of §4 and §5, or updating the signatures and the table in place.

title: "Audio on fixed presets is AAC 128 kbps" is now false for YouTube
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: "Audio on fixed presets is AAC 128 kbps" is now false for YouTube**

This bullet is unchanged, but the YouTube canvases are fixed presets too, and they now target 384 kbps. `resolveExportTarget` picks `YOUTUBE_AUDIO_BITRATE` (384_000) for them in `export-presets.ts:489`, and the table row and the new section in this same doc both say 384 kbps. Suggested wording: "Audio on Vertical and Square is AAC 128 kbps …; YouTube uses 384 kbps (see below)".

title: Wrong claim that upscaling used the default filter before this PR
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Wrong claim that upscaling used the default filter before this PR**

The fixed-canvas framer, which upscales YouTube Fit output, already set `imageSmoothingEnabled = true` and `imageSmoothingQuality = "high"` before this PR (`compose-output-frame.ts:213-214` and `:220-221`, untouched here). The code comment this PR adds at `:99` says so too: "as the fixed-canvas framer does". The zoom crop also already had `"high"` quality. This PR only adds `imageSmoothingEnabled = true` there, plus high-quality smoothing for contained slides (`drawContained`). Saying upscaling "now" uses high quality and "used the default filter" before overstates the change: readers will think it explains a visual difference. Suggested wording: "slides drawn onto the canvas now use `imageSmoothingQuality = \"high\"` as well (the framer and zoom crop already did)". For the same reason, the first two tests in `compose-output-frame.test.ts` cover behaviour that existed before this PR, not something it adds.

title: Preview sync uses `t + offset`; the rest of the spec uses `t − offset`
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Preview sync uses `t + offset`; the rest of the spec uses `t − offset`**

The spec defines `startOffsetMs = webcamT0 − screenT0` (line 255). With that definition, screen time `t` maps to webcam time `t − offset`. Section 2 says so (line 262: `webcamTs ≤ t − startOffsetMs / 1000`), failure 8 agrees (`timestamp + offset ≤ sourceTs`, line 137), and so does the export iterator window (`[sourceStart − offset, sourceEnd − offset]`, line 486).

The preview rules have the sign the other way round: the seek at line 457 (`webcam.currentTime = t + offset`), the drift check at line 460, and failure 13 at line 152 (`|webcam.currentTime − (t + offset)| > 80 ms`). If someone implements these as written, a late-started webcam is shifted by twice the offset in the preview only, and the preview disagrees with the export. Change all three to `t − offset`.

title: getUserMedia width `lines * 4/3` gives 960×720, not the 1280×720 the decision names
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: getUserMedia width `lines * 4/3` gives 960×720, not the 1280×720 the decision names**

Decision 4 (line 57) and ADR 0032 decision 1 both specify 1280×720 @ 30 fps, which is 16:9. The constraint at line 188 asks for `width: { ideal: lines * 4/3 }`. For 720 lines that is 960, a 4:3 width. For 1080 lines it is 1440 instead of 1920. Use `lines * 16/9`, or state the width outright, so the requested size matches the decided one.

title: Failure 2 sends Windows before 10 2004 to "Plan B's fallback", but Plan B is macOS-only
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Failure 2 sends Windows before 10 2004 to "Plan B's fallback", but Plan B is macOS-only**

Failure 2 says that on Windows before 10 2004 the `fullDisplayBorderAllowed` rule "selects Plan B's fallback behaviour". Section 3.3 (lines 300, 321) and ADR 0032 (consequences, line 107) both say Plan B is a native ScreenCaptureKit module for macOS only, and that "the Windows path stays Chromium either way". So no Plan B exists on Windows to fall back to. Section 3.2 (lines 293–296) uses the same gate only to decide whether Plan A works there.

Please state what the bubble actually does on pre-2004 Windows: for example, it is not shown during a take, or it is captured. Otherwise the test this failure line is supposed to seed has no defined expectation.

title: Page now says the repo is public, but the "Pre-open checklist" still reads as future work
body:
This PR rewrites the intro (line 10, "public since 2026-10-05") and the Timing section (lines 128–131). It also drops "what has to happen before the repository goes public" from the description. The rest of the page still treats opening the repo as a future event:

- "The monorepo opens as a whole" (lines 71–74) says "the cost of that is a security pass on the server before the day it happens" and calls it "a hard prerequisite".
- The "Pre-open checklist" (line 76) says "Nothing below is optional". Items 1–4 and 8 (history secret scan, security hardening, docs language, personal references, first signed release) are not marked done, while 5–7 are.

A reader can't tell whether the repo went public with items 1–4 still open, or whether they were finished and never marked. Consider marking each item done or accepted. You could also rename the section (for example "Open-time checklist") and change the "before the day it happens" wording to describe what happened.

title: Who holds the copyright that Niway would relicense: Cristian Sotomayor or Niway S.A.C.?
body:
🟡❓ **Consider · question: Who holds the copyright that Niway would relicense: Cristian Sotomayor or Niway S.A.C.?**

The CLA's whole purpose is stated here: "Kaipu has one owner who can decide how the whole project is licensed", and CONTRIBUTING.md:38-39 repeats it ("keep the whole project under one owner, including the right to change its license later"). Every contributor license goes to **Niway S.A.C.** (CLA.md:5, §2). But README.md:284 names the copyright holder as **Cristian Sotomayor** personally, "published by Niway S.A.C.".

If Cristian holds the copyright in the bulk of the code and has no written assignment or exclusive license to Niway, Niway would hold relicensing rights only over contributors' code, not the core. The "one owner" premise would then fail. Is there an assignment or license from Cristian to Niway? If not, should the README notice name Niway, or should the CLA grant go to both parties? You flagged this in the PR body. I'm raising it on the CLA because that is the document whose promise depends on the answer.

title: The CLA claims to cover issue attachments and any communication, but only PR authors ever sign it
body:
🟡❓ **Consider · question: The CLA claims to cover issue attachments and any communication, but only PR authors ever sign it**

§1 defines "Contribution" to include an "issue attachment or any other channel", and "Submit" covers "any form of electronic or written communication". CONTRIBUTING.md:9-11 says issues are how everyone outside the collaborator group contributes. The only way to accept the CLA is a comment on a first pull request (How to sign, CLA.md:89). So an issue reporter who attaches a patch or snippet has never agreed to these terms, and §2's relicensing grant does not reach their material. Do you want to narrow §1 to material submitted by someone who has signed? Or should CONTRIBUTING say that code pasted into issues is used only once its author has signed the CLA?

title: LEGAL_VERSION is not imported anywhere; the visible version is a hard-coded i18n string
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: LEGAL_VERSION is not imported anywhere; the visible version is a hard-coded i18n string**

Nothing in the repository imports `LEGAL_VERSION`. legal-page.tsx, legal-links.tsx and signup-legal-notice.tsx import only `LEGAL_DOCUMENTS` and `LEGAL_CONTACT_EMAIL`. The "Version 2026-10-30" shown on `/legal/*` comes from the literal `updated` messages in packages/i18n/messages/en.json:1335 and es.json:1335 (legal-page.tsx:26). Bumping this constant changes nothing at runtime, and the next legal update has to change three places by hand. Either drop the constant, or build the `updated` message from it with an ICU `{version}` parameter so there is a single source of truth.

title: New `metadataIssue` branch of isCloudUploadEligible is untested
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: New `metadataIssue` branch of isCloudUploadEligible is untested**
