`isCloudUploadEligible` now also returns false when `local.metadataIssue` is set. The only test for it, `library-item.test.ts:50-55`, still covers only `kind`. The function has no production caller yet: the only matches are in that test file. So the upload flow for NIW2-214 will depend on this rule without a test protecting it. Consider adding a case such as `isCloudUploadEligible({ kind: "recording", local: { metadataIssue: "corrupt" } }) === false`.

title: Quarantine set is never cleared, so a second corruption in the same session gets no copy
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Quarantine set is never cleared, so a second corruption in the same session gets no copy**

`quarantinedSidecars` keeps a path for the rest of the process (line 73), and nothing removes it after the sidecar reads cleanly again. Here is the sequence: a sidecar is corrupt and gets copied aside. It is repaired, for example by a cloud sync, and later writes go into it. Then it becomes corrupt again (truncated again, or hand-edited). The second corrupt version is never copied, because `quarantine` returns early. Consider calling `quarantinedSidecars.delete(path)` in `sidecar()` when a parse succeeds. Alternatively, key the set by path plus size/mtime.

title: PART_RE gained a capture group that nothing reads
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: PART_RE gained a capture group that nothing reads**

`PART_RE` is now `/^kaipu-rec-(.+)\.mp4\.part$/`, but the code only calls `.test()` on it. The webcam pairing uses `webcamPartFor` and a string `replace` instead. You could drop the parentheses so nobody goes looking for where the captured id is used.

title: A trailing `--vault` with no value crashes the script instead of printing usage
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A trailing `--vault` with no value crashes the script instead of printing usage**

`argv[++i]` returns `undefined` when `--vault` is the last argument. `vault` then becomes `undefined`, and `join(vault, ...)` at line 79 throws a TypeError with a stack trace, when the user should get the usage message and exit code 2. You could check for a missing value and fall through to the same usage error.

title: Doc comment still says 480 lines is the ceiling, but the only caller now always asks for at least 720
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Doc comment still says 480 lines is the ceiling, but the only caller now always asks for at least 720**

The comment still says "480 lines is the ceiling worth asking for without framing; more would only cost CPU", and `DEFAULT_PREVIEW_LINES = 480` is still the default. That is no longer how the hook is used. Its only caller, `camera-bubble.tsx:115`, now passes `bubblePreviewLines(bubble)`. That value is `max(cameraCaptureLines, webcamCaptureLines)` (`shared/webcam-track.ts:67-69`), and `webcamCaptureLines` never goes below `WEBCAM_LINES_DEFAULT = 720` (`webcam-track.ts:16,56`). So the bubble now opens the camera at 720 lines even without framing, as the updated camera-bubble tests show (480 → 720).

The 480 default is now reached only by the hook's own tests. Please rewrite the comment to say the bubble asks for 720 lines because the webcam track shares the capture, and either drop the default or note that it is not the bubble's real request.

title: "turned on or off during the countdown" only tests turning it off
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "turned on or off during the countdown" only tests turning it off**

The start input resolves `webcam` the first time and `null` the second (line 1519). So this test only covers a camera turned off during the countdown. The opposite case is a take that began with the camera off, where turning it on during the countdown should re-acquire it with a webcam (`recorder-store.ts:386-387`). That case is not exercised. You could add the mirror case (`resolves++ === 0 ? null : webcam`) and assert that the last `prepareEngine` call has `webcam: { deviceId: "cam-1", lines: 720 }`, or rename the test to "turned off".

title: Comment says the export burns in the webcam layer, but nothing draws it yet
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Comment says the export burns in the webcam layer, but nothing draws it yet**

The comment says "with one, the layer is part of what the export burns in". Today that is false. Outside the tests, `webcamAt` and `scene.webcam` are only read by webcam-model.ts, webcam-edits.ts, scene.ts and session.ts. No composer or export worker reads them. So exports made from webcam recordings between this PR and NIW2-575 carry a fingerprint that claims the face is in the file. The PR body says the `ENCODE_REVISION` bump that fixes this is deferred (W4). Consider saying that in the comment too, e.g. "once the export draws the layer (NIW2-575, which bumps ENCODE_REVISION)". Then nobody reading this code later assumes interim exports already contain the webcam.

title: The DIP-fallback test says "within the limits" but never reaches a limit
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The DIP-fallback test says "within the limits" but never reaches a limit**

Both cases stay inside `WEBCAM_LIMITS` without being clamped. 270/1080 = 0.25 and 120/1080 ≈ 0.111, and both are already between `minSize` 0.1 and `maxSize` 0.6 (`webcam-model.ts:46-47`). So nothing here checks that the fallback at `webcam-model.ts:114` goes through the clamp. If someone later moved the clamp off that path, this test would still pass. Add a case below 108 DIP that should clamp to the minimum, e.g. `expect(size(60)).toBe(WEBCAM_LIMITS.minSize)`. Or drop "within the limits" from the test's name.

title: Bubble reads as selected whenever any webcam segment is selected, including a hidden one
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Bubble reads as selected whenever any webcam segment is selected, including a hidden one**

`selected={selectedWebcamId !== null}` is true for the layer selection and also for any segment id picked in the lane. WebcamLayer uses it for `aria-pressed` and `data-selected` (webcam-layer.tsx:187,195). So if you click a *hidden* segment in the lane, the bubble on screen shows as pressed/selected even though that segment's inspector has no layout controls. The same happens with an override segment while the playhead sits outside it. Consider marking the bubble selected only when `selectedWebcamId === WEBCAM_LAYER_SELECTION`, or when the selected id is the override that covers the current source time (the same check `onSelect` already does).

title: Selecting the bubble drops its shadow
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Selecting the bubble drops its shadow**

Both `[data-shadow="true"]` and `[data-selected="true"]` set `filter`, and the selected rule comes later. So a selected bubble with Shadow on loses its drop shadow, and the preview stops matching the setting while the user is editing it. You could add a combined rule, `.bubble[data-shadow="true"][data-selected="true"]`, that chains the accent outline drop-shadows with the shadow.

title: Shrink note says the webcam stays "in its corner", but the bubble can be anywhere
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Shrink note says the webcam stays "in its corner", but the bubble can be anywhere**

The inspector offers nine presets, including Center and the edge midpoints, and the bubble can be dragged anywhere. "Stays in its corner" is wrong for those positions. Something like "the webcam keeps its position either way" would be accurate. The same applies to es.json line 1180 ("se queda en su esquina").

title: A failed webcam fetch fails the whole export
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A failed webcam fetch fails the whole export**

`fetchWebcamTrack` runs in the same `try` as the source fetch, so if the webcam fetch or `response.blob()` throws, the result is `fail(GENERIC_ERROR, …)` and no file is made. A 404 is already handled: it returns null (media-protocol.ts serves 404 when the take has no webcam file). But the rest of the PR says a broken webcam never fails the export (`openWebcamSourceOrNone`, the `webcam-error` message). Consider catching the webcam fetch on its own: report it via `captureException` with context `video-export-webcam` and continue with `webcam = null`. The GIF path has the same coupling: in use-gif-export.ts:200/264, `await webcamTrack(args)` rejecting goes to `fail(t("gifExportError"))`.

title: Fill frames shrink the bubble with zoom while the crop stays frozen
body:
🟡❓ **Consider · question: Fill frames shrink the bubble with zoom while the crop stays frozen**

Each fill re-composes the held frame at `frame.timestamp`, so `planClipFrame`'s crop (the zoom) stays at the held frame's time. The webcam layer, though, reads `cameraAt(camera, t).scale` at the fill time `t` (compose-output-frame.ts:178). If a zoom ramps during a still-screen gap, the export shows the bubble shrinking or growing while the content under it stays put, then jumps at the next screen frame. The preview animates both together. Is this mismatch intended? One option: pass the held frame's time for the camera scale on fills. Another: let fills advance the crop and keep redactions on the held frame's span.

title: Source-text regex guard is brittle and checks only a little
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Source-text regex guard is brittle and checks only a little**

This test strips comments and then matches the worker sources against `createOutputComposer\(\{[^}]*webcam: plan\.webcam` and `compose\.clip\([^)]*webcam`. It fails on harmless refactors: a nested object literal before `webcam:` (the `[^}]*` stops at the first `}`), a renamed local, or the composer options being built in a variable first. It also passes when the code is wrong in ways that matter, for example passing `webcam` in a branch that never runs, or passing a webcam frame from the wrong timestamp. A better shape: pull the small piece of each worker that builds the composer options and the per-frame `clip` arguments into a shared helper, and unit-test that helper. If you keep the source scan, a comment on its limits would stop later readers from relying on it as coverage.

title: "never past it" is in the test name but no assertion checks it
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "never past it" is in the test name but no assertion checks it**

The test only passes `x: 1, y: 1`, which sits exactly on the edge. It never passes a pan beyond ±1, so nothing exercises the `clamp(value, -1, 1)` in `webcamSourceRect` (`webcam-layout.ts:117`). If that clamp were removed, the test would still pass. Suggestion: add a case such as `{ zoom: 2, x: 3, y: -3 }` and assert it equals the `x: 1, y: -1` result. A non-finite pan (NaN → 0) could go in too. Either change makes the test check what its name says.

title: Files dropped while an import runs are silently thrown away
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Files dropped while an import runs are silently thrown away**

`run` returns right away when `busy.current` is set (line 64), and nothing tells the user. The header button and the drop zone are disabled while `importing` is true, but `useFileDrop` keeps catching drops on the whole window (`use-file-drop.ts:40-46`). `LibraryPage` sends every drop to `importDropped` (`library-page.tsx:55`), and that calls `run` at line 98. If the user drops a second batch during a long copy (files can be gigabytes), those files are never imported and no toast appears. The `importing` doc at line 27 says "a second one waits for it", which the code doesn't do. Either queue the second call behind the running one (chain it on a stored promise), or show a toast such as "An import is already running" when `busy.current` is set. Then update the comment to match.

title: Doc says every failed file gets its reason, but the multi-failure toast drops the reasons
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Doc says every failed file gets its reason, but the multi-failure toast drops the reasons**

The doc says "Every file that failed is named in an error toast with the reason". `failureMessage` in `use-import-videos.ts:109-121` gives a reason only when exactly one file failed. When two or more fail, it uses `importFailedMany` ("Couldn’t import {count} files: {fileNames}"), which lists the names and no reasons. The test at `use-import-videos.test.tsx:95` asserts exactly that. Change the sentence to say that a single failure shows its reason and several failures list only the file names. The other option is to add the reasons to the many-files toast.

title: "Only videos can be imported" also names video files that were skipped only because they have no path on disk
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: "Only videos can be imported" also names video files that were skipped only because they have no path on disk**

`importDropped` (`use-import-videos.ts:86-93`) puts a file in `skipped` for either of two reasons: its extension isn't importable, or `pathForFile` returns "" (for example, a file dragged out of a web page). Both cases get the same message. So a dropped `web.mp4` produces "Only videos can be imported (MP4, MOV, M4V or WebM). Skipped: notes.pdf, web.mp4", which tells the user their MP4 isn't a video. The test at `use-import-videos.test.tsx:137` locks this wording in. Consider a separate message for path-less files, such as "isn’t a file on your computer", or a more neutral wording for the shared one. The same applies to `es.json:624`.

title: YouTube's "Ready" badge and the detail's "Open existing" can disagree
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: YouTube's "Ready" badge and the detail's "Open existing" can disagree**

The list row shows the Ready badge when *any* preset of the destination already has a reusable copy (`presetsOf(d).some(...)`). The detail pane's `existing` (line 329) only looks at the preset that is selected right now (`presetForDestination(selected, probe, youtube)`). Example: a 4K YouTube copy exists, but the default for a 1080p source is 1440p. The row says "Ready", and clicking it shows a plain "Prepare for YouTube · ~N MB" button with no "Open existing". One fix is to compute the badge from the preset the row would actually make (`reusable[presetForDestination(d, probe, youtube)]`). The other is to switch `youtube` to the preset that already exists when the user picks the row.

title: "Only when the copy fits" test never checks the negative case
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "Only when the copy fits" test never checks the negative case**

This test's name is "GitHub promises the 10 MB limit only when the copy fits it". It uses the 3:02 recording, whose Light estimate does not fit the 10 MB limit (`destinations.test.ts:114`). But it only checks that the "Small copy that plays inline" subtitle is shown. It never checks that "Under the 10 MB limit" is absent. If the conditional at `prepare-page.tsx:271` (`d === "github" && plan.underGithubFreeLimit`) regressed to always show the promise, this test would still pass, because `getByText` on the fallback subtitle succeeds either way only when the branch is correct. Add `expect(within(github).queryByText("Under the 10 MB limit")).toBeNull()` so the test covers what its name says.

title: "not merged yet" goes stale when this PR merges
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: "not merged yet" goes stale when this PR merges**

The new superseded note says Prepare lives "on `feature/niw2-578-prepare-screen` (not merged yet)". This note arrives in the same PR as the code, so once the PR merges the sentence is false: the recording page will already use Prepare on main. Consider removing the branch name and the parenthesis, or naming the PR instead. prepare-screen.md's status line already tracks merge state, so this note doesn't need to.

title: Any `workspaces:changed` clears the switching guard, not only the end of a switch
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Any `workspaces:changed` clears the switching guard, not only the end of a switch**

The listener sets `switching = false` on every `workspaces:changed`. Main sends that broadcast for registry edits and busy-state changes too (dismissHint, remove, `notifyWorkspaceBusyChanged`), not only when a switch ends. If one of those arrives after this window answered prepare but before the switch commits, the window takes item calls again, still under the old stamp. The main-side gate should still refuse them, so this is defence in depth rather than a leak. Still, the preload's own guarantee ("nothing this window starts can reach main") breaks. One fix: clear `switching` only when the generation in the broadcast differs from the current stamp's, or on `prepare-abort`.

title: Only screenshot and thumb URLs carry `w`; a URL without it still resolves in whatever workspace is active
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Only screenshot and thumb URLs carry `w`; a URL without it still resolves in whatever workspace is active**

`LibraryVault.describe` adds `w` only to the `screenshot/` and `thumb/` URLs (library-vault.ts:182-184). This check skips every URL without `w`, so recording/video playback URLs, and any URL built elsewhere without `w`, resolve against the active workspace. A video URL cached before a switch can therefore play another workspace's item that has the same id, which is the case this comment says cannot happen. Either stamp every media URL the app hands out, or narrow the comment to what is actually covered.

title: Can `requireCaptureWorkspace` rebind the stamp inside a scoped call and make a successful save reject as stale?
body:
🟡❓ **Consider · question: Can `requireCaptureWorkspace` rebind the stamp inside a scoped call and make a successful save reject as stale?**

`requireCaptureWorkspace` calls `rebindAfterAdoption(id)` when the folder's identity differs from the stamp (workspaces/index.ts:109). Here it runs inside `scoped(...)` for the editor's Save. If that rebind broadcasts `workspaces:changed` with a new generation before the invoke reply, the preload's `sameStamp(stamp, sent)` check (preload/index.ts:86) throws `stale-workspace` even though the PNG was written. The user could then save again and get a duplicate item. Does the rebind broadcast before the reply? If it does, should adoption happen outside item-scoped calls?

title: Adoption check compares the probed id with the gate stamp, so it can rebind the gate to a workspace that is no longer active
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Adoption check compares the probed id with the gate stamp, so it can rebind the gate to a workspace that is no longer active**

`requireCaptureWorkspace` captures `active` before the `await reg.availability(active.id)` but compares the result with `workspaceGate().stamp.workspaceId` after the await. If a switch commits while the probe is running (`switchWorkspace` → `gate.commit(target)`, switch-transaction.ts:75), `id` is still the old workspace's id and the stamp is the new one. They differ, so `rebindAfterAdoption(id)` points the gate back at the old workspace while `reg.active()` is the new one. Renderer calls stamped with the committed stamp are then refused until the next broadcast.

`listState` (line 137) has a related window. `registry.setActive` sets `key.activeId` before it awaits `persist` (registry.ts:511-513). A `listState` running during that write sees the target as `reg.active()` while the gate still holds the old id, so it rebinds the gate to the target. If `persist` then fails, `setActive` restores the old activeId and the switch calls `gate.reopen()`. The gate ends up open and bound to the target while the registry's active entry is the old one.

Adoption is the only case that should trigger a rebind: the probed entry's own id changed. Testing that directly (`if (id !== active.id && reg.active().id === id)` here, and the equivalent `id !== <entry id before the await>` in `listState`) would stop a concurrent switch from being mistaken for an adoption.

title: A window closed during prepare blocks the switch for the full 120 s timeout
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A window closed during prepare blocks the switch for the full 120 s timeout**

`prepareWindows` sends one request to each window and waits until that window answers or `PREPARE_TIMEOUT_MS` (120 s) expires. If a window is closed or its renderer crashes after the request goes out, nothing answers. The switch waits two minutes and is then cancelled, and `inFlight` blocks any other switch during that time (switch-transaction.ts:48). Listening for `webContents` `destroyed` / `render-process-gone` inside the promise and resolving `true` (that window has nothing left to flush), or `false`, would end the wait at once.

title: update() keeps the in-memory change when the write fails
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: update() keeps the in-memory change when the write fails**

`update` runs `mutate(this.key)` and then `persist`. If `persist` throws (for example preferences.json became unparseable, line 548, or the disk is full), the change stays in memory. So `add()` (lines 467/471/490) rejects, yet the new entry is in `entries()` and shows in the switcher. `remove()` (line 500) also rejects, yet the entry is gone for the rest of the session. The next successful write then stores a change the user was told had failed. `setActive` (lines 510–517) already rolls back on failure. Snapshotting `this.key` (e.g. `structuredClone`) before `mutate` and restoring it on a failed `persist` would give `add` and `remove` the same guarantee. `refresh` can keep its best-effort behaviour.

title: Pending captures are dropped before the step that can still abort the switch
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Pending captures are dropped before the step that can still abort the switch**

`dropPendingCaptures()` runs before `persistActive(target)`. If `persistActive` throws (`setActive` rethrows a failed persist, registry.ts:513–516), the old workspace stays active and the windows go back to normal, but the retained quiet-capture bytes and toasts are already gone. That breaks the doc comment's promise that a failure before the commit leaves the old workspace "active and unchanged". A Copy whose save failed (the bytes are kept once for Edit) loses its only stored copy. Dropping the captures after `persistActive` succeeds, still under the closed gate, keeps that promise.

title: "refuses ... the last workspace" never reaches the `last` refusal
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "refuses ... the last workspace" never reaches the `last` refusal**

Both assertions in this test expect `reason: "active"`. The test never sees the `"last"` outcome. In `registry.ts:498-499` the `active` check runs before `entries.length <= 1`. The active id always points at a registered entry, so with a single entry that entry is the active one, and `remove` returns `"active"` before it gets to `"last"`. So the test name promises coverage of a branch that, as far as I can tell, can't be reached at all. You could rename the test to cover only the active refusal. Or, if the `last` guard is there on purpose as defence in depth, add a comment in `registry.ts` that says so, so nobody assumes this test covers it.

title: Menu says "Saving to: Here" while the active workspace is not connected
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Menu says "Saving to: Here" while the active workspace is not connected**

The current-workspace card always shows `Saving to` → `savingToHere` ("Here"). When `active.state === "unavailable"`, the bar beside it says "Not connected · Captures paused" (`notConnectedState`, en.json:2195) and the notice says nothing is saved anywhere else. So the menu shows two statements that contradict each other. Show the paused state (or hide this stat) when `active.state === "unavailable"`, the same way line 149 already dims the tile.

title: Show in Finder is enabled for a disconnected active workspace
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Show in Finder is enabled for a disconnected active workspace**

Settings → Workspaces disables Show folder when `workspace.state === "unavailable"` (settings-pages.tsx:256). This menu shortcut stays enabled for an active workspace that isn't connected, so it tries to open a folder that doesn't exist. Disable it the same way here so both places behave alike.

title: Any Escape anywhere in the window dismisses the one-time hint for good
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Any Escape anywhere in the window dismisses the one-time hint for good**

The keydown listener is on `window` and does not check `event.defaultPrevented` or where the key was pressed. While the hint shows, an Escape that closes an editor dialog, a modal or a select also calls `dismissHint()`, which saves the dismissal for good. While the menu is open, the same Escape also closes the menu along with whatever else handles it. Ignore events that are already handled (`event.defaultPrevented`), or only react when focus is inside the switcher.

title: A refused Remove fails silently
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A refused Remove fails silently**

`remove(id)` resolves to a `WorkspaceRemoveResult` that can be `{ ok: false, reason: "active" | "last" | "unknown" | "read-only" }` (shared/types/workspaces.ts:72-74), but the result is dropped. A race can cause a refusal: for example, the workspace became active through the switcher after the dialog opened. The dialog then closes, the row stays, and nothing explains why. Show a toast for a refusal the way `switchTo`/`add` do in workspaces-context.tsx.

title: Windows users see "This Mac" as the location of workspaces on the internal drive
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Windows users see "This Mac" as the location of workspaces on the internal drive**

`workspaces.thisMac` ("This Mac" / es "Este Mac") is the location label for any workspace without a volume: `useLocationLabel` in `workspace-switcher.tsx:47` returns `workspace.volume ?? t("thisMac")` whatever the host is. The same component already picks a label per host for the folder shortcut (`isWindowsHost() ? t("showInExplorer") : t("showInFinder")` at `workspace-switcher.tsx:172`), so the app ships on Windows and the switcher bar, the menu stats and the row meta (`rowMeta`, `rowNotConnected`, `notConnectedBody` all fill `{location}` from this label) read "This Mac" on a PC. Fix: add a host-neutral or Windows key (e.g. `thisComputer` / "This PC", es "Este equipo") to both catalogs and pick it in `useLocationLabel` the way line 172 does.

title: "leaves a tile empty" only checks that no image is drawn, not that an empty tile is there
body: 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "leaves a tile empty" only checks that no image is drawn, not that an empty tile is there** The test asserts `tiles(late.container)` has length 0, so it only proves that no `` was rendered. It would still pass if the strip dropped the null tiles entirely (other tiles would then shift into the gap), or if it rendered no strip at all. The component renders a placeholder `` for each null tile (webcam-lane.tsx:127). To pin the behaviour the test names, also assert that the strip exists and holds the expected number of placeholder tiles, for example `[data-webcam-filmstrip] span`.

title: "Open" only closes the card, and only the tooltip says so
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: "Open" only closes the card, and only the tooltip says so**

The **Open** button calls `onDismiss`, which does exactly what ✕ does. The page passes `() => setCardDismissedFor(location.key)` (library-detail-page.tsx:253), and the user is already on the recording's page. The only explanation, "Close this and stay on the recording", is in a `title` attribute. Keyboard and screen-reader users don't reliably get `title` tooltips, and the accessible name stays "Open", which suggests the button opens something. Consider a label that matches what the button does, such as "Keep it here" or "Stay on the recording". Alternatively, drop the button, since ✕ already covers this.

title: The rail badge still counts copies that were deleted
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: The rail badge still counts copies that were deleted**

`libraryBadgeCount` (`ready-copies.ts:74`) counts every unannounced entry in the store. The Library page, though, only counts copies that are still in `videos` (`library-page.tsx:62`). Say a copy finishes and the user deletes it before opening the Library, for example from its detail page through another path. The rail then shows "1 new copy ready", and the Library page shows no chip and no outlined card for it. The entry also stays in the store until the app relaunches, because nothing calls `markCopySeen` for a deleted asset. One fix: call `markCopySeen(assetId)` from the Library's delete path. Another: filter the badge count by the assets that still exist.

title: "Drag to upload" can get keyboard focus but does nothing when pressed
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: "Drag to upload" can get keyboard focus but does nothing when pressed**

The old drag chip had `tabIndex={-1}`. It now renders through `StatusCardButton` as a real `<button>` with no `onClick`. Keyboard users can Tab to it, and Enter or Space does nothing, because the only thing it does is a mouse drag. One option: keep it out of the tab order. Another: give it a keyboard fallback, such as revealing the file.

title: The verify test's name still says the old "Ready to share" card
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The verify test's name still says the old "Ready to share" card**

The comment on line 5 and the locators on lines 24–26 now look for the "Your export is ready" card. The test is still called `"export: editor to the Ready to share card"`, which names a card that no longer exists.

title: Spanish drag label switched from infinitive to imperative
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Spanish drag label switched from infinitive to imperative**

The removed `readyDragLabel` read "Arrastrar {name} fuera de Kaipu". The new `backgroundCopy.readyDragLabel` reads "Arrastra {name} fuera de Kaipu". The other action labels in this block use the infinitive: "Abrir {name} en tu Biblioteca" and "Arrastrar para subir". If the change wasn't intended, keep "Arrastrar" so the aria-labels match.

title: Effort "Small" is not on the table's scale
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Effort "Small" is not on the table's scale**

Every other row in the Effort column uses Low / Medium / High / Large (or Low–Medium, Varies, —). The new row says "Small". Use "Low" to stay on the same scale.

title: "keeps the copy untagged" passes only because the earlier render is still mounted
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "keeps the copy untagged" passes only because the earlier render is still mounted**

`renderDetail("gh")` runs while the `renderDetail("src")` tree from line 443 is still in the DOM. The assertion `getAllByText("Master · full quality")).toHaveLength(1)` only holds because the `src` player contributes exactly one tag and the `gh` page contributes none. If the master tag is ever dropped from the src page, or the src render shows it twice, this test fails or passes for reasons unrelated to the copy. Suggested fix: call `cleanup()` (or unmount) before the second render and assert `queryByText("Master · full quality")` is null. Alternatively, move the copy case into its own `it`.

title: pointer-events: none hides the master tag's tooltip on the player
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: pointer-events: none hides the master tag's tooltip on the player**

`.masterTag` sets `pointer-events: none` so clicks reach the video. `pointer-events` is inherited, so the `MasterTag` inside it (library-detail-page.tsx:264-266) gets no hover either. That means its `title={t("masterTagHint")}` (master-tag.tsx:13) never shows on the recording page, which is where the tag is largest. On the Library card and row it still works. If the hint matters here, one option is `pointer-events: auto` on the tag itself. It sits in the corner, clear of the video's controls bar, so it would only block clicks on its own small area. The other option is to accept that the hint doesn't show on this page.

title: role="img" hides the size bar's '% lighter' and GitHub-limit text from screen readers
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: role="img" hides the size bar's '% lighter' and GitHub-limit text from screen readers**

The size bar section has `role="img"`. With that role its children are presentational, so assistive tech reads only the `aria-label`. That label is `meterLabel` ("Your recording {from}, the copy {to}", en.json:824). The visible text in `parts` (lines 326-333), "{percent}% lighter" / "Not lighter" and "under the 10 MB limit" / "over GitHub's 10 MB free-plan limit", is never announced. For GitHub, whether the file fits the 10 MB free-plan limit is the one fact this card exists to give, and screen-reader users don't get it. Put `role="img"` and the label on the decorative bar only (line 352, which is currently `aria-hidden`) and leave the text labels readable, or add `parts.join(", ")` to the aria-label.

title: Radio groups have no arrow-key navigation or roving tabindex
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Radio groups have no arrow-key navigation or roving tabindex**

The destination rows here, and the 1440p/4K and Fill/Fit segments in destination-detail.tsx (lines 259-275 and 391-405), use `role="radiogroup"`/`role="radio"` on plain buttons. Every radio is a separate Tab stop, and arrow keys do nothing. Screen readers announce these as radio groups, and users expect the WAI-ARIA radio pattern: one Tab stop, with arrows moving the selection. `isPrimaryEnter` in prepare-page.tsx:272 already treats these buttons as radios for Enter, so you could add arrow-key handling with `tabIndex={selected === d ? 0 : -1}`. The other option is to drop the radio roles and use `aria-pressed`/`aria-current`.

title: The "does not re-select" check passes even without preventDefault
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The "does not re-select" check passes even without preventDefault**

In jsdom, `fireEvent.keyDown(youtube, { key: "Enter" })` only sends a keydown event. jsdom never fires the click that a real browser fires on Enter over a `<button>`. So `aria-checked` stays "false" whether or not `prepare-page.tsx:215` calls `event.preventDefault()`, and this test would still pass if that line were removed. To test the behaviour, assert on the event itself: `fireEvent.keyDown` returns `false` when the default was prevented, so `expect(fireEvent.keyDown(youtube, { key: "Enter" })).toBe(false)` would do it. Otherwise, reword the test name so it doesn't claim the row isn't re-selected.

title: Enter listener on the whole document reacts to elements outside the page and to non-native controls
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Enter listener on the whole document reacts to elements outside the page and to non-native controls**

The listener sits on `document`, so it sees every Enter in the window, not just Enter pressed inside the Prepare screen. `isPrimaryEnter` (line 263) only skips form fields, links and `<button>` elements, so Enter on other focusable controls still starts a copy. In this repo those include `div role="button"` (`export-status-cards.tsx:179`, `video-card.tsx:56`), `role="tab"` and `role="option"`. There is also an ordering problem: `onboarding-overlay.tsx:62-74` handles Enter in a `window` listener, and an event bubbling up reaches `document` before `window`. If onboarding is open over this page (it opens on first launch, and Settings can replay it) and focus is not on its Continue button, one Enter would both advance onboarding and start an encode. One option is to only act when the event target is inside the screen root, or is `document.body`.

title: New key `prepare.sizeBarTitle` is never used
body:
🟠🧹 **Fix · cleanup: New key `prepare.sizeBarTitle` is never used**

`sizeBarTitle` ("Your recording and the copy, on one scale") is new in this PR, but nothing under `apps/kaipu-record/src` reads it. `SizeBarCard` (`destination-detail.tsx:313-359`) has no visible title and labels itself with `meterLabel` instead. Every other key this PR adds is used by `destination-list.tsx` or `destination-detail.tsx`. The doc's note about keeping old keys for now (`prepare-screen.md:131-132`) covers the dropped keys, not new ones. Either show it as the card's kicker, like the other cards' `h2`, or remove it from `en.json` and `es.json` (line 780 in both).

title: Files dropped while an import is running are silently discarded
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Files dropped while an import is running are silently discarded**

The `importing` doc comment (line 36) says "a second one waits for it", but `run` returns at once when `busy.current` is set (line 78), and it shows no toast. `useFileDrop` keeps the whole window as a drop target during an import (`use-file-drop.ts:40-46`). `importDropped` also skips the `busy` check until it reaches `run` (line 112). So if a user drops more videos while a large file is still copying, those videos are never imported, and the user gets no message. The only exception is the "ignored" toast for files that aren't videos. Fix this by queueing the second call so it runs after the current one (what the comment promises), or by showing a toast such as "an import is already running" when it is refused. Then update the comment to match.

title: A finished import navigates to Prepare even after the user has left Prepare
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A finished import navigates to Prepare even after the user has left Prepare**

`onImported` always runs `relist().then(() => navigate(preparePath(...)))`. Nothing checks whether Prepare is still mounted when the import resolves. `useImportVideos.run` (use-import-videos.ts:82-83) awaits the IPC and then calls `report` → `onImported` with no mounted guard. The Back button stays enabled during an import (destination-list.tsx:62; only the footer is `disabled={importing}`), and so does "From your Library" (prepare-drop-zone.tsx:39).

So here is the failure: you drop a large video on Prepare, click "Back to recording" or "From your Library" while the copy runs, and when the copy finishes the app takes you back to `/prepare/<new>`. The data router's `navigate` still works after the component unmounts.

You could drop the navigation once the hook unmounts, for example with a mounted ref cleared in a `useEffect` cleanup. In that case the Library's usual "is in your Library" toast would fit better. Or disable Back while `importing` is true.

title: Centered flex container with overflow-y: auto can clip the top of the zone
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Centered flex container with overflow-y: auto can clip the top of the zone**

`.wrap` sets `align-items: center` and `overflow-y: auto` (lines 6 and 9). When `.zone` is taller than the column (short window, large font size, or long Spanish copy wrapping), the flex item overflows equally above and below. The part above the scroll origin can't be reached by scrolling, so the icon and title get cut off. One fix is `align-items: safe center`. Another is to drop `align-items` and give `.zone` `margin: auto`: auto margins fall back to 0 on overflow, so the content stays reachable.

title: Limit says drops on other pages still navigate, but Prepare now handles drops
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Limit says drops on other pages still navigate, but Prepare now handles drops**

This PR also adds `usePrepareImport` (`features/prepare/use-prepare-import.ts:55`), which calls `useFileDrop` while Prepare is mounted, and `prepare-page.tsx:81` uses it. So it is no longer true that a drop on any page other than the Library falls through to Electron's default. Change the limit to say that drops are caught on the Library and Prepare, and that every other page still navigates. You could also link to [prepare-drop-zone](./prepare-drop-zone).

title: Prepare drop body lists only MP4 or MOV
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Prepare drop body lists only MP4 or MOV**

`prepare.dropBody` says "MP4 or MOV from anywhere". The import accepts `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.m4v` and `.webm` (`src/shared/import-video.ts:12`), and the Library strings (`importReasonUnsupported`, `importDropIgnored`) list all four. A user who has a WebM may think Prepare won't take it. Consider listing the same four formats here. The same applies to es.json line 907.

title: The copyright holder (Cristian Sotomayor) is not the party the CLA licenses (Niway S.A.C.)
body:
🟡❓ **Consider · question: The copyright holder (Cristian Sotomayor) is not the party the CLA licenses (Niway S.A.C.)**

The README names Cristian Sotomayor as the copyright holder, with Niway S.A.C. as publisher. CLA.md, though, grants the relicensing rights to Niway (CLA.md:5, §2), and open-source.md says the CLA keeps "one owner". If the existing code belongs to a person and the contributions are licensed to a company, the relicensing rights sit with two parties. Is there an assignment or license from the author to Niway that makes Niway the single owner? If so, could the README or CLA say so? If not, should the CLA name the actual copyright holder?

title: A second Fix all call clears the cancel handle of the run that is already waiting
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A second Fix all call clears the cancel handle of the run that is already waiting**

The handler sets `reconcileWait = wait` (line 163) before it knows whether this call will get into maintenance mode. Suppose a second `library:reconcile-fix` arrives while the first run is still waiting for the vault to go idle, from another window or a double trigger (the reconcile store guards only within one renderer). `enterMaintenance` rejects it straight away with `MaintenanceAlreadyRunningError` (vault-activity.ts:136-137). Its `finally` then finds `reconcileWait === wait`, because this call overwrote it, and sets it to `null` (line 173). After that, `library:reconcile-cancel` (line 177) has no controller to abort. The first run's dialog shows "waiting" but can no longer be cancelled, and it keeps waiting until the vault goes idle or a recording or export starts.

Fix: only claim the slot when it is free, e.g. `if (reconcileWait) return { status: "already-running" }` before creating the controller. Another option is to keep the previous controller and abort through a set of controllers.

title: A source whose removal check fails is neither removed nor set aside in "set-aside" mode
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A source whose removal check fails is neither removed nor set aside in "set-aside" mode**

`removeSource` returns `"unknown"` when `lstat` of the placed source fails (line 302–305). With `stuck: "rollback"` that case throws (line 277). With `stuck: "set-aside"`, the mode used for staging files, nothing happens: `setAside` runs only from the `catch` at line 269, and line 286 only syncs on `"removed"`. So the bytes end up at `to`, and the staging source keeps a name the stranded sweep still matches. The doc comment of `StuckSource` says such a source is set aside "or marked placed" so it is not swept up as a second recording. If the read error goes away later (a network share comes back, for example), the next sweep can recover the same take a second time. Consider calling `setAside(from, sourceId, to, placed.size)` for `"unknown"` when `stuck !== "rollback"`. Even if the rename fails, it falls back to the marker.

title: onWaiting fires on every release, not only when the set of kinds changes
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: onWaiting fires on every release, not only when the set of kinds changes**

The comment says `onWaiting` gets the kinds still in flight "each time that set changes while waiting". But `settle()` (line 178-180) calls `entering.onWaiting?.(this.active())` on every release while `count > 0`. Example: two `library` leases are held and one is released. The set is still `["library"]`, and the callback fires anyway. Either fix the comment ("each time a lease is released while waiting") or keep the last reported set and skip the call when it hasn't changed. Skipping would avoid sending the renderer progress events that repeat the same set.

title: Screenshot overwrite test accepts any Error, so it doesn't prove the item was found and then refused
body:
🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: Screenshot overwrite test accepts any Error, so it doesn't prove the item was found and then refused**

The comment on line 105 says "the item is found and still refused", but the test only checks `toBeInstanceOf(Error)`. `overwriteImage` (library-vault.ts:1196-1199) also throws a plain `Error` when `expectedAssetId` is missing, and an `ItemGoneError` when `resolveIdentity` doesn't match the identity. If identity resolution broke for this sidecar (valid `assetId`, invalid `title`), the test would still pass because of the `ItemGoneError`, even though the refusal path never ran. Assert `toBeInstanceOf(UnreadableRecordError)` instead, as the test above does at line 95. You could also check that the message contains `UNREADABLE_RECORD_MARKER`.

title: EACCES case isn't skipped when running as root or on Windows
body:
🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: EACCES case isn't skipped when running as root or on Windows**

The `unreadable (EACCES)` case relies on `chmod(manifestPath, 0o000)` to make the manifest unreadable. When the tests run as root (common in CI containers), or on Windows, the file stays readable. The test then reads it as a valid pending manifest (`pendingManifest()`), so the scan never reports `unreadable-orphan-run` and the assertion at line 395 fails.

Other tests that use chmod in this PR guard against this: `vault-reconcile.scan.test.ts:10`, `library-vault.unreadable.test.ts:8` and `library-vault.rename.test.ts:113` each define `const canChmod = process.platform !== "win32" && process.getuid?.() !== 0;`, and `library-vault.test.ts:405` uses `it.skipIf(...)`. This case should be skipped the same way.

There is another option, because this file already mocks `node:fs/promises`: inject the error with `faults.fail = (op, p) => op === "readFile" && p === manifestPath`, changing the injected code to EACCES. That would make the case independent of the platform.

title: Fixture comment says a 6-item chain, but the loop builds 5
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Fixture comment says a 6-item chain, but the loop builds 5**

The comment reads "A 6-item chain: titles B…F over files A…E, F free", but the loop at line 97 only creates the five items A–E, and their titles are B–F. Also, the comment sits above the X/Y cycle entries instead of above the loop that builds the chain. Change it to "5-item chain" and move it to line 97 so it matches the fixture.

title: Header comment points to review history instead of what the test covers
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Header comment points to review history instead of what the test covers**

"Fifth review of NIW2-561:" ties the file to a review round that readers can't look up from the code, and it stops meaning anything once the PR merges. The rest of the sentence already lists the three scenarios. Dropping the prefix would match the headers of the sibling files (`no-hard-link`, `move-failure`).

title: Test title doesn't parse
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Test title doesn't parse**

"a reload %s finalize reserves its destination waits for it" puts two verbs back to back, so it's hard to tell when the reload happens. Something like "a reload %s finalize reserves its destination: the vault stays busy until finalize settles and nothing is overwritten" would say it clearly in the failure output.

title: autosaveEdits' JSDoc now sits on the maintenance-retry effect
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: autosaveEdits' JSDoc now sits on the maintenance-retry effect**

The new `persistRef` / `onLibraryMaintenanceEnded` block (lines 463–474) was inserted between the JSDoc at lines 457–462 ("Write the current edits over the vault item, quietly…") and `autosaveEdits` at line 476, which that JSDoc describes. Editors and tooling now attach that doc to `persistRef` instead. Moving the new block above the JSDoc (for example, right after the `persist` definition) puts the comment back next to the function it describes.

title: English plural for reconcileKept mixes "their" and "its"
body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: English plural for reconcileKept mixes "their" and "its"**

The `other` branch says "# items kept their names for now (open in the editor, locked by another app, or its new name just taken)". With a plural subject this should be "their new name just taken" (or "their new names"), not "its". The `one` branch is correct as written. The Spanish string already agrees in both branches.

title: Third-party action on a mutable `@v0` tag gets every provider API key
body:
🟡🔐 **Consider · security: Third-party action on a mutable `@v0` tag gets every provider API key**

`pullfrog/pullfrog@v0` is a third-party action referenced by a tag that can be moved. Lines 35–48 hand it up to 14 provider secrets (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, OpenRouter and others), plus an `id-token: write` OIDC token (line 21). If someone retags `v0` upstream or the account is compromised, the next dispatch sends all of these keys to that new code.

The other workflows also use tags, but mostly for first-party or well-known actions like `actions/*` and `oven-sh/setup-bun`. None of them passes a secret set this broad to a vendor's runner code.

Two changes would shrink the exposure:
- Pin to a full commit SHA, e.g. `pullfrog/pullfrog@<sha> # v0.x.y`, and let Dependabot or Renovate bump it.
- Keep only the env line for the provider you actually configure and delete the rest. An unset secret expands to an empty string, but any key added to the repo later would quietly flow to this action.

The rest of the setup is sound: `workflow_dispatch`-only, `contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false`, and `inputs.prompt` goes through `with:` rather than a `run:` shell, so it can't be used for shell injection.

title: When the camera can't reopen, the face goes into the same parked window, not a new one
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: When the camera can't reopen, the face goes into the same parked window, not a new one**

Say the camera is turned on again mid-take. The hub sees `takeRecordsWebcam()` still true and calls `show()` on the parked window. That window is protected and left out of the running capture (recording-hub.ts:304-305). If `turnWebcamOn` then returns "unavailable", the engine ends the file and main only runs `bubbleProtection.webcamEnded` + `applyProtection()` (recording-hub.ts:456-459). Main's own docs call that best effort: it is unverified whether a running ScreenCaptureKit stream picks up a window that drops its protection (camera-bubble-window.ts:140-144).

The hub handles the parked case differently. When the file ends while the window is parked, it destroys the window and creates a new one (line 304), because a new unprotected window is "the one a running capture is known to record". The reopen-failure path, which this PR adds, gets no such replacement. The face can then be missing from both the webcam file and the screen. Meanwhile this comment says "main put the bubble back in the capture", and `webcamReopenFailed` sets `webcamUnavailable`, which tells the user the face is in the screen.

You could have the `recordingWebcamEnded` handler recreate a visible bubble during a take the same way. Or reword this comment and the user message so they don't promise the face is in the screen.

title: Comment says a following off waits on the queue, but off runs synchronously
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Comment says a following off waits on the queue, but off runs synchronously**

The comment reads "On the queue, so an off that follows waits for this camera to open and releases it". But the off branch (lines 924-934) calls `handle.turnWebcamOff()` synchronously, outside `queue`. What actually releases a camera that was opened late is the engine's `cameraRequest` counter (recorder-engine.ts:790-793 and 810). The behavior is correct; only the explanation is wrong. Suggest rewording it: the on is queued after earlier mic changes, and an off that comes while the camera is still opening supersedes it through the engine's request counter.

title: Test name says it covers the hub reset, but only abort is tested
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Test name says it covers the hub reset, but only abort is tested**

"a bubble parked when the take is aborted or the hub reset is destroyed too" only calls `recordingAbort`. The reset path (`releaseParkedBubble()` after `bubbleProtection.reset()`, recording-hub.ts:1022) and the stop path (`applyStopWindowState`, line 846) have no test. Either add those cases or rename the test to cover abort only.

title: The "dropped (and closed)" path for a cut camera's late frame never runs
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The "dropped (and closed)" path for a cut camera's late frame never runs**

The comment says a frame the old camera still delivers after `cut()` is "dropped (and closed), not relayed". In practice `cut()` cancels the reader (`webcam-relay.ts:69`), so `first.push(late)` throws inside the `try` and the frame never reaches the pump. That means the `current !== reader` branch that calls `value.close()` (`webcam-relay.ts:91-93`) is not exercised, and nothing checks `late.close`.

The `written` assertion passes either way. To cover the branch, have a frame already queued before the cut so it is read after `current` changes, for example by pushing it before calling `relay.cut()` without flushing. Then assert `expect(late.close).toHaveBeenCalled()`. If you'd rather not, change the comment so it doesn't claim a close the test never checks.

title: `crypto.randomUUID()` makes the seeded layer different on every call, and Share's fingerprint hashes that layer, ids included: `wholeFingerprint(scene.webcam)`…
body:
`crypto.randomUUID()` makes the seeded layer different on every call, and Share's fingerprint hashes that layer, ids included: `wholeFingerprint(scene.webcam)` → `stableStringify(webcam)` in `export-reuse.ts:81`. Each time `ShareRecording` mounts it gets a new `whole:<hash>`, so `findReusableExports` never finds the earlier Share file and re-encodes the take whenever it has a gap. Takes without gaps are not affected, because they seed `segments: []`. The PR body says the fingerprint is "covered automatically", but that only holds if seeding is deterministic. The ids only need to be unique within the scene, and `validateWebcamSegment` accepts any string, so ids derived from the gap are enough.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Seeded gap segments must have deterministic ids

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/webcam/webcam-model.ts:155 — `id: crypto.randomUUID()` in `gapSegments`
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/library/components/share-recording.tsx:126-130 — `initialScene(...)` → `wholeFingerprint(scene.webcam)` → reuse lookup at :183
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/video-editor/scene.ts:153 — `reconcileWebcam` seeds again for sessions that have no saved webcam layer; the editor's post-export stamp check (`video-editor-page.tsx:712`) compares `editFingerprint` against that reseeded scene

## Required outcome
- `seedWebcamScene` returns the same ids for the same sidecar, so `wholeFingerprint` is stable across Share mounts and the reuse lookup matches.
- Add a test: seeding the same `WebcamTrackMeta` twice gives equal `wholeFingerprint` values.

## Suggested approach
- e.g. `id: `gap-${segments.length}`` (or derive from `gap.startMs`). User-created segments use UUIDs, so these cannot collide.
````

</details>

```suggestion
    segments.push({ id: `gap-${segments.length}`, start, end, mode: "hidden" });
```

title: Nothing re-checks whether the camera was turned off again before this queued on reaches the engine, and an off is not queued.
body:
Nothing re-checks whether the camera was turned off again before this queued on reaches the engine, and an off is not queued. Take off → on1 (still opening) → off → on2 (queued behind on1) → off. The last off reaches the engine while on1 is still opening, and on2 runs after that. The engine's `cameraWanted` is `false` at that point, so `turnWebcamOn()` opens the camera and feeds the file. The light stays on while the Camera toggle shows off, until the take stops or the camera is turned on again. The gap stays open, so the editor hides those frames, but the user's "off" was not honoured. The comment above says the engine drops a camera that is turned off while it opens, but an on still waiting in the store's queue never reached the engine, so it cannot be dropped.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# A queued turn-on must not reach the engine after a newer off

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:943-944 — the queued closure calls `handle.turnWebcamOn()` without checking `webcamOn` / `request`
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:829-833 — `turnWebcamOn` treats `cameraWanted === false` as "open it", which is correct for its own contract

## Required outcome
- An on whose request is no longer the newest, or that runs after the camera was turned off again, does not call the engine. The engine already has the newer state: off was applied directly, and a newer on is queued behind this one.
- Add a store test: `onOffOnWhileOpening()` followed by `broadcast({ isCameraEnabled: false })` before `answers[0]` resolves. Expect `turnWebcamOn` to be called only once, and the gap to stay open until the stop.
````

</details>

```suggestion
      queue = queue.then(async () => {
        // Turned off again, or on again by a newer on, before this one reached the engine: the
        // engine already has the newer state, and opening the camera would light it.
        if (!webcamOn || request !== webcamOnRequest) return;
        const result = await handle.turnWebcamOn();
```

title: Ready cards can be retired before anyone has seen them (list view, filtered out)
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Ready cards can be retired before anyone has seen them (list view, filtered out)**

`leading` only renders in the grid branch (line 409), and only for copies that pass the current filters (line 129). Leaving the Library still calls `retireReadyCards()` for every copy with `card: true` (sidebar.tsx:102). So if the Library is in list view, or a filter hides the copy, the user never sees its "Ready to upload" card, and it is gone the next time they come back. The comment on `retireReadyCards` (ready-copies.ts:93–96) says "every card it showed has been seen", and that isn't true in these cases. You could retire only the cards that were actually rendered, or show the leading cards in list view as well.

title: The `aria-label` here hides what the pill says.
body:
The `aria-label` here hides what the pill says. A `button`'s children are presentational in ARIA, so the inner `role="progressbar"` and the visible "YouTube copy · 38%" are dropped, and a screen reader announces only "Show the export's progress, button". The accessible name also no longer contains the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3), so a voice command like "click YouTube copy" won't find it.

One fix: drop the `aria-label` and the inner `role`/`aria-value*`, and let the visible text be the name. Another: put the percent into the label, e.g. `t("pill", …)` plus the expand hint.

title: Show in Finder and the drag in this card don't call `markCopySeen`, but the same two actions in the ready toast do (they count as "acted on it").
body: Show in Finder and the drag in this card don't call `markCopySeen`, but the same two actions in the ready toast do (they count as "acted on it"). So if the user drags the copy from this card into YouTube Studio and then leaves the Library, the copy comes back as "unseen": it keeps the pink `justReady` outline, the "1 copy ready" chip and the badge logic, even though it has already been uploaded. Either match the toast, or note when a card's copy was acted on and drop it from the unseen set when `retireReadyCards` runs. Marking it seen right away would also remove the card mid-interaction, since `markCopySeen` drops the whole entry.

title: An Email copy is tagged "For email" only while its `ReadyCopy` entry still holds the job's destination.
body:
An Email copy is tagged "For email" only while its `ReadyCopy` entry still holds the job's destination. When the user opens the copy, `markCopySeen` drops that entry. After that, or after a relaunch (the store lives only in memory), the tag falls back to the sidecar. The sidecar reads `balanced` → `destinationOfPreset` → `chat`, so the same file now says "For chat". Email and chat share a preset, so the sidecar can't tell them apart.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Email copy's tag changes from "For email" to "For chat"

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library/library-page.tsx:399: `copyDestinationOf(video, readyInfo.get(...)?.destination)` gets `email` only while the copy is still in the ready store
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/prepare/copy-destination.ts:29: the fallback `destinationOfPreset("balanced")` returns `chat` (by design, see `destinations.ts:11-13`)

## Required outcome
- A copy keeps the same tag (and the same `MasterCopiesPanel` name) after it is opened or the app relaunches.

## Suggested approach (optional)
- Write the destination into the export sidecar next to `preset`/`fingerprint`, and have `copyDestinationOf` prefer it over the preset lookup. Or, if that is out of scope here, show `balanced` copies from the sidecar with a tag that does not claim chat.
````

</details>

title: "shows only where…" never checks the button is absent
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "shows only where…" never checks the button is absent**

The test name says Open in Export → appears *only* where there is an export screen, but it only renders with `onOpenExport` and clicks the button. It never renders without the prop to check the button is missing, and that missing case is the one `library-detail-page.tsx:513` relies on for a non-preparable copy. Add `renderPanel([copy({})])` followed by `expect(within(panel).queryByRole("button", { name: "Open in Export →" })).toBeNull()`.

title: Overwrites the shared electronAPI stub without restoring it
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: Overwrites the shared electronAPI stub without restoring it**

`window.electronAPI.startFileDrag = startFileDrag` replaces the stub that `test/setup.ts:109` builds once for each file, and nothing puts it back. Every later test in this file then runs against the mock. `export-status-cards.test.tsx:143-152` handles the same API with `vi.spyOn(window.electronAPI, "startFileDrag")` and `mockRestore()`. Use that pattern here too.

body:
Since the `feature/export-screen` merge, this note is wrong: `DESTINATION_IDS` now includes `email`, and the panel renders seven cards (the page test asserts `toHaveLength(7)`). Line 100 has the same problem: it says a card "opens Prepare", but `preparePath` now goes to `/export`. The PR description's "Six destinations, not seven" note is stale for the same reason.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Stale destination count and screen name after the export-screen merge

## Affected sites
- apps/documentation/src/content/docs/backlog/prepare-screen.md:114-116 — says the code has six destinations; it has seven (`destinations.ts` adds `email`)
- apps/documentation/src/content/docs/backlog/prepare-screen.md:100 — "A card opens Prepare on that destination"; `preparePath` now builds `/export/:assetId`
- PR #465 description, "Six destinations, not seven" bullet

## Required outcome
- The doc and the PR body describe seven destinations (Email as its own card over the Balanced preset, as `export-screen.md` explains) and say that the cards open Export.
````
