title: `show()` returns true before the card can paint, so a renderer that never loads loses the card
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: `show()` returns true before the card can paint, so a renderer that never loads loses the card**

`show()` returns true as soon as `ensureWindow()` creates the BrowserWindow (line 146). The window only appears later, in `present()`, once the card sends `recording-ready:card-ready`. `load()` throws away the `loadURL`/`loadFile` promise (lines 261/265), and nothing watches `did-fail-load` or `render-process-gone`. So if the bundle fails to load or the card renderer crashes, `useFloatingReadyCard` has already received `true` and never turns on `inApp`. The user sees no card at all, which contradicts the hook's comment that the card is "never lost".

The same gap exists after a renderer crash on a window that already exists. `rendererReady` stays true, so `present()` sends to a dead renderer and still calls `showInactive()` on a blank transparent window.

One option: resolve the invoke only after `card-ready`, or after a short timeout, and answer false on a load failure. Another: reset `rendererReady` and drop the window on `render-process-gone`.

title: `recording-ready:show` accepts any renderer, unlike the card channels
body:
🟡🔐 **Consider · security: `recording-ready:show` accepts any renderer, unlike the card channels**

The three card channels check `isOwnSender` (lines 109, 114, 123). The `recording-ready:show` handler does not check who sent it. Any window that loads the shared preload can invoke `showRecordingReady` and float an always-on-top card with an arbitrary `assetId`: the card window itself, the capture toast, the overlay, the panels. Pressing that card then makes the main window navigate to that id.

The payload is validated and `generatePath` encodes the id, so the impact is small. Still, it widens what non-main windows can do across the bridge. Checking that `event.sender` is the main window's `webContents` would keep the channel to the caller the docs describe ("Main window → main").

title: The floating card comes back after the user has already answered it.
body:
The floating card comes back after the user has already answered it. After TikTok, More places or Edit first, the main window pushes Prepare or the editor, and `LibraryDetailPage` unmounts. When the user presses Back, the page remounts on the same history entry, with the same `location.key` and `fromRecording` state. This ref starts empty again, so main is asked a second time and the always-on-top card pops up on the desktop again. The in-app card already reappeared on Back before this PR, but a floating window over every app is much more intrusive. It also goes against this hook's "once per arrival" docstring.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Floating card re-asks on remount of the same history entry

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording-ready/use-floating-ready-card.ts:18 — `asked` is per component instance, so it resets on remount
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library-detail/library-detail-page.tsx:141 — passes `location.key`, which stays the same on Back/Forward to the same entry

## Required outcome
- A given history entry (`location.key`) asks main to show the floating card at most once for the renderer's lifetime, even when `LibraryDetailPage` unmounts and remounts (Prepare → Back, editor → Back).

## Suggested approach (optional)
- Keep the keys that were already asked in a module-level `Set<string>`, not a `useRef`. That also covers StrictMode's second effect run, which is what the ref is for today.
````

</details>

title: The 16 DIP padding does not leave room for the card's shadow.
body: The 16 DIP padding does not leave room for the card's shadow. `StatusCard`'s shadow is `0 30px 80px -30px`, so it reaches about 40px below the card, and the window cuts it off with a hard edge at 16px, at roughly 25–30% opacity. That edge will show on light backgrounds. You could give the window more room below the card (the window height and the body padding in `main.css`), or use a smaller shadow for the floating variant. Either way, this comment is inaccurate right now.

title: "Pick from Library" stays enabled while a dropped file is importing
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: "Pick from Library" stays enabled while a dropped file is importing**

"Browse files" is disabled while `importing` is true (line 51), but the `VideoPicker` trigger is not. If the user picks a Library video during an import, `openVideo` sends them to that video. Then the import finishes, and `usePrepareImport` sends them to the imported one. One navigation overwrites the other. You could pass `disabled={importing}` to the trigger `Button` here too, so both ways in act the same.

title: GitHub size bar's accessible label leaves out the 10 MB limit it is drawn against
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: GitHub size bar's accessible label leaves out the 10 MB limit it is drawn against**

For GitHub, `scale` is `max(copyBytes, GITHUB_FREE_LIMIT_BYTES)` (line 297), so the bar shows the copy measured against the 10 MB free limit, and the visible tag says "fits" or "over" that limit. But the section is `role="img"` with `aria-label={t("barLabel", { from, to })}`, which en.json:925 renders as "Your recording {from}, the copy {to}". Because `role="img"` hides the children, screen-reader users never get the fits/over verdict. Consider adding the `tag` text to the label, or a separate label for the limited case.

title: Picker is a `role="dialog"` but focus stays on the trigger and isn't restored on Escape
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Picker is a `role="dialog"` but focus stays on the trigger and isn't restored on Escape**

When the panel opens, focus stays on the trigger. Escape (line 51) and a click outside close the panel without moving focus anywhere. A keyboard user has to Tab into the list, and assistive tech announces a dialog that never took focus. Consider moving focus to the first (or `aria-current`) item when the panel opens and back to the trigger on Escape. Another option is to drop `role="dialog"` and treat the panel as a disclosure list.

title: The in-progress row puts the video title in the slot where finished rows show the destination name
body:
🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: The in-progress row puts the video title in the slot where finished rows show the destination name**

The running row puts `running.sourceTitle` in `styles.name` and the percentage in `meta`. Finished rows (lines 71–73) put the destination name (`t(EXPORT_NAME[destination])`) in `name` and size · title in `meta`. In the same three-row strip, the bold line therefore means two different things. Consider showing the destination name in `name` for the running row as well, with the title next to the percentage.

title: "does not take a video dropped on the window" would pass even if Library still handled drops
body:
🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: "does not take a video dropped on the window" would pass even if Library still handled drops**

This test now runs on the default stub `pathForFile: () => ""` from `src/test/setup.ts:156`. The test that used to override it (`/Users/me/Movies/...`) was removed in this PR. In `use-import-videos.ts:102-111`, a file whose path comes back empty is moved to `skipped` and the function returns before it calls `importVideoFiles`. So if `LibraryPage` still mounted `useFileDrop` and the drop import, `importVideoFiles` would still never be called, and the test would still pass. It also asserts right after `fireEvent.drop`, before the async import could resolve.

To make it test the claim, stub `window.electronAPI.pathForFile = vi.fn((f: File) => `/Users/me/Movies/${f.name}`)`. Then, more directly, assert that nothing intercepted the drop: `expect(fireEvent.drop(document.body, …)).toBe(true)`, since `useFileDrop` calls `preventDefault` on drop (`use-file-drop.ts:42`). You could also assert that `getToasts()` is empty.

title: "with and without a video" only renders the with-video URL
body:
🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: "with and without a video" only renders the with-video URL**

The test is named "is active on Export with and without a video", but it only renders `/export/asset-1`. It never checks `/export` (`ROUTES.exportNew`). The rail item's `to` is `ROUTES.exportNew` (sidebar.tsx:53), and `isActive` matches it with `end: false`. So the bare `/export` case is the main one, and nothing asserts it. Render `ROUTES.exportNew` as well and check `aria-current="page"` there too.

title: The badge's "in progress" count is not tested
body:
🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: The badge's "in progress" count is not tested**

`useExportBadge` (sidebar.tsx:121-122) now adds 1 while `useExportRunner().status === "exporting"`. That is why the label changed to "copy in progress or ready". These tests only use `noteFinishedCopy`, so the running part of the count and the label it produces are never checked. You could add a case that puts the export runner in the `exporting` state and asserts that the badge counts it.

title: Orphaned comment for the removed import drop strip
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Orphaned comment for the removed import drop strip**

The `.importZone` rule was removed, but its comment `/* NIW2-579: the "Drop a video here" strip, between the header and the toolbar. */` is still there. It now sits right above the `.stickyBar` comment, so it reads as if it describes the sticky bar. The Library no longer has a drop strip, so delete line 108.

title: This page never re-reads the Library when a background export finishes.
body:
This page never re-reads the Library when a background export finishes. Main sends no `library:changed` when `recordingFinalize` saves the copy, so only an explicit `refresh()` brings it into `videos`. `library-detail-page.tsx` does that when `runner.ready` changes; this page doesn't. Prepare left the screen once an export started (`onStarted={() => navigate(recordingPath)}`), so it didn't matter there. Export now stays, so after the copy lands:

- the card never reads "Ready";
- the primary button still says "Export for …" instead of "Open the copy you have";
- Enter encodes the same copy again;
- on `/export`, "Recent exports" drops the running row and doesn't show the finished copy until you navigate away and back.

The existing tests seed the finished copy before mount, so they don't catch this.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Export screen does not see a copy that finishes while it is open

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/export/export-page.tsx:70 — `useLocalLibrary()` is never refreshed when `useExportRunner().ready` changes, so `lineage.exportsOf`, `reusable`, `existing` and `RecentExports` stay stale.
- apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/export/export-page.tsx:117 — `if (isLoading) return …` unmounts `ExportScreen` during any `refresh()`. It remounts with `initialDestination={urlDestination}`, so the destination picked on screen, the 1440p / 4K choice and Fill / Fit are lost. The cloud-catalog refresh on mount already triggers this today. A refresh added on `ready` would trigger it right after every export.
- Reference: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/pages/library-detail/library-detail-page.tsx:136-140 already refreshes on `runner.ready?.recording.id`.

## Required outcome
- While Export is open, a copy that finishes makes its card read "Ready", makes the primary action open it, and stops Enter from encoding it again.
- "Recent exports" on `/export` lists the copy once it finishes.
- A Library re-list does not reset the screen's selected destination or options.

## Suggested approach
- In `ExportPage`, refresh when `useExportRunner().ready?.recording.id` changes, the same way library-detail does.
- Show the loading screen only for the first load (`isLoading && !video`), so a re-list doesn't unmount `ExportScreen`.
- Add a test: start a copy, then resolve the runner's ready state with the new item returned from `listLibraryItems`, and check that the card reads "Ready".
````

</details>

title: Comment says nothing is composited over this player, but it now draws the webcam
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Comment says nothing is composited over this player, but it now draws the webcam**

The comment under the player says the vault file is shown untouched and that anything is "composited only in the editor's preview and burned in only by an export". With this PR the same player draws a second `<video>` (the webcam file) on top of the screen recording, at the recorded layout and with the camera-off gaps applied (`recording-player.tsx:81-91`). The file on disk is still untouched, so ADR 0003 still holds. But a reader of this comment would now expect the player to show the bare screen file. Add a sentence that the recorded webcam is overlaid here too (it comes from the take, not from an edit). That way the 'original' note and the overlay don't seem to contradict each other.

title: Overlay sits outside the <video>: it covers the native controls and is lost in native fullscreen
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Overlay sits outside the <video>: it covers the native controls and is lost in native fullscreen**

`.picture` is a sibling of the `<video controls>`, and the webcam `.slot` inside it has `z-index: 3` (`webcam-layer.module.css:5-10`). Two things follow. (1) The bubble paints over the native control bar. A bottom-corner bubble, which is the usual place, hides the timeline end, the volume and the fullscreen button. Clicks still pass through (`pointer-events: none`), but users can't see what they are clicking. (2) The native controls' fullscreen button puts only the `<video>` element into fullscreen, so the face disappears in fullscreen. The two options are: (a) custom controls, or calling `requestFullscreen` on `.player` instead of the video; or (b) accept and document the limitation. Either is a judgement call, but nothing in the PR mentions it.

title: With a webcam take, the native controls' fullscreen button (and Picture-in-Picture in Chromium's overflow menu) shows only this `<video>` element.
body:
With a webcam take, the native controls' fullscreen button (and Picture-in-Picture in Chromium's overflow menu) shows only this `<video>` element. The face overlay is a sibling outside it, so it disappears exactly when the user enlarges the take. That is the same "the recording lost the camera" impression this PR fixes, and it isn't in the PR's out-of-scope list.

A cheap fix: when `webcam` is set, pass `controlsList="nofullscreen"` and `disablePictureInPicture`. A fuller fix: offer a fullscreen action that calls `requestFullscreen()` on `.player`, the way `video-editor-page.tsx` does for the editor.

title: Acceptance criterion uses a 0.6 s section, but sections must be at least 1 s
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Acceptance criterion uses a 0.6 s section, but sections must be at least 1 s**

Line 340 says sections are at least `WEBCAM_MIN_SEGMENT_SECONDS` (1 s) long, and `startSectionAt` is refused when the window is under 1 s (line 388). That makes the criterion "A 0.6 s section with a 1000 ms transition animates for 300 ms" impossible to set up, so nobody can check it. Use a section that can exist and still hits the cap, for example "a 1.2 s section with a 1000 ms transition animates for 600 ms". Failure 3 at line 156 already does this with a 1 s section.

title: `webcamStateAt` formula mixes milliseconds and seconds
body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: `webcamStateAt` formula mixes milliseconds and seconds**

`ms` is in milliseconds (line 316, 100–2000), but `s`, `e` and `t` are source seconds (line 323). As written, `d = min(ms, (e − s) / 2)` almost always picks the half-section in seconds, and `p = ease((t − s) / d)` divides seconds by a value that may be either unit. Step 3 (line 360) has the same problem. Spell the conversion out, for example `d = min(ms / 1000, (e − s) / 2)`. This is the spec the implementation and the failure-1 and failure-3 tests will be written from.

title: Open-input bound differs between failure 19 and section 4.5
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Open-input bound differs between failure 19 and section 4.5**

Section 4.5 (line 575) says inputs open at an item's start and are disposed at its end, "so at most two are open at once". Failure 19 asserts at most `maxConcurrentVideos + 1`. Acceptance (line 256) says "one input per visible item". Pick one bound. If the +1 is meant for pre-opening the next item, as the preview does by mounting 1 s early, say so in 4.5. Otherwise the test will allow a leak that the design rules out.

title: Split is not visually a no-op when the 50 % cap changes the left half's transition
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Split is not visually a no-op when the 50 % cap changes the left half's transition**

The spec claims that splitting changes nothing visually. The right half does draw the same, because its from equals its to. The left half does not always: it keeps the transition, but its effective duration is `min(ms, 50 % of the section)` (decision 3), and the section is now shorter. For example, a 2 s section with a 1000 ms slide split at +1.5 s plays a 750 ms slide instead of 1000 ms. Either state this or say how split preserves the original effective duration.

title: Video limit check doesn't cover restoring a hidden media lane
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Video limit check doesn't cover restoring a hidden media lane**

`concurrentVideoCount` counts only visible lanes, and refusal is defined only for placing, moving or trimming an item. Restoring a hidden lane through "+ Add track" (`setMediaLaneHidden`, open question 8) can bring back video items that push the count past 2 at some instant. Say whether that restore is refused with the same message, or what happens instead. Failure 15's test should cover the restore path too.

title: This criterion can't be tested.
body: This criterion can't be tested. §2.1 says sections are at least `WEBCAM_MIN_SEGMENT_SECONDS` (1 s) long, so a 0.6 s section can't exist, and `startSectionAt` and split would both refuse to create one. Failure 3 already uses a valid case (a 1 s section with a 2000 ms request animates for 500 ms). Use a section of 1 s or longer here too, for example "A 1.2 s section with a 1000 ms transition animates for 600 ms".

title: Two hidden segments that touch are covered, but two that are close aren't.
body: Two hidden segments that touch are covered, but two that are close aren't. When the gap between them is under 400 ms, the fade-in after the first and the fade-out before the second overlap, and step 5 doesn't say how to combine them. The choice changes what renders. With `max`, opacity jumps from 0 straight to about 0.45 when a 100 ms gap starts, so the fade pops. With `min` (or a product), it stays continuous. State the combination rule (`min` keeps it continuous) and add the case to failure 6 so the test covers it.

title: The limit is only checked when an item is placed, moved or trimmed, and `concurrentVideoCount` only counts visible lanes.
body:
The limit is only checked when an item is placed, moved or trimmed, and `concurrentVideoCount` only counts visible lanes. So un-hiding a media lane bypasses it: `setMediaLaneHidden`, or restoring the lane from "+ Add track", can bring back a video that overlaps two visible ones. The §6 parser doesn't check the limit either. Then the preview and the export run three decoders, which is exactly what failures 15 and 19 rule out.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Concurrent-video limit can be bypassed by un-hiding a lane

## Affected sites
- specs/2026-10-31-editor-timeline-v2-design.md §4.4 (limit enforced only on place/move/trim)
````

title: An in-app fallback card disappears when the page remounts on the same history entry
body:
🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: An in-app fallback card disappears when the page remounts on the same history entry**

`fallbackFor` is component state, but `askedKeys` is now module-wide. Here is the sequence: the floating window fails (main answers false, which happens more often now because of the new 3 s timeout and the load-failure paths), so the page shows the in-app card. That goes against the doc's promise that the card is "never lost". One option is to record the outcome per key (asked / fell back) in the module map and start `fallbackFor` from it, for example `useState(() => fellBack.has(request?.key) ? request.key : null)`.

title: Check reads a possibly stale `origin/main`, so 'the day main takes the number' depends on a fetch
body:
🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Check reads a possibly stale `origin/main`, so 'the day main takes the number' depends on a fetch**

`mainNames()` runs `git ls-tree origin/main`, which reads the local remote-tracking ref. `git push` does not update that ref. Only `git fetch` or `git pull` does. A developer who has not fetched since `main` took a number will still pass the pre-push hook. The header (lines 9–10) says the collision is flagged "the day `main` takes the number", and `webcam-track.md:134-136` says it "shows up the day it happens". Both claims hold only after a fetch. Either say so in both places, or run a quiet `git fetch origin main` first (ignoring failures, as you already do for a missing ref) so the check matches what the docs promise.

body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠📝 **Fix · docs: ADR says shape and cornerRadius are never per section, but overrides can carry both**

Decision 2 says cornerRadius lives only in the global `WebcamLayout` and, "like shape it is never per section (ADR 0039)". The code does the opposite:
- `webcam-inspector.tsx` shows the same `WebcamControls` for a selected override (see its header comment), and the new Corners slider at lines 107-120 commits `{ cornerRadius }` through the same `commit` as Shape.
- `webcam-edits.ts:100` merges that patch into `segment.layout`.
- `webcamAt` (`webcam-model.ts:190`) spreads `segment.layout` over the global layout.
- `session.ts:383` accepts `cornerRadius` in a partial (override) layout.

Shape is already per section today too: `compose-webcam.test.ts:53` uses an override with `shape: "rounded"`, and `video-editor-page.test.tsx:996` clicks Square on an override.

There are two ways to fix this. Either correct the ADR so it says shape and corner can be overridden per section, matching the code. Or, if they really should stay global, hide Shape and Corners for overrides in the inspector and drop those keys in `validateWebcamLayout` when `complete` is false. As things stand, the ADR describes behaviour the code doesn't have.

title: Snap divides by the literal 100 instead of using the step
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Snap divides by the literal 100 instead of using the step**

`Math.round(clamped / CAMERA_CORNER_RADIUS_STEP) / 100` only works because the step is 0.01. If the step ever changes, the result goes silently wrong. Two options: `Math.round(clamped / STEP) * STEP` (followed by a rounding to two decimals to drop float noise), or derive the divisor from the step (`1 / STEP`).

title: The known-costs list misses two ways a push can cost far more than its own delta.
body:
The known-costs list misses two ways a push can cost far more than its own delta. These are the costs that every-push reviews make routine:

- **Merging `main` into the branch.** The engine diffs `compare/<marker>...<head>`. A merge commit leaves the head `ahead` of the marker, so every file `main` changed since then lands in the review scope, up to the $3 cap. The engine may also comment on code the PR never touched.
- **A partial review keeps the marker in place.** The marker moves only after a full, unscoped review that covered every file (`if (!scoped && notReviewed.length === 0) parts.push(marker(headSha))` in `src/engine.ts`). So when one review hits the budget, every later push re-reviews everything since the old marker and can hit the cap again.

Both seem worth listing next to the rebase case.

title: A name made only of replaced or trailing characters gives a folder name ending in a space
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A name made only of replaced or trailing characters gives a folder name ending in a space**

`validateWorkspaceName` accepts a name like `?`, `...` or `-`. In `newWorkspaceFolderName`, `?` turns into `-`, and the trailing-strip regex then removes it, so `safe` ends up as `""`. The function then returns `"Kaipu Record — "`, which ends in a space: the same trailing space the doc comment says Windows refuses. On macOS a second name like that (for example `*`) collides with the first folder, and `create` refuses it as `exists`. A possible fix: when `safe` is empty, fall back to a placeholder, or strip the trailing space from the whole result. Another option is to reject such names in validation.

title: Edit rollback leaves a newly written identity.json when the folder had none before
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Edit rollback leaves a newly written identity.json when the folder had none before**

When the registry write fails, the rollback only restores the folder's file if `previous.kind === "ok"`. Take a pending entry whose folder is reachable but has no `identity.json` (`previous` is missing). `edit` writes a fresh identity at line 581 with the entry's id and the new name. If `update` then throws, that file stays on disk. The next probe finds an identity with the matching id and adopts it, so the change that was refused shows up again. Calling `removeIdentity(entry.path)` in the non-ok case would undo it the way `create`'s `undo` does.

title: Edit does not re-check name uniqueness inside the locked write, unlike create
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Edit does not re-check name uniqueness inside the locked write, unlike create**

`create` re-runs `validateWorkspaceName` inside `update`, so two concurrent creates cannot take the same name (line 515). `edit` validates only once, at line 540, before several awaits (the probe, `readIdentity`, `writeIdentity`). title: Change folder… refuses the moved folder of a `pendingInit` workspace, which is the case it is meant to fix
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Change folder… refuses the moved folder of a `pendingInit` workspace, which is the case it is meant to fix (confidence medium)**

`open()` registers the migrated Default workspace with `pendingInit` when the old `vaultDirectory` is unplugged at upgrade (lines 298-303). In that case no `identity.json` was ever written to that folder. Suppose the drive comes back at a different mount path. That is the case the not-connected notice's button exists for. The folder has `.kaipu/` sidecars and no identity, so `checkRelocate` reaches line 809 and returns `has-items-no-identity`. The same rule hits a `pendingInit` entry whose moved folder already holds an identity with another id. Line 802 refuses it as `different`, but `availability` adopts that id at lines 678-687.

A possible fix: when `entry.pendingInit` is set, accept a folder with no identity (the probe writes it later). For a folder with another workspace's identity, apply the same `pendingInit && !this.get(identity.id)` adoption rule that `availability` uses.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **An offline `edit` clears `pendingInit`, so "Change folder…" then refuses the moved folder.** `checkRelocate` accepts a moved folder that has `.kaipu` and no `identity.json` only when `entry.pendingInit` is set (Line 848). `edit` clears `pendingInit` unconditionally inside `update` (Line 627), including when `savedToFolder` is `false`. Trace: 1. The Default workspace is migrated while its drive is unplugged. The entry gets `pendingInit`. 2. The user renames or recolors it while the drive is away. `edit` takes the registry-only path and removes `pendingInit`. It sets `pendingIdentity`. 3. The drive remounts at another path. The user picks the new folder in "Change folder…". 4. The folder has `.kaipu` sidecars and no identity. `checkRelocate` now returns `has-items-no-identity`, so the user cannot reconnect the workspace. This is the case the pending-init exception is meant to cover. The same loss disables the identity-adoption branch in `availability` (Line 711), which also requires `pendingInit`. Clear `pendingInit` only when the identity file was actually written. `availability` already clears `pendingInit` and `pendingIdentity` together once the file is written.
🐛 Proposed fix in `edit` (Line 627)
```diff - delete target.pendingInit; + // Still no identity.json in the folder when it was not written: keep the init pending. + if (savedToFolder) delete target.pendingInit; ```
Add a test that edits a `pendingInit` workspace while its folder is missing, then relocates it to a folder with Kaipu items and no identity.

title: No renderer test checks that an unchanged relocate shows no toast
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: No renderer test checks that an unchanged relocate shows no toast (confidence high)**

The flag is only asserted in main (`relocate.test.ts:158`). Nothing in the renderer tests sends `{ ok: true, unchanged: true }` through `changeFolder` and checks that `folderChanged` is not shown. The IPC mapping at `index.ts:349` isn't tested either. If either the spread or the early return were dropped, the misleading "now points to the new folder" toast from the earlier thread would come back and every test would still pass. A context or Settings test with the mocked `relocate` returning `unchanged: true` would cover it.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Keeping `pendingInit` after an offline edit lets the probe's adoption overwrite that edit
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Keeping `pendingInit` after an offline edit lets the probe's adoption overwrite that edit (confidence medium)**

Before this change, an offline edit cleared `pendingInit`. Now it stays set together with `pendingIdentity` (lines 634 and 638). Suppose the folder comes back holding an identity with an id this Mac doesn't know (written by another Mac). `availability` then takes the adoption branch at lines 718-726, and `Object.assign(entry, entryFromIdentity(...))` replaces the name and color the user just typed. The next probe sees a matching id with `pendingIdentity` still set and writes the folder's own name back to it (lines 670-682). The rename is lost and no message tells the user. Before this change, the same folder was shown as `different`. If the registry is meant to win here (that is what `pendingIdentity` stands for), the adoption branch could reapply the pending name and color after adopting the id.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: `MoveItemsFlow` doc says null means nothing was attempted, but a lost IPC reply now also returns null
body: The doc comment on `MoveItemsFlow` says it "Resolves the result, or null when nothing was attempted (cancelled, or the editor stayed)". Since this change, the catch at line 93 also returns `null`, and in that case main may already have moved part or all of the group. One caller relies on this contract: `library-page.tsx:145` reads `null` as "nothing happened" and leaves the selection as it was. That's harmless today, but the comment now gives future callers the wrong idea. Suggest adding "or when the result is unknown (the reply was lost)" to the comment.

title: A relocate that loses to a switch in flight comes back as a silent "cancelled"
body: `relocateActive` returns `{ reason: "cancelled" }` when a switch is already in flight (`switch-transaction.ts:107`), not only when the picker or an editor is cancelled. `relocateRefusalMessage` maps `cancelled` to `null` (`relocate-copy.ts:17-18`). The dialog (`workspace-dialog.tsx:153`) and the context (`workspaces-context.tsx:231-232`) then show nothing. So a user who picked the right folder while a switch was running, for example one started from the tray, gets no change and no message. The doc comment here describes only the two user cancellations. Consider adding a distinct reason, such as `busy` or `switching`, with its own sentence, or at least documenting this case.

title: Spec says relocate accepts only a matching identity.json, but the registry accepts two more cases
body:
The new row says the folder is "Accepted only when the folder's `identity.json` has the same id" and refused for "`.kaipu` items with no identity". `WorkspaceRegistry.checkRelocate` also accepts two other folders:
- the folder the workspace already points at, whose identity file is gone (`registry.ts:849`);
- a folder with `.kaipu/` and no identity, for a `pendingInit` workspace (`registry.ts:855`).

The backlog paragraph (`backlog/several-workspaces.md:24-26`) makes the same unconditional claim. Consider naming both exceptions.

title: Every error in a group move is reported as "stale"
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Every error in a group move is reported as "stale"**

The `catch` around `workspaceGate().run(...)` turns any thrown error into `refuseAll("stale")`. Only a `StaleWorkspaceError` from the gate means that. Two other errors also land here:

- `vaultActivity.run("library", …)` calls `admit()`, which throws `MaintenanceError` (`vault-activity.ts:96`) when "Check and fix files" starts after the early `inMaintenance` check at line 161 but before the gate admits the call.
- A rejected `loadDeviceId` throws too.

In both cases the user is told their window's workspace is no longer active, which is false.

Suggested fix: map `StaleWorkspaceError` to "stale" and `MaintenanceError` to "maintenance". Map anything else to "io". This is the same mapping `runMoveGroup` already uses for an item that throws.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: A rejected device-id promise is cached for the rest of the process
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A rejected device-id promise is cached for the rest of the process**

`deviceId ??= loadDeviceId(...)` keeps the promise even when it rejects. After one failure, for example a transient read error in userData, every later group move rejects at `await deviceId` until the app restarts. With the catch below, the user also sees each of those as "stale". Consider resetting `deviceId = null` when the promise rejects.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: `skipped` doc says whole-group refusals go there, but the code puts them in `failed`
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠📝 **Fix · docs: `skipped` doc says whole-group refusals go there, but the code puts them in `failed`**

The comment on `skipped` says it also holds items from a group that "was refused before it began". But `moveItems` in `main/workspaces/index.ts:153-158` builds a whole-group refusal (`busy`, `stale`, `maintenance`) with every item in `failed` and `skipped: []`. Only Stop fills `skipped` (`move-group.ts:38`). Either change the comment, or have `refuseAll` fill `skipped` if that is the intended contract.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: ensureByName can create tags that the result then drops
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: ensureByName can create tags that the result then drops**

Missing tags are minted and written for every entry in `wanted`, but the result is cut to `TAGS_PER_ITEM_MAX` afterwards. If the input has more names than the per-item cap, the extra tags stay in the destination registry without belonging to any item. Consider stopping once `result.length` reaches `TAGS_PER_ITEM_MAX`, before minting more.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Roll-forward deletes every item's drag folders, not just this item's
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Roll-forward deletes every item's drag folders, not just this item's**

When `healEntry` rolls a move forward, it runs `rm(join(sourceDir, META_DIR, "drag"), { recursive: true })`. That deletes the whole `.kaipu/drag/` folder, so drag copies of every item in the source workspace go with it. Some of those may have been dragged less than `DRAG_SETTLE_MS` ago, so a drop target can still be reading them. The comment says "a drag copy of the item", and `DragLedger.clear` (drag-ledger.ts:38-45) only removes the folders of the one item, in line with decision 11.

This also runs while the app is open, not only on startup. `healMoves` runs before each move (index.ts:117), and `moveLocked`'s post-commit catch calls `healEntry` directly (line 409). So an unrelated drag that is still in progress can lose its file.

Suggested fix: limit the cleanup to this item's folders. Use the ledger's entries when they exist, and on startup the folders whose names identify the item. If the folders cannot be told apart by item, skip folders younger than `DRAG_SETTLE_MS`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: A move that already committed is reported as `io` if post-commit healing throws
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A move that already committed is reported as `io` if post-commit healing throws**

Once `mediaPlaced` is true, the target holds the item. But if the `healEntry` call here throws (for example, `writeJournal` or `readSidecarStrict` fail on an I/O error), the error goes to `moveItem`'s catch at line 204, and the move returns `refuse("io")`. The renderer then says the item failed to move when it is already in the target, and possibly half-removed from the source.

Suggested fix: wrap this `healEntry` call in its own try/catch, log the error, leave the journal for `healMoves` to finish, and still return `{ ok: true, newId }`.

Also, line 414 always reports `mode: "copied"`, even after a hard link. The real `mode` is in scope and could be returned instead.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Pressing Enter or Space on a "Move to" target opens the item instead of moving it
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Pressing Enter or Space on a "Move to" target opens the item instead of moving it**

The menu is portaled to `document.body`, but React portals still pass events up the React tree. The wrappers here (line 49 and line 82) stop only `click`. A `keydown` on a focused target `<button role="menuitem">` in `MoveTargetList` therefore reaches the card's `onKeyDown` (`video-card.tsx:81-86`) or the row's (`video-row.tsx:68-73`). That handler checks for Enter or Space without looking at `e.target`. It calls `e.preventDefault()`, which stops the button's synthesized click, then `activate()` → `onNavigate()`. So a keyboard user who opens the menu and presses Enter on a workspace navigates into the item and never moves it. In select mode the same keypress toggles the item's checkbox instead. The "⋯" button has the same problem: Enter on it opens the item rather than the menu.

Fix: also stop `onKeyDown` propagation on the anchor div and the portal wrapper. Another option is to have the card and row handlers ignore events whose `target !== currentTarget`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Stop before anything moved reports "Moved 0 items"
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Stop before anything moved reports "Moved 0 items"**

When the user presses Stop before the first move finishes, the result can have `moved: []`, `failed: []` and `skipped: [...]`. That state misses the first branch (line 85, because skipped > 0) and the `resultNone` branch (line 87, because failed is 0), so it lands in this `else` branch. The toast then reads `resultAll` with `count: 0`, "Moved 0 items to Personal", followed by the skipped count. Add a branch for `moved.length === 0` that says nothing moved.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: orderForMove puts each recording's exports in reverse order
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: orderForMove puts each recording's exports in reverse order**

The loop walks `rest` backwards and pushes each match as it splices it out. That reverses the exports relative to the loaded list: the test at move-flow.test.ts:43 expects `rec, exp2, exp1`. `MoveRequest.items` is documented as "in the order on screen", and with this ordering the group moves the exports, and reports progress on them, in reverse. You could collect the matches in a forward pass and then remove them from `rest`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: An IPC error is reported to the user as "stale"
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: An IPC error is reported to the user as "stale"**

If `moveItems` rejects, every item is marked failed with reason `stale`. The toast then gives the `reason_stale` text for each item, which is not what happened. The real cause is only written to the console. A generic error message, or a dedicated reason, would describe the failure correctly.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Spanish move strings say "workspace" where the rest of the app says "espacio de trabajo"
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Spanish move strings say "workspace" where the rest of the app says "espacio de trabajo"**

Three new `move.*` strings leave the term in English: `chipLabel` ("Mover a otro workspace", line 2617), `newWorkspace` ("Nuevo workspace…", line 2623) and `reason_stale` ("el workspace cambió", line 2662). The existing Spanish strings for the same idea say "espacio de trabajo": `add` is "Nuevo espacio de trabajo…" (line 2562), and so are `addAction` and `newTitle` (lines 2588–2589), and `editNotWritable` uses it too. As a result, the switcher shows "Nuevo espacio de trabajo…" and the Move to menu shows "Nuevo workspace…" for the same action. Fix: use "espacio de trabajo" in all three strings.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: The roll-forward deletes the source media and every source companion without checking that the source is still the file the journal describes.
body:
The roll-forward deletes the source media and every source companion without checking that the source is still the file the journal describes. Here is how that loses work:

1. The app dies after `media-placed`.
2. The USB target is unplugged at the next start, so the entry stays `waiting`.
3. The item is still listed in the source, so the user keeps editing it there (the `.edit.json`, or a screenshot overwrite).
4. Once the target is back, the next `healMoves` (at startup, or before any group move) deletes those newer edits.

There is a second problem at the same lines. `done()` drops the journal even when `unlink` failed (for example EBUSY on Windows while something holds the file open). By then `removeCompanions` has already deleted the sidecar, so a bare media file stays behind and comes back listed under a new identity.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Roll-forward deletes an unverified or undeletable source

## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/move-item.ts:675 — `unlink(sourceMedia)` runs whenever `sourcePresent`, ignoring `sourceMatches`. Its error is swallowed.
- apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/move-item.ts:676-677 — `removeCompanions` and `done()` run even when the media unlink failed, so the journal is gone and the source sidecar is deleted while the media is still there.
- apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/move-item.ts:674 — removes the whole `.kaipu/drag/` folder, including other items' drag copies that a drop target may still be reading (healing also runs before every group move, not only at startup).
- apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/move-item.ts:395-415 — the live path: if `rm(media)` throws, it goes into `healEntry` and still returns `ok: true`, whatever the heal did.

## Required outcome
- Roll-forward never deletes a source whose media no longer matches the journal (size+mtime, or sha256), and never deletes companions the user changed after `journal.createdAt`. Quarantine those cases instead.
- If the source media cannot be removed, keep the journal (report `waiting`) and keep the source sidecar, so a later heal retries and the file is never left without its record.
- Remove only this item's drag folders, not every folder in `.kaipu/drag/`.

## Suggested approach (optional)
- Compute `sourceMatches` (already available) and branch on it before the unlink. Check the source companions' mtimes against `journal.createdAt` to catch a newer edit project.
- Unlink the media first and stop if it fails; only then call `removeCompanions` and `done()`.
- Add a heal test: a waiting entry, then the source's `.edit.json` is rewritten, then the target reconnects. Assert that the entry is quarantined and the source is intact.
````

</details>

title: Roll-forward healing can delete a different item that took the source stem.
body:
** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Roll-forward healing can delete a different item that took the source stem.** When it rolls a move forward, `healEntry` calls `unlink(sourceMedia)` whenever `sourcePresent` is true. It then calls `removeCompanions(from.companionPaths(journal.sourceId))` without checking that these files still belong to the moved item. A journal entry can stay as `"waiting"` for a long time. This happens when the target was unplugged right after a crash in the `committed` phase, for example after `source-companions-deleted`. In that state the source stem `Demo` is free. A new recording, a screenshot or a rename can then claim `Demo` in the source workspace. When the target reconnects, `healMoves` runs at startup and before each group move. It then deletes the new item's media and its whole record. This loses user data with no way to undo it. Delete the source media only when `sourceMatches` is true. Remove the companions only when the source record is missing, or when its `assetId` equals `journal.assetId`.
🛡️ Proposed fix
```diff --- "a/apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/move-item.ts" +++ "b/apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/move-item.ts" @@ -672,8 +672,16 @@ await refreshFreshness(to, targetId, journal).catch(() => {}); // A drag copy of the item could still name its bytes in the source (decision 11). await rm(join(sourceDir, META_DIR, "drag"), { recursive: true, force: true }).catch(() => {}); - if (sourcePresent) await unlink(sourceMedia).catch(() => {}); - await removeCompanions(from.companionPaths(journal.sourceId)); + const sourceRecord = await readSidecarStrict(from.sidecarPath(journal.sourceId)); + const sourceIsOurs = + sourceRecord.status === "missing" || + (sourceRecord.status === "ok" && sourceRecord.sidecar.assetId === journal.assetId); + if (sourcePresent && sourceMatches && sourceIsOurs) { + await unlink(sourceMedia).catch(() => {}); + } + if (sourceIsOurs && (!sourcePresent || sourceMatches)) { + await removeCompanions(from.companionPaths(journal.sourceId)); + } return done(); } ```
Committable suggestion
> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion const sourceRecord = await readSidecarStrict(from.sidecarPath(journal.sourceId)); const sourceIsOurs = sourceRecord.status === "missing" || (sourceRecord.status === "ok" && sourceRecord.sidecar.assetId === journal.assetId); if (sourcePresent && sourceMatches && sourceIsOurs) { await unlink(sourceMedia).catch(() => {}); } if (sourceIsOurs && (!sourcePresent || sourceMatches)) { await removeCompanions(from.companionPaths(journal.sourceId)); } ```

title: Adopt the pending workspace ID before refreshing capture settings.
Changing the active workspace's folder doesn't re-read its settings.json before commit, unlike a switch
body:
`runSwitch` re-reads the target's folder overrides inside `persistActive`. It does this before the commit (lines 423-428), so `afterCommit`'s `notifyOverridesChanged()` already broadcasts the right effective settings. `relocateFolder` reuses the same `afterCommit` (line 585 → `activeTransactionDeps`, line 406), but `relocateActive`'s `apply` only calls `registry.relocate` (relocate.ts:48). Nothing calls `workspaceSettings.refresh(id)`.

`WorkspaceSettings` caches reads by workspace id (workspace-settings.ts:103-106, 199-206). The usual reason to relocate is that the folder moved and the workspace became unavailable, so the last probe cached `unreadable` (workspace-settings.ts:175). In that case the commit broadcasts `settings:changed` without the workspace's own overrides. The cache is only corrected by a later `refresh`. Today that comes from the renderer: `PendingSettingsHost` calls `getScoped(activeId)` again when the generation epoch bumps (scope-controls.tsx:492-504, workspaces-context.tsx:88-89). Captures also refresh when they start (index.ts:313).

So the stale broadcast is short-lived. But correctness depends on the app shell being mounted, and it is the gap the switch path's comment at lines 425-426 says is closed.

Possible fix: wrap `apply` for the active case, e.g. `async () => { const o = await reg.relocate(id, chosen); if (o.ok) await workspaceSettings?.refresh(id); return o; }`. Also call `await workspaceSettings?.refresh(id)` after a non-active relocate, as `addWorkspace` does at line 476.

title: `workspaces:relocate` row leaves out `unchanged`, the `moving` lock and `not-a-folder`
body: The row says the result is `{ ok, workspace }` and that relocate is refused "while a recording or export runs". The code has more. `WorkspaceRelocateResult` also carries `unchanged?: true` (shared/types/workspaces.ts:180), and the handler sets it at index.ts:617. Relocate is also refused while a group move runs (`moving`, via `busyNow`, index.ts:76-78 and shared/types/workspaces.ts:158), and for a path that isn't a folder (`not-a-folder`, line 160). Consider adding these so the table matches the contract.

title: A failed machine-record write after the folder write makes this Mac's own overrides go pending
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A failed machine-record write after the folder write makes this Mac's own overrides go pending**

`applyFolder` writes the folder file first (line 241), puts the new read in the cache (line 242), and only then records the new sha256 with `decision: "use"` (lines 243-246). If `machine.update` throws (for example a disk error in `atomicWriteFile`), `apply` returns `failed`. By then the folder file on disk already has the new bytes, but the machine record still holds the old hash. `folderState` (settings-overrides.ts:168) then reports the file as `pending`, so `overridesOf` drops every folder override for this workspace, including the ones that were active before the edit. The user is then asked to confirm values this Mac wrote itself. Possible fixes: if the record write fails, put the previous file back, or retry recording the hash. At minimum, keep the cache consistent with what was recorded.

title: A pending folder file blocks clearing `uploadMode` in the same call, and copyToAll may not report it
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A pending folder file blocks clearing `uploadMode` in the same call, and copyToAll may not report it**

In `apply`, when `applyFolder` returns `pending` or `unreadable`, the function returns at line 200 before it reaches the machine-bound `uploadMode` branch (lines 202-209). So `resetOverrides(id, ["screenshotCopy", "uploadMode"])` on a workspace whose folder file is pending leaves `uploadMode` overridden. `copyToAll` (lines 324-328) then adds the workspace to `keptOwn` only when the pending file holds one of the wanted keys. A workspace whose `uploadMode` override survived but whose pending file holds none of the wanted keys is therefore missing from `keptOwn`, and "all" quietly means "some". Today's UI never sends `uploadMode` together with folder keys: the SectionBanner keys in settings-pages.tsx are `[recordingQuality, exportQuality]`, `[showBrandBadge]` and `[screenshotCopy]`. But the IPC handler (index.ts:545-550) accepts any mix. Two possible fixes: apply the machine-bound key whatever the folder outcome, or check `uploadMode` in the `pending` branch of `copyToAll`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Every scope consumer runs its own useAppSettings fetch and listener, even inside the provider
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡⚡ **Consider · perf: Every scope consumer runs its own useAppSettings fetch and listener, even inside the provider**

`useSettingsScope` always calls `useScopeState(shared === null)`. That is how hooks have to be called, but `useScopeState` calls `useAppSettings()` (line 64) on every call, and that hook's effect isn't gated: each call runs `window.electronAPI.getSettings()` and registers an `onSettingsChanged` listener (`use-app-settings.ts:15-18`).

Inside `SettingsScopeProvider`, every `ScopeTag`, `ScopeSelector`, `ScopeDot` (×3), `ScopeLegend`, `ScopeLine`, `AppWideBadge`, `SectionBanner`, `ScopeNotice` and `useScopedSetting` therefore makes an extra IPC round trip and adds an extra listener. Every settings change then re-renders each of these components through its own unused state.

Possible fix: split the provider-less fallback into a separate component, or move the `useAppSettings` call so it only runs when `enabled`. For example, pass `update` in, or call the IPC `updateSettings` directly inside `setValue`.

title: Test asserts on an object that was already built, so it can never fail
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🧪 **Fix · tests: Test asserts on an object that was already built, so it can never fail**

`take` is the plain object that `resolveInput()` returned at line 292. The broadcast at line 293 cannot change a value that already exists, so `expect(take.frameRate).toBe(24)` passes no matter what the hook does. If the hook rebuilt the input from the latest settings, this test would still pass. To test what the name says, check the input the recorder actually uses after the broadcast. If the recorder calls `resolveInput` lazily, call it again after `broadcast(...)` and assert that the result still has `frameRate: 24`. Otherwise, make the assertion against whatever value the hook keeps for the take that is running.

title: Every workspace that is not connected lands in `keptOwn`, even one that never overrode these keys: `apply` returns `unavailable` from the `isAvailable` gate (l…

Every workspace that is not connected lands in `keptOwn`, even one that never overrode these keys: `apply` returns `unavailable` from the `isAvailable` gate (line 192) before it looks at what the workspace holds. With one unplugged drive, every "Copy to all" toast says "<name> keep their own value", which is false whenever that workspace had no override. The existing test (`names a workspace it cannot clear…`) only covers the case where it does have one.

````markdown
## Affected sites
- apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/workspace-settings.ts:322-323 — pushes the name for every `unavailable`/`unreadable` result, whether or not that workspace has an override of `wanted`
````

title: "Never waits long" is only true of the file read: `refresh` first awaits `isAvailable` → `reg.availability()` (a `stat`, a read of `identity.json`, and sometim…
body: "Never waits long" is only true of the file read: `refresh` first awaits `isAvailable` → `reg.availability()` (a `stat`, a read of `identity.json`, and sometimes a write to it), and `READ_TIMEOUT_MS` does not bound that. This all runs before `handleCapture` opens the overlay. So every screenshot hotkey now waits on folder I/O, and on a slow or evicted (iCloud) folder the overlay can lag by more than the 2 s that the ADR note promises. Consider bounding the whole refresh with the timeout, availability probe included, on the capture path.

title: Run override writes for one workspace one at a time. Concurrent `apply` calls can lose an edit or make this Mac's own file pending.
body:
** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Run override writes for one workspace one at a time. Concurrent `apply` calls can lose an edit or make this Mac's own file pending.** `MachineSettingsStore.update` runs its own updates one at a time. Nothing does the same for the read → write → record sequence in `applyFolder`. Two `settings:set-override` calls for the same workspace can therefore interleave. One example is a user who changes Recording quality and then Export quality quickly. Two failures can follow: - B reads the file before A writes it. B computes `next` from the old `base` and writes after A. A's key is then lost from the folder file. - B reads the file after A writes it but before A's `machine.update` records the new sha256. `folderState` then returns `pending` for B, and B's call fails with `reason: "pending"`. If the two `atomicWriteFile` renames finish in one order and the two record updates run in the other order, the recorded hash does not match the file on disk. The workspace then goes `pending`: `overridesOf` drops all of its folder overrides, and the user is asked to confirm values this Mac wrote. `resolvePending` has the same check-then-record shape. Put `apply` and `resolvePending` on one promise chain per workspace id.
🔒️ Proposed fix: one queue per workspace
```diff export class WorkspaceSettings { private readonly reads = new Map(); + private readonly queues = new Map>(); + + private serialized(id: string, run: () => Promise): Promise { + const next = (this.queues.get(id) ?? Promise.resolve()).then(run); + this.queues.set(id, next.catch(() => undefined)); + return next; + } ``` Then use the queue in `setOverride`, `resetOverrides` and `resolvePending`: ```diff - return this.apply(id, { [key]: value }); + return this.serialized(id, () => this.apply(id, { [key]: value })); ```

title: A slow `refresh` can overwrite a newer write in the cache. The active workspace's own overrides then show as pending.
body:
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **A slow `refresh` can overwrite a newer write in the cache. The active workspace's own overrides then show as pending.** `refresh` does not go through `serialize`. It can run at the same time as `applyFolder`. Here is one order of events: 1. `refresh` starts `probe` and reads the old file bytes. 2. `applyFolder` records the new hash in `beforeWrite`, writes the file, and calls `remember` with the new read. 3. `refresh` finishes and calls `remember(id, read)` with the old read. After step 3, the cache holds the old sha256 and the machine record holds the new one. `folderState` returns `pending`, so `overridesOf` drops all folder overrides of the workspace. `refresh` then calls `changed()`, which publishes effective settings without this Mac's own overrides. Several paths call `refresh` while an edit can be in flight: - `requireCaptureWorkspace` calls it at every capture start. - `getScoped("all")` calls it for every workspace. - A second Settings window calls it through its scoped read. The state recovers at the next refresh. Until then, captures and the Settings page use the wrong values. Do not put `refresh` in the queue: a capture must not wait for writes. Use a per-workspace write counter instead. Increment it before and after the folder write. `refresh` drops its read if the counter changed while it ran.
🐛 Proposed fix
```diff --- "a/apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/workspace-settings.ts" +++ "b/apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/workspace-settings.ts" @@ -105,12 +105,15 @@ * readable file. When the active workspace's overrides change because of it (a sync wrote * the file), everyone is told. */ async refresh(id: string): Promise { const ws = this.known(id); if (!ws) return; const before = JSON.stringify(this.overridesOf(id)); + const generation = this.writes.get(id) ?? 0; const read = await this.probe(id, ws.path); + // A write started or ended while the probe ran: its own read is newer than this one. + if ((this.writes.get(id) ?? 0) !== generation) return; this.remember(id, read); if (id === this.deps.activeId() && before !== JSON.stringify(this.overridesOf(id))) { this.deps.changed(); } ``` Add the field and bump it around the write in `applyFolder`: ```ts private readonly writes = new Map(); private bump(id: string): void { this.writes.set(id, (this.writes.get(id) ?? 0) + 1); } // in applyFolder, around writeFolderOverrides … remember: this.bump(ws.id); try { // existing write + catch this.remember(ws.id, { kind: "ok", overrides: next as FolderOverrides, sha256 }); } finally { this.bump(ws.id); } ```

title: A refresh that starts in the middle of a write can still put the old sha256 back
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A refresh that starts in the middle of a write can still put the old sha256 back**

The generation check only drops a probe that started before a `remember` and finished after the next one. `applyFolder` itself calls `remember` twice: once for the pre-write read (line 287) and once after the write (line 324). Between those two calls it records the new hash in the machine file (the `beforeWrite` hook, lines 308-312) and only then replaces the file.

Here is the failing order. A `refresh` (for example the capture-start one at `index.ts:147`) starts after line 287, so it captures that generation. Its probe reads the old bytes before the rename and returns before line 324. The generation has not changed, so line 124 caches the old read with the old sha256. The machine record already holds the new hash, so `folderState` reports `pending`. `overridesOf` then drops every folder override, and `changed()` fires. A capture that snapshots right after that refresh records without this Mac's overrides, which is the failure the new comment at lines 66-70 describes. The window is narrower than before but still there.

One option: treat an in-flight write as a reason to drop the probe too. For example, also return when `this.queues.has(id)` after the probe. The write's own read and `remember` are fresher in that case anyway. The other option is to bump the generation inside the `beforeWrite` hook and again after the write.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Between two refreshes, the first to finish now wins, not the freshest read
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Between two refreshes, the first to finish now wins, not the freshest read**

`refresh` also bumps the generation through `remember`. So when two refreshes of the same workspace overlap, whichever finishes first is cached, and the other is dropped along with its `changed()` notification. The comment says the landed read "is the newer one", but that is not true for two refreshes. Suppose refresh A starts first and reads quickly, a sync then rewrites the file, and refresh B (started later) reads the new bytes. If A finishes first, B's newer read is discarded, and the cache stays stale until the next refresh. Before this change, the last refresh to finish won.

Refreshes can overlap. `getScoped("all")` refreshes every workspace (line 179), and `getScoped(scope)` and `copyToAll` refresh too (lines 208, 410), while the capture start (`index.ts:147`) and activation (`index.ts:410`, `466`) refresh on their own.

One fix is to bump a separate counter only from the write paths (`applyFolder`, `resolvePendingNow`) and compare against that. Another is to give each probe a start sequence number and drop a read only if a later-started read has already landed.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Disk reads in resolvePending and applyFolder no longer fence off a slower refresh
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Disk reads in resolvePending and applyFolder no longer fence off a slower refresh**

Before this change, every `remember` bumped the generation. That included the fresh disk reads in `resolvePendingNow` (line 395) and the read at the start of `applyFolder` (line 319), which is the only read when it returns `pending`, `unreadable` or `unchanged`. Now only `beginWrite`/`endWrite` move `writeEpochs`, and they run only when the folder file is actually rewritten.

Here is the order that fails. A refresh starts and reads the old bytes (sha A). A sync then replaces the file with sha B. The user clicks "Use them", so `resolvePendingNow` reads B and records `{sha256: B, decision: "use"}`. Then the slow refresh finishes. `writing` is 0, the epoch has not changed and its ticket is still the newest, so line 150 caches read A. Record B does not match read A, so the state is `pending` and the overrides the user just accepted are dropped until the next refresh.

The window is narrow because it needs a sync in the middle of the race, but it is the same kind of race the new comment at lines 66-71 says is closed. One possible fix: bump `writeEpochs` (or the refresh ticket/applied counter) in `resolvePendingNow` and at the top of `applyFolder`'s read, so these fresh reads count as newer than any refresh already in flight.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: copyToAll refuses `uploadMode` because of an unrelated folder file
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: copyToAll refuses `uploadMode` because of an unrelated folder file**

The new guard returns `unreadable` whenever the folder file cannot be read, whatever keys are wanted. `uploadMode` is machine-bound. `computeOverrides` (line 196) reads it from `deps.machine` whether or not the folder file can be read, so `copyToAll(id, ["uploadMode"])` could still report what the workspace shows. Today's UI does not seem to send `uploadMode` to copyToAll, but the IPC accepts any overridable key. If that is meant to work, limit the guard to calls whose `wanted` includes a folder key.

title: Disable Edit and Prepare for evicted media.
Journal lists migrations 0000–0002 whose SQL files and snapshots are not in the tree
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Journal lists migrations 0000–0002 whose SQL files and snapshots are not in the tree**

This new journal lists `0000_baseline`, `0001_integrity` and `0002_account_provider_unique`. None of those `.sql` files or their `meta/000N_snapshot.json` files exist in `packages/infra-db/src/migrations/`: only the `0003` SQL and snapshot are there. The spec (`specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md:1112-1118`) explains why: the chain belongs to PR #364, which has not merged. Until it does, `main` has a migrations folder whose journal points at missing files. `bun run db:migrate` (`drizzle-kit migrate`, `packages/infra-db/package.json:24`) would fail as soon as it tries to read `0000_baseline.sql`. The command is documented as unused today (`commands.md:33`), but it is still wired up. One option is to commit only the `0003` SQL and keep the journal out of this PR, so #364 brings the journal. Another is to land this after #364, so the folder never sits in a half-state on `main`.

title: Snapshot chain points to a snapshot that isn't on main
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡❓ **Consider · question: Snapshot chain points to a snapshot that isn't on main**

This snapshot's `prevId` (`86ab3674-…`) points to a `0002` snapshot that exists only in PR #364. In this checkout, `src/migrations/` holds just `0003_cloud_asset_workspace_id.sql`, `meta/0003_snapshot.json` and `meta/_journal.json`. The journal still lists `0000_baseline`, `0001_integrity` and `0002_account_provider_unique` (`_journal.json:9-23`), but none of their SQL files or snapshots are here.

The spec explains this (`specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md:1112-1118`), and `commands.md:32-33` says `db:migrate` and `db:generate` aren't used yet. Until #364 merges, though, main ships a migrations folder that is broken: `bun run db:migrate` would fail looking for `0000_baseline.sql`, and the chain `drizzle-kit check` validates starts from a missing parent.

Could this snapshot and the journal wait for #364, or land on top of it? Then main would carry the column only through `db:push`, which is how the spec says it ships today. If both PRs are definitely merging together, please confirm that this snapshot was generated from #364's exact `0002` snapshot. If #364's snapshot changes before it merges, the `prevId` here will no longer match.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: The queue is not tied to an account, so a sign-in as someone else silently drops the owed assignments
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: The queue is not tied to an account, so a sign-in as someone else silently drops the owed assignments**

`QueuedAssignment` (lines 15-21) stores no `userId`, and `runOnce` sends every due entry with whichever account is signed in when it runs (`this.deps.account()`, line 116). Say user A moves items while offline, then signs out and user B signs in. A's entries go out with B's token. The server's `setWorkspace` is scoped to the owner, so it answers NOT_FOUND, and line 126 deletes the entry for good. A's cloud copies never learn their new workspace. `onConfirmed`/`setCachedWorkspace` in `library/index.ts:145` also writes to the current account's cache, not the account the entry was queued for. A fix: store `userId` on each entry and only send (and confirm) entries whose `userId` matches the signed-in account.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Synced workspaces stop sweeping `.kaipu/tmp/`, and non-synced ones never sweep their scratch folder
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Synced workspaces stop sweeping `.kaipu/tmp/`, and non-synced ones never sweep their scratch folder**

`deps.stagingDir ?? join(deps.vaultDir, STAGING_DIR)` replaces the folder-local staging directory instead of adding to it. The caller (`main/index.ts:763-767`) passes `stagingDir` only when `syncedStagingFor(vaultDir)` says the folder is synced right now. That leaves two gaps:
- A folder that held a take in `.kaipu/tmp/` before it was moved into Drive or iCloud is never swept again while it stays synced.
- Detection can come back null, for example when the xattr-only check in `detectSync` times out after 2 s (`synced-folder.ts:86-91`). On that launch, takes staged in `workspace-scratch/<id>/tmp` are not swept, so recovery depends on the next detection succeeding.

Nothing is deleted, but stranded recordings stay hidden. You could sweep both directories when they exist: the scratch one with `placeByRename`, and `.kaipu/tmp/` too. Also consider sweeping a workspace's scratch folder whenever it exists, not only when the folder is detected as synced.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: The main process does not check for evicted source media before hashing or copying it
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: The main process does not check for evicted source media before hashing or copying it**

When either side is synced, `linkable` is false, so the move reads the whole source media: `fs.sha256(media)` here unless a cached hash exists, then `copyExclusive`. The only guard against an evicted (dataless) source is in the renderer (`move-flow.ts:21`, `notMovableReason` → "evicted"), and that relies on the item list being fresh. `moveItems` (`workspaces/index.ts:248-255`) accepts any `{id, assetId}` from the renderer, and nothing on this path calls `probeDataless`. If the provider offloads the file after the list was built, the move downloads it. That breaks decision 15 ("never reads an evicted file"), and a stuck provider would block this read while the move holds the workspace gate and the switch lock. A `probeDataless` check on the source media when `source.scratch` is set could refuse with an "evicted" reason before any read.

title: Comment in the "is not synced" list describes a case that is synced
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Comment in the "is not synced" list describes a case that is synced**

This comment sits as the last item of the `it.each` that checks paths are **not** synced. But it describes the provider root, which `syncProviderOfPath` reports as synced (`synced-folder.ts:31-34`). The separate test at line 32 checks exactly that. A reader could take it for a missing or disabled case in the not-synced table. Move it to the test at line 32 or delete it.

title: "answers with the path rule before detection" can't tell the path rule from a plain null
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "answers with the path rule before detection" can't tell the path rule from a plain null**

The test uses `/Users/x/Documents/K`, and `syncProviderOfPath` returns null for that path. So the `toBeNull()` before `refresh` would also pass if `SyncStates.of` always returned null for an entry it hasn't detected yet. The path-rule fallback at `sync-state.ts:27` isn't actually exercised. The same holds for the relocation test at line 13: its new path, `/Volumes/T7/K`, is also null by the path rule. Using a `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…` path, with `home` matching it, before detection would pin the fallback.

title: A rejected cloudState() leaves the section on "Loading…" forever
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A rejected cloudState() leaves the section on "Loading…" forever**

`load` awaits `window.electronAPI.workspaces.cloudState()` with no catch, and both callers discard the promise with `void load()` (lines 33 and 35). If the IPC call rejects, the error goes unhandled, `state` stays `null`, and the section shows the `aria-busy` "Loading…" placeholder for as long as the page is open.

This does happen. `library-ipc.maintenance.test.ts:67` lists `IPC_CHANNELS.workspacesCloudState` among the channels that maintenance mode refuses, so the handler in `main/library/index.ts:187` throws there. It also throws if `cache.read` fails.

Fix: catch the error in `load` and store an error state, then render a short message such as `t("failed")`, which `assign` already uses. A later `onLibraryChanged` or epoch change can then retry.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Out-of-order cloudState responses can show the previous workspace
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Out-of-order cloudState responses can show the previous workspace**

`load` runs on every `workspaces?.epoch` change and on every `onLibraryChanged` broadcast. Whichever response arrives last wins, even if it is the older request. Suppose the user switches workspace while a request is still pending. If the old request resolves after the new one, the section shows the previous workspace's location, filter and unassigned list under the new workspace's name. That name comes from `workspaces.active`, so the mismatch would not be obvious.

One fix: keep a request counter in a ref, or a `cancelled` flag in the effect cleanup, and drop responses from older requests. Another: ignore a response whose `workspaceId` differs from `workspaces?.active?.id`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Scratch parts swept on a launch where detection missed are placed with link(), possibly into a synced folder
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Scratch parts swept on a launch where detection missed are placed with link(), possibly into a synced folder**

The sweep now reads the scratch folder whatever detection says (line 765), and the comment in `stranded-recordings.ts:26-28` names the case it is for: a launch where detection did not answer. But `placeByRename` still comes from `syncedStagingFor(vaultDir) !== null`. On that same launch it is false, so `placeTake` (`recording-writer.ts:113`) uses `placeNew`, which hard-links the scratch part into the workspace folder. A Google Drive folder outside `~/Library/CloudStorage` is recognised only by its xattr, and the path rule in `SyncStates.of` (`sync-state.ts:29`) misses it. If that xattr probe times out, the newly swept scratch take is linked into Drive, which is the hazard decision 15 and NIW2-577 forbid. A part in the scratch folder only exists because the workspace was synced when it was recorded, so you could always place parts from `extraStagingDirs` by rename. `placeByRename` already copies on EXDEV (`safe-place.ts:320-321`), so this is also safe for a vault on another volume.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: A failed read after a workspace switch keeps showing the previous workspace's state
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A failed read after a workspace switch keeps showing the previous workspace's state**

`loadFailed` only renders while `state` is null (line 80). After a switch, `workspaces.epoch` changes and `load` runs again. If that read fails (for example, maintenance refuses `workspacesCloudState`), `setLoadFailed(true)` has no visible effect. The section keeps the previous workspace's location, filter and unassigned list under the new workspace's name (`active` comes from `workspaces.active`, line 51), which is the mismatch the request counter was added to prevent. You could clear `state` on failure (`setState(null)` next to `setLoadFailed(true)`), or clear it when the epoch changes.

title: Bound the total eviction probe for a Library listing.
body:
** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Heavy lift** **Bound the total eviction probe for a Library listing.** If a synced provider stalls, `list()` waits for every batch before it can return any items. The probe processes 200 paths per batch in sequence, and each stat call can take five seconds. A workspace with 1,000 media files supplies about 2,000 paths, so stat timeouts alone can delay the Library by 50 seconds. Add a deadline for the whole listing probe and surface a timeout instead of waiting for every batch. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/443a9b0472cffe23d503c34e1cbbfba2d80a243b/apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/dataless.ts))

title: Do not reuse a cached “local” result to authorize a read.
body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Do not reuse a cached “local” result to authorize a read.** If the provider offloads a file within two seconds of a local probe, `EvictionCache` returns the cached `false`. The handler then opens that file, which can start the download this check is intended to prevent. Cache evicted results if useful, but recheck a cached local result before opening a stream. title: The deadline is checked only between batches, so a probe can run past 10 s
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The deadline is checked only between batches, so a probe can run past 10 s**

`now() >= deadline` is checked only before a batch starts (line 79). A batch that starts at 9.9 s can still take `STAT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s, line 19). If `stat` is killed by that timeout and prints nothing, the `lstat` fallback (lines 94-97) then runs over up to 200 paths with no time limit, and that is exactly the stalled-provider case. So the real bound is about deadline + 5 s, plus whatever the fallback takes.

Two places promise a hard bound: line 59 ("The longest a whole probe may take") and the spec (`2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md:1328-1329`, "bounded at 10 s for the whole listing"). Either reword both to say the deadline is checked per batch (worst case about 15 s), or check `now()` inside the fallback loop and treat the paths left over as evicted.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: `now = 5_000` comes after the last call, so the TTL expiry is never tested
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: `now = 5_000` comes after the last call, so the TTL expiry is never tested**

The test name says an evicted answer is remembered "for the window", and it does check that the answer is reused inside the window. But `now = 5_000` runs after the last `isEvicted` call, so the clock change does nothing. Nothing checks that an evicted answer older than `ttlMs` gets probed again (`dataless.ts:127`). Move the clock change before another `isEvicted("/x")` call, without calling `forget()` first, and expect the probe count to go up. As written, the line looks like a check but tests nothing.
