title: Change folder… never re-reads the workspace's folder settings file
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Change folder… never re-reads the workspace's folder settings file (confidence medium)**

`WorkspaceSettings` caches each workspace's folder read by id (`reads`, `workspace-settings.ts:103-106`). That cache is refreshed by `refresh(id)` (`workspace-settings.ts:145-162`). Both sibling paths that point a workspace at a folder call it: `addWorkspace` does (line 597, "An adopted folder may bring its own settings file: read it now"), and `runSwitch` does inside `persistActive` before the commit (line 547).

`relocateFolder` never calls `workspaceSettings.refresh`. After a relocate, the cache still holds the read from the old path. The usual reason for a relocate is that the old folder went missing, so that read is typically `unreadable`, and the folder's overrides stay inactive. For the active workspace, `afterCommit` even runs `notifyOverridesChanged()` (line 526) with those stale overrides. Nothing corrects this until the next capture start (`refreshActiveWorkspaceSettings`, line 167) or a switch. Until then the Settings scope view and the effective settings silently ignore the relocated folder's `settings` file, or don't show it as pending.

Suggested fix: refresh the settings before the commit, the same way `persistActive` does. For example, wrap the registry's `relocate` in `deps` so that a successful relocate runs `await workspaceSettings?.refresh(id)` (and the sync detection, see the other finding) before `relocateActive` calls `afterCommit`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Active relocate commits and re-lists the Library before the new folder's sync provider is detected
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Active relocate commits and re-lists the Library before the new folder's sync provider is detected (confidence medium)**

For the active workspace, `relocateActive` calls `afterCommit` inside `relocateWorkspace` (`switch-transaction.ts:135-136`). That fires `host?.broadcastLibraryChanged()` (line 529) and `broadcastState()`. `syncStates.refresh(current)` only runs afterwards, at line 755.

Until that refresh, `SyncStates.of` sees a changed path and falls back to the path rule alone (`sync-state.ts:26-30`). A Google Drive folder that is recognised only by its xattr therefore reads as not synced. In that window:
- The re-list builds `LibraryVault` with no eviction probe (`activeEvictionProbe()`, line 368, used at `library/index.ts:74`). Evicted items come back as local, with no "In the cloud" state. The renderer keeps that list until the next `library:changed`.
- `syncedStagingFor` (line 393) returns null, so a take started then stages in `.kaipu/tmp/` inside the synced folder.

`runSwitch` avoids this ordering by doing its reads in `persistActive`, before the commit. Here, run the detection (and the settings refresh) inside the `apply` step, after `registry.relocate` succeeds and before `afterCommit`. For a non-active workspace the current order is harmless.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Dragging to select a file name now toggles the row
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Dragging to select a file name now toggles the row (confidence medium)**

The row's `onClick` fires for any click whose target isn't the input. That includes the click Chromium sends after a drag-select when mousedown and mouseup both land inside the `<li>`. Someone who drags over `.rowNow` or `.rowAfter` to copy a long file name will untick (or re-tick) that row as a side effect. The change does show on screen (dimmed row, strikethrough, a different summary count and button label), but it's easy to miss after a copy. One fix is to skip the toggle when `window.getSelection()?.toString()` is non-empty. Another is to add `user-select: none` to `.rowSelectable`, if copying names isn't something users need.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Double-clicking a name to copy it still toggles the row once
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Double-clicking a name to copy it still toggles the row once (confidence medium)**

The guard reads the selection when `click` fires. That covers a drag-select. A double-click on a word is the other common way to grab part of a file name, and it sends two clicks. On the first click nothing is selected yet, so the row toggles. The word is selected on the second mousedown, so only the second click is skipped. The row ends up toggled once, which the new comment says should not happen. A triple-click behaves the same way. One option is to leave the row alone on `event.detail > 1` and also undo the first toggle in `onDoubleClick`. Another is to accept this, since the dimmed row shows the change. The test at reconcile.test.tsx:369-373 mocks a selection that already exists, so it doesn't cover this sequence.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: Prevent the workspace switcher bar from shrinking.
Constrain long volume labels before the hint shrinks.
Clicks now pass through the hint, but the card still hides the Rename pencil
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Clicks now pass through the hint, but the card still hides the Rename pencil (confidence medium)**

With `pointer-events: none`, a click on the card's text now reaches the Rename pencil under it, so the E2E passes: Playwright clicks the button's center and the hit-test skips the card. For a person, though, the card is still painted on top of the pencil. It sits at `z-index: 40` (line 123) with an opaque `background: var(--bg-modal)` (line 132), and that token is `#131315` / `#ffffff` in `packages/tokens/css/tokens.css:13,64`. Where the two overlap, the user can't see the pencil, and clicking on the hint's text would start a rename they couldn't see coming.

The PR's own test step 3 ("click the pencil … even where the card overlaps it") assumes the user knows the pencil is there. If the goal is that the hint never gets in the way of the page, you could place the hint so it doesn't overlap the page header (for example, anchor it to the right of the switcher instead of under it). Another option is to keep `pointer-events: none` and also make the card fade out on hover. This is a design call, not a regression: before this PR the overlapped area couldn't be clicked at all.

title: Add the common hover presentation to the tall example.

The live card's copy pill stays "Copied · ⌘V" on hover; decision 6 says it reads "Copied ✓"

The PR's test steps ask the owner to hover this card. Adding a hover-only label would let the mockup show the rest-to-hover change the spec now describes.

title: Timer bar relies on a `shownAt` field the payload doesn't have, and the spec never adds it
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Timer bar relies on a `shownAt` field the payload doesn't have, and the spec never adds it (confidence high)**

The spec says the bar is "driven by CSS from the payload's `shownAt`". `CaptureToastPayload` has no such field (`apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/types/screenshot-capture.ts:234-247`). The "The window" section, which lists what changes in main, doesn't add it either.

The timestamp is also hard to pin down. Main starts the timer when the renderer reports ready, not when `show` runs (`capture-toast-window.ts:119-125`, `:159-160`). A re-target or a pointer leaving the card restarts the full timeout (`:170-175`). So a `shownAt` taken in `show` would drift from the real timer.

Suggested fix: either add the field to the window changes, saying when main stamps it (on ready, on resume), or drive the bar only from the payload's arrival plus the hover state. The thumbnail change also needs listing: the 160 px limit is set in `screenshot-ipc.ts:131` and the payload doc comment says "at most 160 px wide", but the spec doesn't name either spot.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

title: The "Copied · ⌘V" pill is macOS-only, but the card ships on Windows too
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The "Copied · ⌘V" pill is macOS-only, but the card ships on Windows too (confidence medium)**

The summary, the acceptance criteria (line 84) and the mockup all show the resting pill as **Copied · ⌘V**. Line 87 also asks the card to reveal files in Explorer on Windows, so the card is meant for Windows as well. The spec doesn't say the shortcut hint changes per platform (Ctrl+V on Windows), or that the i18n key takes the shortcut as a parameter.

The pill labels also differ between sections: decision 6 uses "Copied ✓", the summary "Copied · ⌘V", and the mockup's failed-vault card plain "Copied". Pinning down one label per state (at rest, after pressing Copy) would make the `capture-toast.test.tsx` assertions clear.

title: Make the live hover state available to keyboard users.
body:

title: Preserve the tall capture’s aspect ratio.
body:

title: "The timer channel above" points to text that comes below, inside the actions list
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: "The timer channel above" points to text that comes below, inside the actions list (confidence high)**

The `screenshot:toast-timer` channel is first described at lines 133-136, in "The card (renderer)", which comes after this line. So "above" points the reader the wrong way. The bullet also sits in the list under "**Two new actions.**" (`CAPTURE_TOAST_ACTIONS`), but a main→card message is not an action. The section opens with "gains two things" (line 113) and now lists a third. Suggested fix: give the channel its own top-level bullet in "The window" (shape `{ remainingMs: number | null }`, when main sends it, and the `desktop/ipc-contract.mdx` row), and have the renderer section refer back to it.

title: The list of timer events misses Edit waiting on a Save, so the bar would keep draining while the card stays
body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The list of timer events misses Edit waiting on a Save, so the bar would keep draining while the card stays (confidence high)**

The bar only mirrors main's timer. The spec lists when main sends `screenshot:toast-timer` as "renderer ready, re-target, pointer in, pointer out". Main also stops the timer in a fifth case: when Edit (today Annotate) is pressed while that shot's Save is still writing (`capture-toast-window.ts:211-216`). After that, `resume` returns early while that wait is pending (`:172`), so a pointer out does not restart the timer. If the timer is built from this list, no `null` is sent in that case. The bar would then drain to zero and the card would stay on screen. Suggested fix: say that every `stopTimer`/`restartTimer` in main sends the message, or add "Edit waiting on a Save" to the list.

<!-- wachi:finding -->
